issues.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet So AI Agents Can Shop for You
issues.gist: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its AI agents buy things for users. Each purchase needs the user's approval with Face ID or a fingerprint.
issues.gistKo: 오픈AI가 AI 도우미가 대신 물건을 살 수 있는 챗GPT 월렛을 내놓았어요. 결제 때마다 얼굴 인식이나 지문으로 사용자가 승인해야 해요.
issues.easyKo: 이제 챗GPT의 AI 도우미가 내 카드로 쇼핑을 도와줄 수 있어요. 진짜 카드 번호는 가게에 넘어가지 않고, 결제는 내가 직접 승인해요. 지금은 미국 프로 구독자만 써요.

paragraphs.en: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, a feature that lets its AI agents, called Dots, buy things for users. It began rolling out on Friday, November 13, for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States. Users must be at least 18 years old and need a US billing address and an eligible card issued in the US. The launch is limited at first, so OpenAI can test the feature and improve it before a wider rollout.
paragraphs.ko: 오픈AI가 ‘닷츠’라는 AI 도우미가 사용자 대신 물건을 살 수 있게 하는 챗GPT 월렛을 내놓았어요. 11월 13일 금요일부터 미국의 챗GPT 프로 구독자에게 차례로 제공되기 시작했어요. 사용자는 만 18세 이상이어야 하고, 미국 청구지 주소와 미국에서 발급된 사용 가능한 카드가 필요해요. 처음에는 제공 범위가 제한돼서, 오픈AI가 더 넓게 내놓기 전에 기능을 시험하고 고칠 수 있어요.

sents.en: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, a feature that lets its AI agents, called Dots, buy things for users.
sents.ko: 오픈AI가 ‘닷츠’라는 AI 도우미가 사용자 대신 물건을 살 수 있게 하는 챗GPT 월렛을 내놓았어요.

paragraphs.en: Users add a card to the wallet just once, and then they ask a Dot to help with a purchase. Before every checkout, the system shows the items, the total price, and the card that will be used. The user must then approve the payment with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. OpenAI says neither the agent nor the store ever sees the real card number. Instead, payment partners such as American Express, Mastercard, and Visa create a payment token that stands in for the card. Card rewards and the usual bank protections for eligible disputes still apply, according to OpenAI.
paragraphs.ko: 사용자는 지갑에 카드를 한 번만 등록하고, 그다음 닷에게 구매를 도와 달라고 요청해요. 결제 때마다 시스템이 상품, 총액, 사용할 카드를 먼저 보여 줘요. 그러면 사용자가 얼굴 인식이나 지문 같은 보안 확인으로 결제를 승인해야 해요. 오픈AI는 AI 도우미도 가게도 진짜 카드 번호를 보지 못한다고 말해요. 대신 아메리칸 익스프레스, 마스터카드, 비자 같은 결제 협력사가 카드를 대신하는 결제 토큰을 만들어요. 오픈AI에 따르면 카드 혜택과 대상이 되는 분쟁에 대한 은행의 보호는 그대로 적용돼요.

Rivals are already ahead, because Anthropic's Claude Duet, Meta's Muse, and xAI's Grok Bot already have built-in payments. paragraphs.en: The wallet may not work everywhere, because some retailers restrict AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agents, and TechCrunch says Amazon is the largest retailer to ban AI agents. Many websites and payment systems also treat agents as bots and reject their purchases for security reasons. To help, OpenAI published a Commerce Partner Playbook that explains how stores can adjust their firewalls and share product data. pro.en: OpenAI on Friday began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet, a payments feature that allows its AI agents, known as Dots, to complete purchases on behalf of users. The initial release is restricted to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and over who hold a US billing address and an eligible US-issued card, a limited launch the company says will let it test and refine the product before any broader deployment.

Once a card has been registered, a user can instruct a Dot to handle a purchase, and the system displays the items, the total and the chosen card ahead of every checkout. Payment must then be authorised through biometric verification such as Face ID or a fingerprint. Neither the agent nor the merchant sees the actual card number, because networks including American Express, Mastercard and Visa issue a token in its place, and OpenAI says card rewards and standard bank protections for eligible disputes remain in force.

The company is making a second attempt at agentic commerce after discarding Instant Checkout, its earlier tool for buying directly within a chat, which The Decoder says proved too inflexible. Competitors have moved first: Anthropic's Claude Duet, Meta's Muse and xAI's Grok Bot already offer built-in payments. TechCrunch observes that Muse has surpassed 10 million users and that AI-assisted shopping has become one of its leading activities, even as DoorDash and Uber have so far reported modest order volumes from agents.

Whether the wallet works widely will depend on retailers, since some restrict agents or bar them outright. Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agents earlier this year and, according to TechCrunch, is the largest retailer to prohibit them. Many sites and payment systems also flag agents as bots and decline their transactions on security grounds, which is why OpenAI released a Commerce Partner Playbook advising merchants on adjusting firewalls and sharing product data, and naming providers such as Stripe, Adyen and Riskified.

OpenAI expects that users will eventually be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agents by setting parameters such as spending limits, product categories or time periods and pre-approving the transactions. The feature is confined to the United States at launch, and the company intends to widen its retailer support; the key question now is how many merchants will admit agents rather than turn them away.

views.view: OpenAI is catching up with rivals whose agents can already shop, after dropping its first approach.
AI shopping is still finding its fit, and retailers that ban agents, such as Amazon, could limit the wallet.
The wallet hides real card details, but some stores block agents, so it may not work everywhere.

issues.title: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros over Facebook's access to Android photos
issues.gist: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta 805 million euros. It says the Facebook app for Android reached users' photos and videos without specific consent.
issues.gistKo: 이탈리아 개인정보 보호 당국이 메타에 8억 500만 유로의 벌금을 물렸어요. 페이스북 안드로이드 앱이 구체적인 동의 없이 이용자의 사진과 영상에 접근했다는 이유예요.
issues.easyKo: 이탈리아 당국이 페이스북 앱이 폰 갤러리 사진을 추천하려고 접근하면서 동의를 제대로 받지 않았다고 보고 큰 벌금을 냈어요. 메타는 동의하지 않고 항소하겠다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta 805 million euros on Saturday, which is about 887 million dollars. The regulator said the Facebook app for Android phones reached users' photos and videos without specific consent. It also said Meta did not properly tell about 20 million smartphone users that this access existed.
paragraphs.ko: 이탈리아 개인정보 보호 당국은 토요일에 메타에 8억 500만 유로, 약 8억 8,700만 달러의 벌금을 물렸어요. 당국은 안드로이드 폰용 페이스북 앱이 구체적인 동의 없이 이용자의 사진과 영상에 접근했다고 밝혔어요. 또 메타가 약 2천만 명의 스마트폰 이용자에게 이런 접근이 있다는 사실을 제대로 알리지 않았다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: The case is about a feature that suggests photos and videos from a phone gallery as ideas for new posts. Facebook asked for gallery access through one permission for the whole app. The regulator said an earlier notice did not make clear that this permission also let Facebook create suggestions from gallery photos. Meta now has 60 days to turn the feature off by default and ask users for separate consent.

pro.en: Italy's data protection authority on Saturday imposed a fine of 805 million euros, roughly 887 million dollars, on Meta, finding that the Facebook application for Android devices had reached users' photographs and videos without obtaining specific consent. The watchdog added that the company had failed to inform about 20 million smartphone users properly that such access existed.

At the heart of the case lies a feature that proposes images and clips from a handset's gallery as material for new posts. Facebook sought gallery access through a single, app-wide authorisation, and the regulator held that an accompanying notice did not make plain that this would also permit suggestions drawn from stored photographs. Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and to seek users' consent separately.

The authority weighed the large number of people affected and noted that the infringement is still continuing for those who have not updated the app, as well as for those who had already consented to the arrangement. It also cited Meta's lack of cooperation, having opened its inquiry in July 2025. DW reported that the penalty equals 0.4% of Meta's annual turnover, while CBS described it as among the biggest Italy has ever levied on a technology giant.

Meta said it strongly disagrees with the regulator's assessment of the facts, its application of the law and what it termed the disproportionate size of the fine, portraying the tool as a straightforward aid to posting that works only once users grant permission on their device. It told the BBC it intends to appeal. DW added that the company had argued that the case falls under Irish legal jurisdiction, a claim the Italian regulator rejected.

Meta has separately denied using the camera roll feature to train artificial intelligence models, although Italy's regulator did not examine that question. The penalty follows an order by a US judge in New Mexico that Meta pay 25 billion dollars over how it characterised its handling of data. For Korean students, the episode underscores the value of scrutinising app permissions, and attention now turns to Meta's appeal and to whether it meets the 60-day deadline.

views.view: It reports the fine and the regulator's reasons, and also gives Meta's strong disagreement and plan to appeal.
It places the fine among Italy's largest on a tech giant and recalls the earlier Amazon fine that was later cut.
It notes the fine is 0.4% of turnover and that Italy rejected Meta's claim that Irish law should apply.

issues.title: Microsoft Says Services Fully Restored After Global Outage Hit Governments and Businesses
issues.gist: Microsoft says all services are back after an outage that began on Thursday and hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot in more than 70 countries. The company says it was not a cyberattack and promises a full report.
issues.gistKo: 마이크로소프트는 목요일에 시작된 장애로 아웃룩, 팀즈, 코파일럿이 70개국 넘게 멈췄다가 모두 복구됐다고 밝혔어요. 사이버 공격은 아니었고, 전체 보고서를 내겠다고 했어요.
issues.easyKo: 마이크로소프트의 업무용 서비스가 하루 넘게 세계 곳곳에서 멈췄다가 토요일에 돌아왔어요. 회사는 네트워크 용량을 늘리는 작업에서 문제가 생겼다고 설명했어요. 한국 정부도 국내 피해를 점검해요.

paragraphs.en: Microsoft said on Saturday that all its services are fully restored after a huge global outage. The problem hit Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot. It began on Thursday and reached people in more than 70 countries. About 430 million people use these Microsoft 365 apps. Microsoft apologized and said it was deeply sorry for the trouble.
paragraphs.ko: 마이크로소프트는 토요일에 큰 규모의 세계적 장애를 겪은 뒤 모든 서비스가 완전히 복구되었다고 밝혔어요. 문제는 아웃룩, 팀즈, 그리고 AI 비서 코파일럿에 영향을 줬어요. 장애는 목요일에 시작되어 70개가 넘는 나라의 사람들에게 닿았어요. 이 마이크로소프트 365 앱을 쓰는 사람은 약 4억 3천만 명이에요. 마이크로소프트는 사과하며 불편을 끼쳐 깊이 죄송하다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: Microsoft said the failure was not a cyberattack and was not caused by an AI agent. It said the problem came from an earlier network capacity upgrade and showed up after a recent network change. The company first reported that users in the Americas could not open their mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday. Recovery was slow, and Microsoft said it restored services step by step to keep them stable. A full report will come after the company finishes its review.

pro.en: Microsoft announced on Saturday that it had fully restored its services after a sweeping global outage that knocked out Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI assistant. The disruption began on Thursday, spread to people in more than 70 countries, and some 430 million people use the affected Microsoft 365 apps; the company issued a public apology for the trouble.

The company said the breakdown was neither a cyberattack nor the work of an AI agent, tracing it instead to an earlier network capacity upgrade whose flaw surfaced after a recent network change. Microsoft first acknowledged at 17:54 GMT on Thursday that users in the Americas could not open Exchange Online mailboxes, and it brought services back gradually to ensure stability; a full post-incident report is promised once its review is complete.

The fallout struck governments, courts, hospitals, airlines and banks alike. British hospital staff fell back on paper records and a union reported a serious effect on ambulance services; Japanese government email went dark, forcing officials to text; House of Representatives staff in the US said they lost a full day of work; officials at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey could not open Outlook; and a South African winemaker said his operation had ground to a halt.

Specialists described the episode as a stark reminder of the world's reliance on a handful of large technology providers. Steven Murdoch of University College London said outages of this scale typically stem from unexpected interactions among complex systems, while Tim Clement-Jones, a former chair of a House of Lords AI committee, argued it exposed Britain's overdependence on American technology. Another expert noted that the standard advice to adopt a backup service is almost unworkable in practice.

In Seoul, the Ministry of Science and ICT said it would examine disruptions at domestic companies, some of which struggled to reach their email on Friday, and would assess possible damage together with Microsoft Korea. Attention now turns to Microsoft's full account of what went wrong.

pro.en: Former Australia batter David Warner has accused Cricket Australia of a cover-up as the furor over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, widely known as Sandpapergate, continues to escalate.

Warner, then-captain Steve Smith and opener Cameron Bancroft each served lengthy suspensions after the Test series in South Africa in 2018. The controversy was revived last week when batter Usman Khawaja asserted in his new autobiography that the entire Australia team knew sandpaper was being used to alter the ball.

Warner contended that, to his knowledge, Cricket Australia never interviewed Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in its 2018 inquiry, adding that the governing body appeared to have settled on its scapegoats from the outset. Khawaja likewise disclosed that investigators never questioned him, despite his sitting beside Bancroft in the dressing room.

Test captain Pat Cummins used a news conference on Friday to say he had been interviewed and to dismiss the notion of team-wide knowledge as "utter nonsense". Warner countered that he stands by Khawaja and regards the inquiry as botched.

Cricket Australia responded that every player had been afforded the opportunity to speak in 2018 and could have submitted fresh evidence in the eight years since, and it confirmed it will not reopen the investigation.

pro.en: King Charles joined Sir Elton John, 79, on the singer's regular Rocket Hour radio show for a special episode timed to coincide with the monarch's 78th birthday. The pair selected 14 tracks and traded musical recollections; the programme was recorded last month at Apple Music Studios in south London and first aired on Saturday morning.

The broadcast also marked the 50th anniversary of the King's Trust, the charity, and the King singled out I'm Still Standing as a favourite for its message of resilience. He quipped that both he and the Trust were definitely still standing, prompting Sir Elton to laugh and answer that he was still sitting, while the King chuckled that bits dropped off here and there with advancing age.

The King recalled Sir Elton's 1986 appearance at Wembley Arena, which celebrated the charity's 10th anniversary, saying that no one present could possibly forget the performance. He also chose Giant by Calvin Harris and Rag'n'Bone Man, arguing that its message of drawing strength from others encapsulated the charity, and The Beatles' All You Need Is Love, which he remembered Sir Paul McCartney performing in 2002 at a concert honouring the Golden Jubilee of his late mother, Queen Elizabeth II.

The show opened with Tina Turner's Proud Mary, and the King described the late singer as an electrifying character. He said the guard at Buckingham Palace had played her hit Simply the Best after her death in 2023, a modest gesture of thanks for the times she performed for his charities, and the playlist also featured Elvis Presley's Hound Dog and Raye's Joy.

The programme will be rebroadcast on Apple Music One on Saturday and Sunday and will also air on Apple Music Hits on Sunday. The episode demonstrates how music can bolster charitable work and carry a personal narrative, and it offers a notable example of the King using humour to address the subject of ageing.

issues.title: Zelensky Says the US Floated Ukraine Leaving Donbas in Return for NATO Membership
issues.gist: Ukraine's president says US negotiators asked if Ukraine would leave the Donbas region in exchange for joining NATO. He says Ukraine will not give up land easily and that Ukrainians must decide.
issues.gistKo: 우크라이나 대통령은 미국 협상단이 나토 가입을 대가로 돈바스에서 철수할 수 있느냐고 물었다고 말했어요. 그는 영토를 쉽게 내줄 수 없고 우크라이나 국민이 결정해야 한다고 했어요.
issues.easyKo: 젤렌스키 대통령은 미국 협상단이 처음으로 「나토에 가입하면 돈바스에서 철수하겠느냐」고 물었다고 밝혔어요. 그는 안전 보장, 강한 군대, 재건 자금이 모두 갖춰져야 하고, 그러면 국민투표에 부치겠다고 했어요. 러시아의 입장은 아직 크게 달라지지 않았어요.

paragraphs.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States has floated a new idea for ending the war. He said US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would pull out of the Donbas region if it could join NATO. Zelensky said this was the first time anyone had raised that question. He made the remarks on Friday, and his office released them on Saturday. The comments came after a round of peace talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the US in Abu Dhabi this week.

pro.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said US negotiators had floated the prospect of Ukraine withdrawing from the Donbas region in return for NATO membership, an idea he said had never been raised before. His comments, made on Friday and released by his office on Saturday, followed a round of Ukraine-Russia-US peace talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week.

Donbas comprises the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, most of which Russia controls as part of its occupation of roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, and although Ukraine has long sought NATO membership that Washington and others have previously opposed and Moscow calls unacceptable, Zelensky has consistently ruled out surrendering sovereign land.

Zelensky said Kyiv is discussing a comprehensive security package with partners, comprising NATO and EU guarantees, a strong, well-funded army and reconstruction money, and that he would put such an offer to a referendum if the US confirmed it. Any arrangement, he stressed, would not recognize occupied territory as Russian; he sought Article 5-style assurances at a minimum, was told no American troops would be deployed, and said specifics remain lacking because everything is under discussion.

Zelensky described the idea as back on the agenda within an extremely difficult conversation on European security, and the BBC reports that Moscow's position appears unchanged, with proposals for limits on Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and guaranteed neutrality that Kyiv has rejected. Zelensky warned that Moscow's bid to redraw Europe's security architecture could lead to further wars.

The negotiations came after fraught weeks in US-Ukraine relations, in which Trump had asked Kyiv to pause strikes on Russian oil facilities and later said it was time for Ukraine to get a new president. Elections are suspended under martial law, though Zelensky has said he would hold them within months of a peace deal, and envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Putin in Moscow before seeing Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday.

views.view: Russia's position has not shifted, and it still asks for limits on Ukraine's army, land concessions and neutrality, which Ukraine rejects.
Zelensky warns that the Kremlin's bid to change Europe's security structure could lead to more wars.

issues.title: Meetmebythesea Wins the Paddy Power Gold Cup for JP McManus
issues.gist: Meetmebythesea won the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham, giving owner JP McManus his first win in the race. At Windsor, Paul Nicholls equalled the British record of 3,930 jumps winners.
issues.gistKo: 미트미바이더시가 첼트넘 패디파워 골드컵에서 우승해 말 주인 JP 맥마누스에게 이 경주 첫 우승을 안겼어요. 윈저에서는 폴 니컬스가 영국 장애물 경주 최다 승리 기록(3,930승)과 같아졌어요.
issues.easyKo: 영국의 유명한 말 경주 패디파워 골드컵에서 인기 1위였던 미트미바이더시가 이겼어요. 말 주인 맥마누스는 이 경주에서 처음 우승했어요. 같은 날 조련사 폴 니컬스는 영국 최다승 기록과 같아졌어요.

paragraphs.en: Meetmebythesea won the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham in England on Saturday. Jockey Harry Cobden rode the six-year-old horse for owner JP McManus, who had never won this race before. The 2-1 favourite was level with Blueking D'Oroux at the last fence, then pulled away to win by two-and-a-half lengths. Torneo, a 12-1 chance, finished third, almost three lengths further back.
paragraphs.ko: 미트미바이더시가 토요일 영국 첼트넘에서 열린 패디파워 골드컵에서 우승했어요. 기수 해리 코브던이 여섯 살 말을 타고 우승했고, 말 주인 JP 맥마누스는 이 경주에서 처음 우승했어요. 2대 1 인기 말은 마지막 장애물에서 블루킹 도루와 나란히 달리다가 앞서 나가 2.5마신 차로 이겼어요. 12대 1 배당의 토르네오는 거의 3마신 더 뒤에서 3위로 들어왔어요.

The Guardian said the ground had been drying out, and more than 32,000 racegoers watched. Cobden, who is 28, said big days like this do not come along often and that he planned to enjoy each one. He became McManus's retained jockey in Britain and Ireland in May, and this was his first big-race win since then.

pro.en: Meetmebythesea, the 2-1 favourite, landed the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham on Saturday under Harry Cobden, giving owner JP McManus a first success in the feature handicap chase. The six-year-old was upsides Dan Skelton's Blueking D'Oroux at the final fence before pulling clear to score by two-and-a-half lengths, with the 12-1 shot Torneo almost three lengths further adrift in third.

The contest was run in a diminished field of 10 after five non-runners, among them the heavily backed July Flower, and the Guardian reported that the ground had been drying. A crowd of more than 32,000 was on hand. Cobden, 28, said such occasions seldom come around and that he intended to savour each one; it was his first big-race win since becoming McManus's retained rider in Britain and Ireland in May.

Trainer Ben Pauling praised the winner's fluent jumping and the resolve he showed to prevail. He said the race had inspired him as a youngster, that he has attended the meeting since the age of 14, and he noted that he had won it a year earlier with The Jukebox Man, to whom he likened Meetmebythesea in class.

The result was the gelding's second major success at Cheltenham, following a novice win at the Festival in March. Pauling declined to say whether he might develop into a Gold Cup contender at next March's meeting, though the Guardian suggested he could step into Grade One company at the King George VI Chase at Kempton on Boxing Day, for which bookmakers quote him at about 12-1.

Elsewhere, at Windsor, Fasol's victory in a handicap hurdle lifted Paul Nicholls to 3,930 jumps winners in Britain, drawing him level with Martin Pipe's all-time record. Nicholls has a single runner on Sunday, Pourquoi Pas Papa in the 1.25 at Cheltenham, as he seeks to take sole possession of the mark.

issues.title: South Korea Lose 3-2 to Saudi Arabia in Their First Defeat to the Saudis in 21 Years
issues.gist: South Korea lost 3-2 to Saudi Arabia in a football friendly in Qatar. It was the first loss to the Saudis since August 2005.
issues.gistKo: 한국 축구 대표팀이 카타르에서 열린 평가전에서 사우디아라비아에 2-3으로 졌어요. 사우디에 지는 것은 2005년 8월 이후 21년 만이에요.
issues.easyKo: 한국 남자 축구 대표팀이 사우디아라비아에 2-3으로 졌어요. 사우디에 진 건 21년 만이에요. 주장 손흥민 선수는 아쉬운 기회를 놓친 것을 동료들에게 사과했어요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea lost 3-2 to Saudi Arabia in a men's football friendly in Qatar on Friday. It was South Korea's first loss to Saudi Arabia in 21 years, since August 2005. The match was played at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Al Rayyan, just west of Doha. South Korea is ranked 32nd in the world, while Saudi Arabia is 55th, and the Koreans had not lost to them in six earlier meetings.
paragraphs.ko: 한국이 금요일 카타르에서 열린 남자 축구 평가전에서 사우디아라비아에 2-3으로 졌어요. 2005년 8월 이후 21년 만에 처음으로 사우디에 진 경기였어요. 경기는 도하 서쪽에 있는 알라이얀의 자심 빈 하마드 경기장에서 열렸어요. 한국은 세계 32위, 사우디는 55위이고, 한국은 앞선 여섯 번의 만남에서 지지 않았어요.

paragraphs.en: Saudi Arabia scored first in stoppage time at the end of the first half, after the Korean goalkeeper slipped while rushing out. Oh Hyeon-gyu equalized less than two minutes after the restart. Then Saudi Arabia scored twice in three minutes, in the 56th and 59th minutes, to lead 3-1. Lee Jae-sung came on as a substitute and made it 3-2 in the 68th minute. South Korea took 15 shots, six of them on target, but could not score again.

pro.en: South Korea suffered a 3-2 defeat to Saudi Arabia in a men's friendly in Qatar on Friday, their first loss to the Middle Eastern side in 21 years, since August 2005. The fixture was staged at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Al Rayyan, just west of Doha, where 32nd-ranked South Korea saw an unbeaten run of six matches against the 55th-ranked Saudis come to an end.

The Saudis struck first in first-half stoppage time after the Korean goalkeeper lost his footing while charging off his line, and Oh Hyeon-gyu levelled within two minutes of the restart. Saudi Arabia then scored twice in the space of three minutes, in the 56th and 59th, to build a 3-1 lead, before the substitute Lee Jae-sung narrowed the gap to 3-2 in the 68th minute. Despite 15 attempts, six of them on target, the Koreans could not find a second equalizer.

Captain Son Heung-min squandered a significant opening in the 66th minute, blazing his shot well over the crossbar, and said he owed his teammates an apology and needed to examine his own performance. He nonetheless argued that the side had shown encouraging signs, including constant communication and a determination to fight back, and lamented that the result would overshadow them.

The match was the first since a rift within the squad became public: after the 2-0 victory over Uzbekistan on Oct. 6, three 30-year-old veterans, Hwang In-beom, Hwang Hee-chan and Kim Min-jae, had threatened to retire from international duty, apparently out of discontent with a leadership group that includes Son. They issued a joint statement on Thursday saying they had set their differences aside, and all those involved except Lee Jae-sung started on Friday.

It was only the fifth game in charge for interim head coach Robert Moreno, a Spaniard, whose record now stands at two wins, one draw and two defeats. South Korea face Qatar in Doha on Tuesday at 5 p.m. local time, or 11 p.m. in Korea, and the three goals conceded were the most they have allowed Saudi Arabia since a 5-4 loss in an Olympic qualifier in April 1984.

views.view: Son said the team did not get the result it deserved, but he saw good signs such as talking more and a strong wish to come back.
It reported the match as South Korea's first loss to Saudi Arabia in 21 years and noted the recent dispute inside the squad.

issues.title: Thousands march in Edinburgh against plans for large AI data centres
issues.gist: Thousands of people marched in Edinburgh to protest against large AI data centres. The Scottish government says it will soon publish new planning guidance.
issues.gistKo: 수천 명이 에든버러에서 대형 AI 데이터센터에 반대하며 행진했어요. 스코틀랜드 정부는 곧 새 계획 지침을 내놓겠다고 해요.
issues.easyKo: 스코틀랜드 사람들이 큰 AI 데이터센터 건설을 걱정하며 거리로 나왔어요. 전기와 환경 문제를 걱정해요. 정부는 새 규칙을 곧 발표한다고 해요.

paragraphs.en: Thousands of people joined a protest in Edinburgh on Saturday against the building of large AI data centres. Demonstrators with placards, some dressed in costume, gathered at the top of the Royal Mile. They then marched towards the Scottish Parliament. The event is part of a wave of protests across Europe.
paragraphs.ko: 토요일 수천 명이 대형 AI 데이터센터 건설에 반대하는 에든버러 시위에 참여했어요. 팻말을 든 시위대 가운데 일부는 분장을 하고 로열 마일 꼭대기에 모였어요. 그런 다음 스코틀랜드 의회를 향해 행진했어요. 이 행사는 유럽 곳곳에서 일어나는 시위의 한 부분이에요.

paragraphs.en: Protesters carried slogans such as "AI data centres threaten humanity" and "AI data centres: costing the Earth." Some came to oppose plans in particular communities, including Cockenzie in East Lothian and Larbert in Falkirk. Kim Cairns, who campaigns against a planned centre at Chapelcross, said her community worries about noise and road closures during construction. She said the site is now green fields with sheep and cows, and the centre would need a huge amount of electricity.
paragraphs.ko: 시위대는 'AI 데이터센터는 인류를 위협한다', 'AI 데이터센터: 지구에 큰 값을 치르게 한다' 같은 구호를 들었어요. 일부는 이스트로디언의 코켄지와 포커크의 라버트 같은 특정 지역의 계획에 반대하려고 왔어요. 채플크로스 계획에 반대하는 킴 케언스는 지역 사회가 공사 중 소음과 도로 폐쇄를 걱정한다고 했어요. 그 부지는 지금 양과 소가 있는 푸른 들판이고, 센터는 막대한 전기를 쓸 거라고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: The size of the plans is a key part of the debate. The biggest data centre in Scotland is thought to be DataVita's site in Airdrie, North Lanarkshire, with a capacity of 12MW. If the planned Chapelcross centre goes ahead, its capacity would be 1,000MW, one of the largest in the world. The Scottish Greens and campaign groups have called for a moratorium on large data centres.

paragraphs.en: Friends of the Earth campaigner Kim Pratt said these projects will bring big profits for big tech companies but huge impacts for people in Scotland. She said people should have the final say, and warned of higher energy bills and climate impact. Innovation Minister Alyn Smith has said data centres are "the whisky bonds of the AI sector." He has also said some of the discussion has been "wild," because you would think there was no planning system at all.
paragraphs.ko: '지구의 벗' 활동가 킴 프랫은 이런 사업이 빅테크 기업에는 큰 이익을, 스코틀랜드 사람들에게는 큰 영향을 줄 거라고 말했어요. 사람들이 최종 결정권을 가져야 한다며 에너지 요금 상승과 기후 영향을 경고했어요. 혁신 담당 장관 앨린 스미스는 데이터센터가 'AI 분야의 위스키 본드'라고 말한 적이 있어요. 그는 계획 제도가 아예 없는 것처럼 말하는 일부 논의가 '터무니없다'고도 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: The Scottish government confirmed it will publish new planning guidance on data centres before the end of the year. pro.en: Thousands of demonstrators converged on Edinburgh on Saturday to protest against the construction of large-scale AI data centres, in an event that forms part of a wider wave of protests across Europe. Placard-bearing marchers, some in costume, assembled at the top of the Royal Mile before processing towards the Scottish Parliament.

Placards bore slogans including "AI data centres threaten humanity" and "AI data centres: costing the Earth," and several attendees had come to oppose specific proposals, among them schemes at Cockenzie in East Lothian and Larbert in Falkirk. Kim Cairns, a campaigner against the planned Chapelcross facility, said residents feared noise and road closures during construction, and noted that the site is currently green fields with sheep and cows, while the centre would require an enormous amount of electricity.

Scale lies at the heart of the dispute. The largest data centre in Scotland is believed to be DataVita's campus in Airdrie, North Lanarkshire, rated at 12MW, whereas the proposed Chapelcross complex would offer 1,000MW, placing it among the biggest in the world. The Scottish Greens and several campaign groups have demanded a moratorium on large facilities.

Kim Pratt of Friends of the Earth argued that the projects would deliver substantial profits to big tech firms while imposing national-level burdens on Scots, including higher energy bills and climate costs, and insisted the public should have the final say. Innovation Minister Alyn Smith, who has likened data centres to "the whisky bonds of the AI sector," has called some of the surrounding discourse "wild," saying it sounds as though no planning system existed.

The Scottish government confirmed that it will issue fresh planning guidance on data centres before the year is out. A spokesperson added that planning authorities must now alert ministers to new applications, and that a new planning direction mandates an Environmental Impact Assessment for every new facility with a power capacity exceeding 50 megawatts.

views.view: It reports the protesters' worries about noise, electricity and climate, and the government's plan for new guidance.

pro.en: North Korea has altered the proportions of its national flag for the first time since the state's founding in 1948, a revision written into the amended constitution. Article 166, published on Friday on Naenara, a North Korean propaganda website, now sets the flag's height-to-width ratio at 1 to 1.65, down from 1 to 2, which narrows its width.

The flag's basic design is intact, with a broad red stripe in the center, narrower white and blue stripes, and a red five-pointed star in a white circle. According to the constitution, the red stripe commemorates the blood of fighters who resisted Japan's colonial rule from 1910 to 1945, the white circle and stripes denote loyalty to the leader and the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, and the blue stripes signify peace, friendship and the country's sovereignty.

Analysts read the revision as part of Kim Jong-un's broader campaign to forge a distinctive national identity. In 2024 the regime rewrote its national anthem, substituting i sesang, meaning this world, for samcholli, the traditional term for the entire peninsula, and earlier this year it struck reunification-related provisions from the constitution, consistent with Kim's contention that the two Koreas are separate, hostile states.

Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University, said the revision seeks to balance continuity with the legacy of previous leaders against the imprint of a Kim Jong-un-era identity, and that it helps institutionalize the two-hostile-states doctrine in the constitution and in national symbols. Reports tie such steps to Pyongyang's increasingly hostile stance toward South Korea.

Because the colors and the star are unchanged, the alteration could easily go unnoticed. The reports do not indicate whether further changes to national symbols are planned, and for now the new ratio stands in Article 166 while the design remains as it was.

views.view: Analysts say the flag change is another step by Kim Jong-un to build a distinct national identity under his two hostile states idea.
Observers say the new ratio may reflect Pyongyang's effort to create a new national image under Kim, the third-generation ruler.

issues.title: South Korea holds a separate Sado mines memorial for a third year as forced labor dispute with Japan continues
issues.gist: South Korea held its own memorial for Korean forced laborers at Japan's Sado mines for the third year in a row. Seoul and Tokyo still disagree on how to describe the forced nature of the labor.
issues.gistKo: 한국이 일본 사도광산의 한국인 강제 노역 피해자를 위한 추도식을 3년 연속 따로 열었어요. 강제성을 어떻게 표현할지를 두고 두 나라의 의견은 아직 달라요.
issues.easyKo: 사도광산에서 일한 한국인들을 기리는 행사를 한국 정부가 올해도 일본과 따로 열었어요. 강제로 일했다는 사실을 일본이 분명히 말하지 않아서 합의가 되지 않았기 때문이에요. 세계유산이 된 지 3년이 지났지만 갈등은 풀리지 않았어요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea held its own memorial ceremony for Korean forced laborers at the Sado mines in Japan on Friday. It was the third year in a row that Seoul skipped an event organized by Japan. The ceremony began at 10 a.m. in Sado, in Niigata Prefecture. South Korean Ambassador to Japan Lee Hyuk, other government officials and nine bereaved family members attended, according to Seoul's Foreign Ministry.
paragraphs.ko: 한국은 금요일 일본 사도광산의 한국인 강제 노역 피해자를 위한 추도식을 따로 열었어요. 서울이 일본이 연 행사에 불참한 것은 3년 연속이에요. 추도식은 니가타현 사도에서 오전 10시에 열렸어요. 한국 외교부에 따르면 이혁 주일 대사와 다른 정부 관계자, 유족 아홉 명이 참석했어요.

sents.en: South Korea held its own memorial ceremony for Korean forced laborers at the Sado mines in Japan on Friday.
sents.ko: 한국은 금요일 일본 사도광산의 한국인 강제 노역 피해자를 위한 추도식을 따로 열었어요.

sents.en: South Korean Ambassador to Japan Lee Hyuk, other government officials and nine bereaved family members attended, according to Seoul's Foreign Ministry.
sents.ko: 한국 외교부에 따르면 이혁 주일 대사와 다른 정부 관계자, 유족 아홉 명이 참석했어요.

paragraphs.en: In his address, Lee spoke about the suffering of Korean workers forcibly mobilized to the mines during Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule. He said they were given especially dangerous and demanding tasks and lived with fear of injury, isolation from the outside world and an uncertain future. Lee said remembering the past would deepen empathy and healing. It would also let people understand the whole history of the Sado mines as a World Heritage site. He also hoped the two countries would remember their shared painful history while moving toward cooperation and solidarity. Choi Jae-sik, who spoke for the bereaved families, hoped his late father could finally rest in peace.
paragraphs.ko: 이 대사는 연설에서 일본이 식민 지배한 1910~45년에 광산으로 강제로 끌려간 한국인 노동자들의 고통을 이야기했어요. 그는 이들이 특히 위험하고 힘든 일을 맡았고, 다칠까 하는 두려움과 바깥세상과의 단절, 불확실한 앞날 속에 살았다고 했어요. 이 대사는 과거를 기억하면 공감과 치유가 깊어진다고 말했어요. 또 세계유산인 사도광산의 전체 역사를 이해할 기회가 된다고도 했어요. 그는 두 나라가 함께 겪은 아픈 역사를 기억하면서 협력과 연대로 나아가길 바란다고도 했어요. 유족 대표 최재식 씨는 세상을 떠난 아버지가 이제 편히 쉬기를 바란다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Two months earlier, on Sept. 12, Japan held its own memorial, organized by a local committee in Sado. Yukiya Hamamoto, a Japanese foreign ministry official in charge of cultural affairs, attended for Tokyo. He said workers from the Korean Peninsula had labored in dangerous and harsh conditions. But his remarks did not clearly say that the labor was forced, which has long been a point of dispute between the two governments. Seoul did not take part in that ceremony because the sides could not agree on how the history should appear in the address.
paragraphs.ko: 두 달 전인 9월 12일 일본은 사도의 지역 위원회가 연 자체 추도식을 열었어요. 일본 외무성 문화 담당 하마모토 유키야 국장이 일본 정부를 대표해 참석했어요. 그는 한반도 출신 노동자들이 위험하고 가혹한 조건에서 일했다고 말했어요. 하지만 그의 발언에는 그 노동이 강제였다는 말이 분명히 없었는데, 이는 두 정부 사이의 오랜 쟁점이에요. 서울은 역사를 연설에 어떻게 담을지 양쪽이 합의하지 못해 그 행사에 참석하지 않았어요.

paragraphs.en: The dispute goes back to July 2024, when the Sado mines were added to UNESCO's World Heritage List with South Korea's consent. About 1,500 Koreans were mobilized to work there under harsh conditions during colonial rule. To win Seoul's support, Tokyo promised to show the full history of the site. It also promised a yearly memorial for all workers, attended by Japanese central government representatives. Disagreements over the ceremony's name and the wording of the remarks appeared before the first event in 2024, so Seoul withdrew and held its own. In 2025 the two sides again failed to agree on wording that clearly admits forced labor. Seoul held a separate ceremony on Nov. 21, with Ambassador Lee and 11 bereaved family members.

pro.en: South Korea held a separate memorial in Sado, Niigata Prefecture, on Friday for Korean forced laborers at the Sado mines, the third consecutive year Seoul has boycotted a ceremony organized by Japan. The 10 a.m. service was attended by Ambassador to Japan Lee Hyuk, other officials and nine bereaved family members, according to the Foreign Ministry.

In his commemorative address, Lee dwelt on the suffering of Koreans forcibly mobilized to the mines during Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule of the peninsula, noting that they were assigned especially perilous and punishing work and endured constant fear of injury, isolation from the outside world and uncertainty about their futures. He said that remembering the past would foster empathy and healing and an opportunity to grasp the full history of the site as a World Heritage property, and he voiced hope that both countries would recall their shared painful history while advancing toward cooperation and solidarity. Choi Jae-sik, speaking for the bereaved families, said he hoped his late father could at last rest in peace.

The ceremony came two months after Japan's own event on Sept. 12, organized by a local committee in Sado and attended by Yukiya Hamamoto, director-general for cultural affairs at Japan's foreign ministry, who acknowledged that workers from the peninsula had toiled in dangerous and harsh conditions. His remarks, however, made no explicit reference to the forced nature of that labor, a longstanding point of contention, and Seoul stayed away after the two sides failed to bridge differences over how the historical circumstances should be reflected in the address.

The dispute dates to July 2024, when the mines were inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List with Seoul's consent, and roughly 1,500 Koreans had been mobilized to work there under harsh conditions during colonial rule. To secure that support, Tokyo pledged to present the site's full history and to hold an annual memorial for all workers attended by central government representatives, but disagreements over the ceremony's name and the wording of remarks surfaced before the inaugural event in 2024, prompting Seoul to withdraw and hold its own, and the same impasse over explicit language on forced labor recurred in 2025, when Seoul's separate service on Nov. 21 drew Ambassador Lee and 11 bereaved relatives.

The Korea Herald observed that the continued division underscores the unresolved historical sensitivities surrounding the UNESCO-listed site despite broader efforts to strengthen bilateral cooperation. Three years after Japan's commitment, Seoul and Tokyo have yet to agree on a joint ceremony that addresses South Korea's concerns about acknowledging forced labor.

views.view: The split shows that history problems around the Sado site are still unresolved after three years.

why: The Sado mines are a World Heritage site, so how their history is told matters to both countries.
The dispute shows that history still affects relations between South Korea and Japan.
lines.agree: Both governments say that Korean workers labored in dangerous and harsh conditions at the mines.
lines.split: Seoul wants clear words that the labor was forced, but Japan's remarks did not say this clearly.
lines.life: South Korea and Japan are close partners for trade and travel, so history disputes can matter to students, too.
lines.next: Watch whether the two governments agree on a joint ceremony next year.

issues.title: Myanmar Airstrike on Displacement Camp Kills 12 in Rakhine State
issues.gist: A Myanmar military airstrike hit a camp for displaced people in Rakhine state and killed 12 people. Rescuers say a five-year-old child was among the dead.
issues.gistKo: 미얀마 군의 공습이 라카인주 피란민 수용소를 덮쳐 12명이 숨졌어요. 구조대는 다섯 살 아이도 숨졌다고 말해요.
issues.easyKo: 내전 중인 미얀마에서 군 전투기가 피란민들이 사는 캠프를 공격했어요. 12명이 숨지고 18명이 다쳤다고 구조대가 밝혔어요.

paragraphs.en: A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp for displaced people killed 12 people in Rakhine state, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday. The attack happened on Friday evening at the Byar La camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of the state capital Sittwe.
paragraphs.ko: 미얀마 군의 공습이 라카인주의 피란민 수용소에서 12명의 목숨을 앗아갔다고 목격자와 구조대원이 토요일에 말했어요. 공격은 금요일 저녁 주도 시트웨 북동쪽 폰나균 군구의 바야라 수용소에서 일어났어요.

sents.en: A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp for displaced people killed 12 people in Rakhine state, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday.
sents.ko: 미얀마 군의 공습이 라카인주의 피란민 수용소에서 12명의 목숨을 앗아갔다고 목격자와 구조대원이 토요일에 말했어요.

sents.en: The attack happened on Friday evening at the Byar La camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of the state capital Sittwe.

pro.en: A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp for displaced people killed 12 people in Rakhine state, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday. The attack took place on Friday evening at the Byar La camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of the state capital Sittwe.

Khine Hein Htet, chairman of the rescue service Phyusin Yin Khwin Foundation, confirmed the toll of 12. He said a five-year-old child was among the dead and that 18 others were wounded. Many residents had lived in the camp for four years, and he said it was not a combat zone.

A shopkeeper named Chit Su Wai said she lost her daughter, aunt and mother in the strike, adding that nobody heard a fighter jet before the bombs fell. CNA reported that it was not possible to reach the Myanmar military for comment.

Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military seized power in a coup five years ago, which provoked armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions. Rakhine is among the regions hit hardest; it is controlled almost entirely by the Arakan Army, an ethnic minority force, and has been blockaded by the military and subjected to regular airstrikes.

ASEAN has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings since the 2021 coup, citing a lack of meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities. The monitoring group ACLED estimates that more than 100,000 people have been killed on all sides since the civil war began.

views.view: Witnesses and a rescue worker said the camp was not a combat area, and the military could not be reached for comment.

issues.title: Nvidia says it will still supply 260,000 GPUs to South Korea after its CEO resigned
issues.gist: South Korea's science minister said Nvidia will keep its plan to bring up to 260,000 GPUs to Korea. The news came after Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, suddenly resigned.
issues.gistKo: 과학기술정보통신부 장관은 엔비디아가 한국에 GPU 최대 26만 개를 들여오는 계획을 지키겠다고 했다고 밝혔어요. 젠슨 황 CEO가 갑자기 사임한 뒤 나온 소식이에요.
issues.easyKo: 엔비디아 CEO가 갑자기 물러나서 한국 AI 계획이 흔들릴까 걱정이 컸어요. 그런데 정부가 엔비디아와 회의를 해 보니 26만 개 GPU 공급 계획은 그대로라고 해요. 그래도 주식시장은 하루 종일 불안했어요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea's science minister said on Friday that Nvidia still plans to deploy up to 260,000 graphics processing units in Korea. Minister Bae Kyung-hoon wrote about it in a Facebook post after his ministry held a meeting with Nvidia. The meeting took place because Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, had suddenly resigned, and people worried that the plans might change. A GPU is a powerful chip that does many calculations at the same time and is widely used to train and run AI models.
paragraphs.ko: 과학기술정보통신부 장관은 금요일에 엔비디아가 한국에 최대 26만 개의 그래픽 처리 장치(GPU)를 배치할 계획을 그대로 유지한다고 말했어요. 배경훈 장관은 부처가 엔비디아와 회의를 연 뒤 페이스북 글로 이 내용을 알렸어요. 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자가 갑자기 사임해서 계획이 바뀔까 걱정하는 사람들이 있었기 때문에 회의가 열렸어요. GPU는 많은 계산을 동시에 하는 강력한 칩으로, AI 모델을 훈련하고 돌리는 데 널리 쓰여요.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia first announced the supply plan in October so that Korea could build large AI factories. The plan involves the government and big companies such as Samsung Electronics, SK Group, Hyundai Motor Group, and Naver Cloud. Each of them will build its own AI computing center powered by Nvidia's latest Blackwell chips. The minister said the government's own project to secure 50,000 GPUs is moving ahead as planned. So far Korea has obtained about 21,000 of the roughly 35,000 chips it will get directly from Nvidia. The rest should arrive by early next year.
paragraphs.ko: 엔비디아는 한국이 대규모 AI 공장을 지을 수 있도록 10월에 이 공급 계획을 처음 발표했어요. 이 계획에는 정부와 삼성전자, SK그룹, 현대자동차그룹, 네이버클라우드 같은 큰 기업이 함께해요. 각자 엔비디아의 최신 블랙웰 칩으로 돌아가는 자체 AI 컴퓨팅 센터를 세울 거예요. 장관은 정부가 GPU 5만 개를 확보하는 사업이 계획대로 진행되고 있다고 말했어요. 한국은 엔비디아에서 직접 받을 약 3만 5천 개 가운데 지금까지 약 2만 1천 개를 확보했어요. 나머지는 내년 초까지 들어올 예정이에요.

paragraphs.en: Bae said other projects will also go forward. They include building AI computing infrastructure and using Nvidia's NVLink to connect Korean-made AI chips to Nvidia's platforms. NVLink is an open, very fast data link that lets custom chips from other companies plug into Nvidia's AI networks. Markets were nervous that day, and the main Korean stock index, KOSPI, closed down 0.98 percent at 5,290.53. SK hynix fell 3.03 percent, and an analyst at Daishin Securities said foreign selling and rising AI uncertainty pulled the market down.

NVLink는 다른 회사가 만든 맞춤형 칩을 엔비디아의 AI 네트워크에 꽂아 쓸 수 있게 해 주는 개방형 초고속 데이터 통로예요. 그날 시장은 불안했고, 한국의 대표 주가 지수인 코스피는 0.98퍼센트 내린 5,290.53에 마감했어요. paragraphs.en: Industry voices were mixed about what the change means for Korea. Ahn Ki-hyun of the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association told The Korea Herald that Huang's exit could even be better for Korean memory makers. His reason was that Nvidia still needs high-bandwidth memory from a handful of suppliers, and it has few alternatives. An official at a Korean company with ties to Nvidia worried more about new businesses that Huang personally pushed, such as AI factories and robotics. The same official expected existing contracts to hold.

pro.en: South Korea's science minister said Friday that Nvidia remains committed to deploying up to 260,000 graphics processing units in the country, moving to calm concerns raised by chief executive Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation. Minister Bae Kyung-hoon disclosed the assurance in a Facebook post after his ministry held a meeting with the company. A GPU is a high-performance semiconductor designed to handle numerous calculations simultaneously, and it is widely used to train and operate AI models.

Nvidia first unveiled the supply plan in October to enable the construction of large-scale AI factories in Korea. The initiative brings together the government and major conglomerates, among them Samsung Electronics, SK Group, Hyundai Motor Group and Naver Cloud, each of which is to set up its own AI computing center powered by Nvidia's latest Blackwell processors. Bae said the state's separate effort to secure 50,000 GPUs is proceeding on schedule, with roughly 21,000 of the approximately 35,000 units due directly from Nvidia already in hand and the remainder expected by early next year.

Bae added that other collaborative projects will continue, including the buildout of AI computing infrastructure and the use of Nvidia's NVLink to integrate domestically produced AI chips with its platforms. NVLink is an open, ultrafast data link that allows third-party custom chips to plug directly into Nvidia's AI networks. Markets were jittery that day, with the benchmark KOSPI closing down 0.98 percent at 5,290.53, while SK hynix slid 3.03 percent. An analyst at Daishin Securities attributed the decline to foreign selling and mounting AI uncertainty.

Industry reaction to the leadership change was divided. Ahn Ki-hyun of the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association told The Korea Herald that Huang's departure could even prove advantageous to Korean memory manufacturers, arguing that Nvidia still depends on high-bandwidth memory from a small group of suppliers and has few viable alternatives. An official at a Korean company with ties to Nvidia voiced greater unease over new ventures Huang personally championed, such as AI factories and robotics, though the same person expected existing contracts to stand.

Nvidia has appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim chief executive and pledged to honor its customer commitments and product plans. For Korean students, the episode illustrates how tightly the country's AI ambitions are bound to a single foreign company. Attention now turns to whether the remaining GPUs arrive by early next year and whether the newer projects hold their pace.

pro.en: South Korea defeated Taiwan 6-4 in Tokyo on Saturday, collecting its first victory of the Asia Professional Baseball Championship, or APBC, and booking a place in Sunday night's final against Japan.

Korea had dropped its opening two games, 8-7 to Australia and 9-5 to Japan, and Japan's 16-1 rout of Australia earlier that day left Japan unbeaten at 3-0 while Korea, Taiwan and Australia all finished the round-robin phase at 1-2. A tiebreaking formula known as Team Quality Balance, or TQB, settled the standings, and Korea emerged on top of it.

Korea struck for three solo home runs at Tokyo Dome, the first from Park Jae-hyun leading off the third inning as Korea opened a 3-0 lead. Taiwan pulled level at 3-3 in the fifth through a solo homer and a two-run blast, but Kim Do-yeong, who topped the Korea Baseball Organization with 45 homers this season, snapped the tie with a solo shot in the bottom of that inning.

Park stretched the advantage to 5-3 with a sixth-inning double, and Taiwan trimmed the deficit to a single run in the seventh on a second home run from Zeng Sheng-An. Korea responded at once with a solo drive from Moon Jeong-bin.

The tournament is restricted to players 24 and under or those with no more than three years of professional experience, although each roster may include up to three players aged between 24 and 29. This third edition will feature a third consecutive Korea-Japan final, and Japan prevailed in both previous ones.

issues.easyKo: OpenAI는 로봇만 따로 연구하던 팀을 없애는 대신 연구원들을 다른 팀으로 옮겼어요. 하나의 큰 AI 모델이 로봇까지 조종할 수 있다고 보기 때문이에요. 다만 아직 모의 시험 결과가 많아서, 실제 로봇에서도 그런지는 더 지켜봐야 해요.

paragraphs.en: OpenAI has reorganized its robotics team and moved its researchers into other groups. Robotics researchers are joining the main research team, which is led by Chief Research Officer Mark Chen. The applied robotics and hardware teams are joining the Applied organization led by Greg Brockman. The Decoder first wrote that OpenAI was disbanding the team again, but OpenAI later said it was a reorganization and that robotics work continues. Fortune reports that the decision came very fast. OpenAI had already booked a booth at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, and the booth sat empty.
paragraphs.ko: OpenAI가 로봇 팀을 개편해 연구원들을 다른 조직으로 옮겼어요. 로봇 연구원들은 최고연구책임자 마크 첸이 이끄는 주 연구팀으로 합류해요. 응용 로봇 팀과 하드웨어 팀은 그레그 브록먼이 이끄는 Applied 조직에 들어가요. The Decoder는 처음에 OpenAI가 팀을 또 해체한다고 썼지만, OpenAI는 나중에 개편일 뿐이고 로봇 작업은 계속된다고 밝혔어요. 포천은 결정이 아주 급하게 내려졌다고 전해요. OpenAI는 이미 오스틴의 로봇 학습 학회에 부스를 예약해 뒀고, 그 부스는 비어 있었어요.

paragraphs.en: OpenAI apparently believes that general-purpose models such as GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly. If that is true, the company needs fewer special AI models built only for robots. In an Nvidia study, an agent powered by Astra succeeded on 74.8 percent of simulated robot tasks. The best specialized models reached 51 percent in the same study. The tests used a simulated DROID robot, not a real one.

paragraphs.en: Another test, called StationeryBench, compared Astra with MolmoAct2, a model from Ai2, on five tasks with desk objects. The tasks used dual-arm YAM robots. Across 200 trials, Astra fully completed 7 out of 100 tasks, while MolmoAct2 completed none. Astra's average progress score was 46, compared with 12 for MolmoAct2. In another test, Astra running on a humanoid robot moved around a kitchen and cleaned it up. Yoav Artzi, an AI researcher at Cornell University and Google DeepMind, also sees Astra as a major leap in spatial understanding. He says it reaches near-human accuracy on REMAP, a benchmark that is still unpublished. He suspects OpenAI trained it on large amounts of 3D data such as Blender scenes.
paragraphs.ko: StationeryBench라는 다른 시험은 Astra와 Ai2의 모델 MolmoAct2를 책상 물건을 다루는 다섯 과제로 견줬어요. 이 과제에는 팔이 둘인 YAM 로봇을 썼어요. 200번의 시도에서 Astra는 100개 중 7개 과제를 끝까지 해냈고, MolmoAct2는 하나도 끝내지 못했어요. Astra의 평균 진행 점수는 46점으로, MolmoAct2의 12점보다 높았어요. 다른 시험에서는 사람 모양 로봇에서 돌아가는 Astra가 주방을 돌아다니며 치웠어요. 코넬대와 구글 딥마인드의 AI 연구자 요아브 아르치도 Astra를 공간 이해의 큰 도약으로 봐요. 그는 아직 공개되지 않은 시험 REMAP에서 사람에 가까운 정확도를 보인다고 해요. 그는 OpenAI가 블렌더 장면 같은 3D 자료를 많이 학습시켰을 것으로 짐작해요.

paragraphs.en: OpenAI closed its robotics division in 2020. Co-founder Wojciech Zaremba said the company lacked the training data it needed and that large language models were a faster path to AGI. The company rebuilt the team in 2024. CEO Sam Altman is reportedly aiming for a first public robot demo in 2027. OpenAI wants to build its own everyday robots in the long term. The company also faces heavy financial pressure to focus on its core AI business, where it has lost significant ground to Anthropic.

pro.en: OpenAI has restructured its robotics group, folding researchers into other teams: robotics researchers are moving to the main research organization under Chief Research Officer Mark Chen, while the applied robotics and hardware units are joining Greg Brockman's Applied division. The Decoder initially reported that the company was disbanding the team again, but OpenAI subsequently clarified that this was a reorganization and that robotics work continues, and Fortune reports that the decision came so abruptly that OpenAI had already reserved a booth at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, which then stood empty.

OpenAI evidently believes that general-purpose models such as GPT-6 Astra can operate robots directly, which would reduce the need for dedicated robotics models. In an Nvidia study, an agent driven by Astra succeeded on 74.8 percent of simulated robotics tasks, against 51 percent for the strongest specialized models, although the experiments relied on a simulated DROID robot rather than physical hardware.

A new benchmark, StationeryBench, pitted Astra against Ai2's MolmoAct2 on five desk-object tasks performed by dual-arm YAM robots: across 200 trials, Astra fully completed 7 of 100 tasks and MolmoAct2 none, with average progress scores of 46 and 12, respectively. In a separate demonstration, Astra running on a humanoid robot navigated a kitchen and tidied it, and Yoav Artzi, an AI researcher at Cornell University and Google DeepMind, likewise regards the model as a major advance in spatial understanding, citing near-human accuracy on the still-unpublished REMAP benchmark and speculating that OpenAI may have trained it on extensive 3D data such as Blender scenes.

How much robotics data OpenAI and its rivals folded into training remains unclear, and large general-purpose models from Anthropic and Google have also advanced on robotics tasks of late. Specialized robotics models may nonetheless retain advantages in cost, reliability, speed and energy consumption, even if they generalize less well.

OpenAI shut down its robotics division in 2020 because, in co-founder Wojciech Zaremba's account, it lacked the training data it required and large language models offered a quicker route to AGI, then rebuilt the team in 2024. CEO Sam Altman is reportedly aiming for a first public robot demonstration in 2027, and the company wants eventually to build its own everyday robots, yet it also faces heavy financial pressure to concentrate on its core AI business, where it has lost considerable ground to Anthropic.

pro.en: Two Americans, a 38-year-old man and a 40-year-old woman, died in a suspected drowning in the Bahamas on Friday afternoon after strong ocean currents carried off a group of swimmers, police said. Several swimmers were swept away at once.

The Royal Bahamas Police Force said it received a report shortly before 3 p.m. and dispatched officers to the southern point of North Bimini, near the entrance to Bimini Harbour, on an island in the Bahamas. The group had ventured beyond an area marked with a sign warning of strong currents.

A nearby ferry boat helped some of the swimmers to safety. The two Americans were found unresponsive and received CPR before being taken to a local clinic, where an attending physician pronounced them dead shortly before 4 p.m.

Police said foul play is not suspected. An autopsy will be conducted to establish the precise cause of death, and the investigation is ongoing. The incident underscores the importance of heeding posted warnings about strong currents at beaches.

pro.en: Wales ended a 73-year drought against New Zealand with a 35-28 victory in the Nations Championship in Cardiff on Saturday, their first win over the All Blacks since 1953. The result snapped a run of 34 consecutive defeats to the three-times world champions.

The hosts struck twice early, the first try coming inside 90 seconds, through Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake to open a 14-0 lead. New Zealand rallied, and the sides were level at 21-21 at the interval.

The All Blacks were widely expected to pull clear after the break, but Wales scored twice more in quick succession: Eddie James crossed in the 44th minute and Louis Rees-Zammit five minutes later, stretching the lead to 35-21. Peter Lakai pulled one back for New Zealand in the 53rd minute.

The visitors then laid siege to the Welsh line, only to be held up three times as the home defence made 346 tackles in all. Man of the match James Botham credited belief, the crowd's energy and defensive training, and several Wales players were in tears at the final whistle.
It was only the fourth time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 39 meetings. Sam Costelow kicked superbly for the hosts, while all four New Zealand tries were converted by Richie Mo'unga.

pro.en: The Guardian has launched a series tracking eight young Britons through their job searches. The opening instalment profiles four of them, who recount an unending cycle of applications and rejections; all names have been changed.

Aamir, 25, holds a BA and an MA from two London universities and reckons he has submitted more than 1,000 applications since graduating last year. A temporary digital publishing post lapsed after a few months, and he now lives with his parents and receives universal credit. He argues that the social contract in Britain feels broken and that employers should be asked why entry-level roles have become so hard to secure.

Alice, 24, attended Oxford and Cambridge yet, more than a year on, lives at home in Bristol and depends financially on her parents; she has filed 50 tailored applications and has reached interview five times. Liam, 20, of Exeter, trained in horticulture and land management but has spent two years cycling through brief jobs and rejections. Autistic, he says employers ought to make reasonable adjustments, and he volunteers at community gardens while attending Connect to Work, a government-backed scheme.

Peter, 21, studied computer science at Leicester University and has applied for more than 50 posts without securing an interview. He blames AI for eroding entry-level work, questioning why a firm would take on 10 graduates when one equipped with AI can do the work of 10. Official data sketch the broader picture: the Office for National Statistics estimated that 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were NEET, neither in education, employment nor training, in April to June 2026, or 13.0% of young people.

Many students in Korea likewise face a punishing job hunt, so the accounts may resonate: experience is demanded yet hard to acquire, replies are scarce, and AI may reshape entry-level work. The series will continue to follow the eight young people.

issues.title: US blames old technology and a contractor's upgrade work for a nationwide flight stop
issues.gist: All flights in the United States were stopped for about four hours on Friday after communication and radar problems at air traffic control centers. Officials blamed old equipment.
issues.gistKo: 금요일에 항공 교통 관제 센터의 통신과 레이더에 문제가 생겨 미국 전역의 비행기가 약 네 시간 동안 멈췄어요. 당국은 낡은 장비를 탓했어요.
issues.easyKo: 미국 교통부 장관은 오래된 통신선을 새것으로 바꾸는 계약업체의 작업 중에 문제가 시작됐다고 말했어요. 사이버 공격의 증거는 없다고 했고, 지연과 결항은 주말까지 이어졌어요.

paragraphs.en: A rare nationwide ground stop stopped thousands of flights at all US airports on Friday, Nov. 13. It lasted about four hours and was one of the biggest disruptions to US air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001. The Federal Aviation Administration said the problem hit the regional air traffic control centers that handle high-altitude traffic.
paragraphs.ko: 11월 13일 금요일, 드문 전국 운항 정지 때문에 미국 모든 공항에서 수천 편의 비행기가 멈췄어요. 이 정지는 약 네 시간 이어졌고, 2001년 9월 11일 테러 이후 미국 항공 교통에서 가장 큰 혼란 가운데 하나였어요. 연방항공청은 높은 고도의 항공 교통을 맡는 지역 관제 센터들에 문제가 생겼다고 밝혔어요.

paragraphs.en: On Friday night, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the centers had "intermittent" outages of their radar and communications systems. He blamed old technology and said, "It got overloaded." When reporters asked why the systems failed on a normal travel day, he did not have a ready answer. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was zero evidence of a cyber attack.
paragraphs.ko: 금요일 밤 숀 더피 교통부 장관은 관제 센터의 레이더와 통신 시스템이 "간헐적으로" 끊겼다고 말했어요. 그는 낡은 기술을 탓하며 "과부하가 걸렸다"고 말했어요. 기자들이 평범한 여행일에 왜 시스템이 고장 났는지 묻자 그는 바로 답하지 못했어요. 마크웨인 멀린 국토안보부 장관은 사이버 공격의 증거가 전혀 없다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: On Saturday, Duffy gave more detail. He said a contractor, L3Harris, was doing routine maintenance at a remote location, changing old copper wire to fiber optics. An error then started flooding other routers in the air traffic control system. The FAA is still checking whether it was a user error or a faulty router. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said there was no evidence of anything nefarious or any AI-related issue.

pro.en: A rare nationwide ground stop halted thousands of flights at every US airport on Friday, Nov. 13, for roughly four hours, in one of the most severe disruptions to American air travel since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. The Federal Aviation Administration said the failure struck the regional Air Route Traffic Control Centers that manage high-altitude traffic.

At a Friday night briefing, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the facilities had suffered intermittent outages of radar and communications systems, which he attributed to antiquated technology that had become overloaded, though he had no ready explanation when pressed on why it faltered on an ordinary travel day. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was zero evidence of a cyberattack.

On Saturday, Duffy said the trouble began when L3Harris, a longtime FAA contractor, was performing routine maintenance at a remote site, swapping copper wire for fiber optics, and an error began flooding other routers in the air traffic control network. The agency is still investigating whether it was installer error or a faulty router, and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said there was no sign of foul play or any AI-related problem.

The fallout stretched into the weekend: FlightAware logged nearly 25,000 delays and more than 9,000 cancellations on Friday, and Cirium counted over 4,000 cancellations on Saturday morning, or 18% of US departures. Bedford said schedules should normalize by Sunday evening, with passengers rebooked or fully refunded.

Duffy noted that Congress approved $12.5 billion in July 2025 to modernize air traffic control, with Bedford saying 70% of copper communications had since been replaced by fiber, and Duffy argued that more funding is needed to finish the work. Sen. Richard Blumenthal demanded a prompt, penetrating investigation into the causes.

pro.en: South Korean equities slid almost 1 percent on Friday, Nov. 13, with the benchmark KOSPI closing down 52.20 points, or 0.98 percent, at 5,290.53. The index had opened 2.05 percent higher and touched 5,504.44 before slipping into negative territory around 12:35 p.m.

Investors turned cautious over the potential fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure for the artificial intelligence ecosystem, given his pivotal role in the recent AI boom. Major U.S. indices had closed lower overnight following his exit, and traders were also awaiting U.S. producer price data that might offer clues to Federal Reserve policy after a steeper-than-expected rise in consumer prices earlier in the week.

Foreign investors were net sellers of 550.5 billion won in shares, whereas institutions bought 2.3 billion won and individuals made net purchases of 17.2 billion won. Turnover was subdued at 237.3 million shares worth 16 trillion won, or $11.9 billion, and advancers outnumbered decliners 450 to 418.

Technology shares drove the decline. Samsung Electronics shed 0.96 percent to 206,000 won, while SK hynix sank 3.03 percent to 1.2 million won, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics tumbled 3.5 percent. Naver, in which Nvidia is the third-largest shareholder, slumped 5.12 percent to 172,500 won, and Korea Electric Power plunged 9.79 percent, whereas Hyundai Motor gained 1.13 percent and KB Financial Group surged 4.74 percent.

Lee Kyoung-min of Daishin Securities said the market opened higher but turned negative on foreign selling, adding that, absent prominent negative factors, mounting AI uncertainty weighed heavily. The won was quoted at 1,336.7 per dollar at 3:30 p.m., and bond prices closed lower, with the three-year yield adding 3 basis points to 3.759.

pro.en: A new food tour called Kkokkio Gyorae has been introduced in Gyorae-ri, a village in Jeju City designated a native chicken distribution special zone in 2009, as part of the K-Food Belt project led by the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs and the Korean Food Promotion Institute, which this year turns to chicken with belts in Suwon, Gumi, Chuncheon and Jeju Island.

The Jeju program centers on the Gueom chicken, the only breed recognized as native to the island, which was listed in 2025 on the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's Domestic Animal Diversity Information System; the bloodline was once broken and later restored, and the birds are now raised free-range on 10 farms in Aewol, where hens lay roughly one egg every three days and producers are still working to bring quality and volume up.

The itinerary begins at 1950 Winery, where visitors bake egg tarts with Gueom eggs and tour a winery that makes wine from tangerines rather than grapes, a label once poured as an official dinner wine at the 2010 G20 Seoul Summit; dinner revives charcoal-grilled chicken, a Jeju dish that had largely vanished, and breakfast is dakgomtang, a clear native chicken soup.

The group then walks the Samdasoo Forest Trail for 50 minutes in the Nordic style with poles, before visiting the Jeju Samdasoo factory, which is permitted to draw 4,600 tons of groundwater daily and whose operator runs bottle collection bins that, since 2021, have given 8 won in points per bottle at some sites.

A lunch course serving a single chicken in three stages -- raw slices for shabu-shabu, boiled whole chicken and mung bean porridge -- closes the tour, which the institute describes as being as much about regional stories as about food, though producers must still lift quality and volume to a level the market can sustain.

views.view: The tour mixes local food, drinks and walks to tell the story of a restored native chicken.

pro.en: Spain manager Luis de la Fuente has insisted that "there is no racism in Spain" after England head coach Thomas Tuchel said he would remind his squad of anti-racism protocols ahead of Sunday's fixture. De la Fuente made the remarks at a news conference on Saturday.

The Nations League tie marks the first time Spain has hosted England in Madrid since 2004, when England's players were targeted with racist abuse from the stands. The sides have met three times elsewhere in Spain since, without incident.

Tuchel stressed that he did not anticipate any trouble at the Metropolitano. Last month, however, FIFA fined the Spanish football federation 15,000 euros and ordered a partial stadium closure after supporters chanted an Islamophobic slogan during a friendly against Egypt on March 31, an episode forward Lamine Yamal branded ignorant and racist.

De la Fuente also confirmed that Yamal is available to face England and in perfect condition, after the winger sat out Spain's 2-0 victory in Czechia on Thursday with a knee problem. Spain top Group C having won all five matches, including a 3-1 triumph over England at Wembley, and De la Fuente billed the contest as among the best in world football at present.

views.view: ESPN reports that the Spain coach rejected claims of racism in Spain, while also noting the past abuse in 2004 and last month's FIFA fine.

pro.en: South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT announced on Saturday that it will look into disruptions suffered by domestic companies as a result of a worldwide outage of Microsoft services.
Microsoft 365 services experienced problems earlier in the week, beginning on Thursday, and some firms in Korea reported difficulty accessing their email on Friday.

The ministry intends to verify whether the services have been fully restored and whether Korean users sustained any damage, working with Microsoft Korea, and it will set up a joint emergency response team with the company to monitor developments.

The BBC and the Guardian reported that Microsoft said on Saturday morning that every service was restored; the outage reached more than 70 countries and, the company said, was not a cyberattack; about 430 million people use the affected Microsoft 365 apps. The ministry's findings and Microsoft's full report are the next points to watch.

views.view: The ministry will check damage to Korean users and form a joint emergency team with Microsoft.

pro.en: The South Korean government on Friday left its ceilings on fuel prices untouched for a fifth consecutive period, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced, citing elevated international crude prices and persistent instability in the Middle East.

The ceilings, which limit what refiners may charge when supplying gas stations, remain at 1,784 won per liter for gasoline, 1,773 won for diesel and 1,380 won for kerosene for the four weeks starting Saturday. Authorities have held them at those levels for 20 weeks since June 27, following a reduction on June 26.

The ministry acknowledged that crude had slipped below $100 a barrel, with Brent reaching $96 on Nov. 12, but noted that the price remains more than $20 above its level at the end of June. The freeze, it said, is intended to ease upward pressure on consumer prices amid elevated oil prices and high ocean freight costs.

The price caps were first introduced in mid-March to stabilize domestic fuel prices after supply chain disruptions stemming from the US-Iran war in the Middle East. The ministry said it would adjust the emergency measures as necessary while closely monitoring Middle East developments and domestic economic conditions.

views.view: The government says the freeze is meant to ease price pressure while oil stays high and the Middle East stays tense.

pro.en: Anthony Santander, an outfielder for the Toronto Blue Jays, issued an apology on Friday for sharing anti-Muslim posts on social media. In a statement on Instagram, he said the content had caused hurt and fallen short of his own convictions.

Santander shared the posts on Nov. 4 and removed them the following morning. They included a video of a Christian preacher disparaging Muslims and another post suggesting Sharia law would be imposed on the United States after Abdul El-Sayed's election to the Senate in Michigan.

Santander said reflection and conversations with people he trusts had led him to recognize that he should have been more thoughtful. He asserted that every person deserves dignity and respect regardless of religion, background or beliefs, voiced respect for the Muslim community and pledged to avoid content that promotes hate.

The apology came a day after the club's president and chief executive, Mark Shapiro, apologized to the Muslim community and to fans following a meeting with community leaders. General manager Ross Atkins had urged Santander to address the controversy publicly.

Santander, a 32-year-old Venezuelan, signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with Toronto in January 2025 but missed the entire 2026 season with injuries. It remains unclear whether the club will discipline him.

views.view: Santander apologized, saying the posts hurt people and did not match his beliefs, and it is unclear if the team will discipline him.
The player deleted the posts the next morning, and the Blue Jays have not announced any disciplinary action.

issues.title: Could the AI Boom Make Borrowing More Expensive in Europe?
issues.gist: US tech giants are selling huge amounts of bonds to pay for AI, and they now compete with European governments and firms for investor money. Some worry this could push European borrowing costs higher.
issues.gistKo: 미국 빅테크가 AI 투자 자금을 마련하려고 채권을 대량으로 팔면서, 유럽 정부와 기업과 투자금을 두고 경쟁해요. 유럽의 빌리는 비용이 오를 수 있다는 걱정이 나와요.
issues.easyKo: AI 데이터센터를 짓는 큰 회사들이 빚을 많이 내고 있어요. 돈이 그쪽으로 몰리면 프랑스 같은 유럽 나라가 돈을 빌릴 때 이자가 더 오를 수 있다는 이야기예요.

paragraphs.en: DW reported on Nov. 3 that US tech companies are borrowing huge amounts to pay for artificial intelligence, and that may make borrowing harder for European governments and firms. More than $1 trillion is going into the AI buildout, so tech giants now compete with Europe for the same investment money.
paragraphs.ko: DW는 11월 3일 미국 기술 기업들이 인공지능 비용을 대려고 막대한 돈을 빌리고 있고, 이는 유럽 정부와 기업의 차입을 더 어렵게 할 수 있다고 전했어요. AI 구축에 1조 달러 넘게 들어가면서 빅테크는 이제 같은 투자금을 두고 유럽과 경쟁해요.

paragraphs.en: Four of the five biggest hyperscalers, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle, have issued about $250 billion in dollar bonds since the start of 2025. They have also sold €37 billion in bonds in euros. Microsoft recently joined with a $25 billion bond sale in dollars. Goldman Sachs expects new AI hyperscaler bond sales to reach $420 billion next year. The Dutch bank ING expects about €60 billion of those sales to be in euros.
paragraphs.ko: 5대 하이퍼스케일러 가운데 아마존, 알파벳, 메타, 오라클 네 곳은 2025년 초부터 약 2,500억 달러어치 달러 채권을 발행했어요. 이들은 유로 채권도 370억 유로어치 팔았어요. 마이크로소프트도 최근 250억 달러어치 달러 채권을 팔며 합류했어요. 골드만삭스는 내년 AI 하이퍼스케일러의 새 채권 판매가 4,200억 달러에 이를 것으로 내다봐요. 네덜란드 은행 ING는 그중 약 600억 유로가 유로로 발행될 것으로 봐요.

paragraphs.en: This is bad news for countries like France, Germany and Italy, whose bond yields have risen sharply in recent months. France has public debt of 119% of gross domestic product and a deficit above 5%. Over six months, its 10-year bond yield rose from roughly 3.7% to nearly 5%. Its interest bill is set to rise from €79 billion to €91 billion next year.

paragraphs.en: In August, economists at the European Central Bank said the euro bond market was adapting well. They also warned that the AI giants could make it harder for other companies and sectors to get finance. Viktor Hjort of BNP Paribas called the situation bond abundance and said companies and governments already compete for available funds. Goldman Sachs said interest costs as a share of sales at Stoxx 600 firms have risen by nearly half since 2022. The bank said this cut earnings by more than 5%.

DW notes that AI bonds are not the only cause of Europe's money problems, but more sales next year could add pressure.
