sents.en: DW notes that AI bonds are not the only cause of Europe's money problems, but more sales next year could add pressure.
sents.ko: DW는 AI 채권이 유럽 재정 문제의 유일한 원인은 아니지만 내년 추가 발행이 압박을 더할 수 있다고 짚어요.

pro.en: DW reported on Nov. 3 that US technology giants are borrowing on an enormous scale to finance artificial intelligence, a trend that could make credit costlier for European governments and companies. With more than $1 trillion flowing into the AI buildout, the hyperscalers now vie with Europe for the same pool of investment capital.

Four of the Big Five hyperscalers, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle, have issued about $250 billion in dollar bonds since the start of 2025, and a further €37 billion in euro-denominated debt. Microsoft, the last to hold back, recently joined with a $25 billion dollar bond sale. Goldman Sachs projects that new hyperscaler bond sales will reach $420 billion next year, and the Dutch bank ING expects about €60 billion in euros.

That is unwelcome news for France, Germany and Italy, whose sovereign yields have climbed sharply in recent months. France carries public debt equal to 119% of gross domestic product and a deficit above 5%, and its 10-year yield has risen from roughly 3.7% to nearly 5% over six months. Its annual interest bill is set to increase from €79 billion to €91 billion next year.

In August, economists at the European Central Bank said the euro bond market was adapting well but cautioned that the AI giants could make it harder for other firms and sectors to obtain financing. Viktor Hjort of BNP Paribas described the phenomenon as bond abundance and said companies and governments already compete for available fixed income funds. Goldman Sachs found that interest costs as a share of sales at Stoxx 600 companies have climbed by nearly half since 2022, trimming earnings by more than 5%.

An OECD study published in January compared local bond markets in five countries and found that borrowing costs for cities and regions tended to rise where AI was spreading fastest. Its co-author Christos Makridis noted that in the United States, AI investment is linked to lower borrowing costs, whereas the opposite appears to hold in several European countries. DW stresses that AI bonds are far from the sole cause of Europe's fiscal strains, yet the additional issuance planned for next year could add further pressure.

views.view: US tech borrowing for AI could add pressure on European governments and firms, though AI bonds are far from the only cause of Europe's fiscal strain.

pro.en: Since September, a canvas by the Korean painter Paek Yunzo has been on view at the Louvre-Lens, the Louvre's regional outpost in a former coal-mining town in northern France. Her 2024 oil painting "Free Riders" is among more than 300 works in "So Cute! The Art of Happiness."

The exhibition, a sweeping survey of cuteness in art, remains open through Jan. 18. It was organized by Annabelle Teneze, the Louvre-Lens director, together with Emilie Girard of the Musees de la Ville de Strasbourg, and includes a section examining how cuteness is articulated and prized in Korean society.

"Free Riders" is one of several paintings with that title in Paek's "Walk" series, which depicts figures strolling with small animals in tow. Gallery Joeun has characterized the series as a humorous riff on the artist's affection for pets. Her paintings frequently distill the human form into spare lines and vivid color set against flat, single-hue grounds. Born in 1980, Paek completed her studies in painting at Dongduk Women's University in Seoul.

According to 313 Art Project, one of her galleries, Paek and the painter Woo Kukwon are the first Korean artists of their generation to exhibit at the Louvre-Lens. Paek has mounted five solo shows in Seoul since 2019, and her work has also been presented at Art Paris and Art Miami.

She is now showing roughly 10 new paintings in "Still," a two-person exhibition with the Tokyo-based painter Tatsuhito Horikoshi at Gallery Joeun in Itaewon, which runs through Dec. 5. The gallery says the title carries a double meaning: a moment frozen in time, or a state that persists.

views.view: Paek is one of the first Korean artists of her generation to join a Louvre-Lens show, and her new Seoul show pairs her with a Tokyo painter.

pro.en: The South Korean startup DeepX Co. intends to commit more than $100 million to a next-generation artificial intelligence chip, the DX-M2, which will be fabricated on Samsung Electronics Co.'s advanced 2-nanometer process.

DeepX has completed the design of the DX-M2 and delivered the final plans to Samsung's foundry unit for production. The company expects to secure its first silicon by March 2027, before moving on to customer evaluations and mass manufacturing in 2028.

The project is projected to cost more than $100 million, a figure that covers performance verification and production engineering expenses. DeepX is targeting robots, industrial equipment and AI-enabled personal computers, and says the chip is built to run generative-AI models on roughly 5 watts of power.

The outlay represents a significant wager on running AI models directly on devices rather than depending on computing power in remote data centers. The approach can curb the energy use, costs and latency associated with shuttling data to and from the cloud. DeepX's semiconductors are meant for workloads outside data centers, which face mounting backlash over their enormous power and water consumption.

views.view: The bet on on-device AI could cut energy use, costs and delays, and it avoids the backlash facing data centers.

pro.en: South Korea's largest festival devoted to traditional alcoholic beverages opened in Seoul on Friday with a record 142 producers, as the government seeks to convert swelling global interest in Korean cuisine into overseas sales of rice wine, fruit wine and distilled spirits.

The three-day event, now in its 16th year, runs through Sunday at the aT Center in Yangjae, southern Seoul. The Agriculture Ministry anticipates roughly 30,000 visitors, up from 28,000 last year, when 120 producers took part. Attendees can brew makgeolli, a cloudy Korean rice wine, and sample cocktails mixed with traditional drinks. Among other attractions are an artificial intelligence sommelier that recommends drinks according to a visitor's palate and a blind tasting in which participants try to pick out this year's presidential award winner.

At the opening ceremony, the ministry presented awards to 18 drinks. Blue Wine Company, based in Yeongdong, North Chungcheong Province, took the top honor for Berry Wine 1168CS, a fruit wine. Deputy head Jin Kyung-sook said it was the first producer in Yeongdong County to win the presidential award, adding that the recognition showed a sweet wine could appeal to a broad audience.

Douglas Passos, a 29-year-old visitor from Mexico, took part in a makgeolli workshop and learned how rice ferments with nuruk, a traditional Korean fermentation starter, telling the ministry he hoped to introduce the drink to friends back home. Agriculture Minister Song Mi-ryung met producers after the ceremony to discuss ways of reaching more overseas buyers, pledging that the government would help them secure high-quality ingredients and distributors abroad and gauge demand in new markets. The ministry also honored Kooksoondang, a makgeolli maker whose exports totaled $46.15 million over the past five years.

views.view: The report frames the festival as a chance to turn interest in Korean food into overseas sales of traditional drinks.

issues.title: Samsung Lions Stars Lead the List of Free Agents After the Korean Series Title
issues.gist: Two stars of the Samsung Lions top the list of 28 players who can become free agents in Korean baseball. The Lions just won the Korean Series.

paragraphs.en: Two stars of the Samsung Lions headlined the list of possible free agents in South Korean baseball this week. The Korea Baseball Organization released the list on Friday, Nov. 13, and it names 28 players who can become free agents this offseason. The Lions won the Korean Series title this month by beating the KT Wiz in five games.

pro.en: Two stars of the Samsung Lions topped the list of prospective free agents in South Korean baseball this week. The Korea Baseball Organization published the roster on Friday, Nov. 13, naming 28 players who are eligible for free agency this offseason, and the Lions secured the Korean Series title this month with a five-game victory over the KT Wiz.

Captain Koo Ja-wook, 33, was named Korean Series MVP after going 10-for-20 at the plate with a home run and six RBIs. He also captured his first career batting title this season with a .371 average. He has reportedly retained a U.S.-based agent in pursuit of a major league opportunity, although the Lions are expected to try to retain him for several more years.

Starter Won Tae-in, 26, was the winning pitcher in the title-clinching game, working five innings and yielding a single run. His postseason success belied a difficult regular season, in which he went 7-9 with a 4.52 ERA over 26 outings, his worst ERA and fewest wins in six years. With few viable starting pitchers available, he is expected to command considerable interest.

Eligible players have until Sunday to exercise their rights, and the final list will be published on Monday, after which clubs may negotiate and sign them beginning Tuesday. The league divides free agents into three classes by salary, each carrying its own compensation terms. For a Class A player, the signing club must pay his former team twice his previous salary and surrender a player outside its protected list, or pay three times the salary.

views.view: Two Lions stars, Koo Ja-wook and Won Tae-in, lead the list, and few other good starting pitchers are available.

issues.title: Severe Drought Could Push Many Cactus Species Toward Extinction
issues.gist: A new study looked at 993 cactus species and added severe drought to its forecasts. It found that many more species could lose much of their living area.
issues.gistKo: 새 연구가 선인장 993종을 대상으로 심한 가뭄까지 넣어 예측했어요. 더 많은 종이 서식 가능한 땅을 크게 잃을 수 있다고 나왔어요.
issues.easyKo: 보통 선인장은 가뭄에 강하다고 생각하지만, 이 연구는 심한 가뭄과 더위가 겹치면 위험이 훨씬 커진다고 했어요. 평균 기후만 본 예측보다 훨씬 나쁜 결과가 나왔어요.

paragraphs.en: A new study in Nature, published on Nov. 11, looked at how severe drought and warming could affect cacti. Cacti are often seen as plants that handle dry weather well. The researchers studied 993 cactus species from a family that is already highly threatened.
paragraphs.ko: 11월 11일 네이처에 실린 새 연구는 심한 가뭄과 온난화가 선인장에 어떤 영향을 줄지 살펴봤어요. 선인장은 흔히 건조한 날씨에 잘 견디는 식물로 여겨져요. 연구진은 이미 큰 위협을 받는 과에 속한 선인장 993종을 연구했어요.

sents.en: A new study in Nature, published on Nov. 11, looked at how severe drought and warming could affect cacti.
sents.ko: 11월 11일 네이처에 실린 새 연구는 심한 가뭄과 온난화가 선인장에 어떤 영향을 줄지 살펴봤어요.

sents.ko: 연구진은 이미 큰 위협을 받는 과에 속한 선인장 993종을 연구했어요.

paragraphs.en: Most forecasts of climate change and wildlife use long-term average climate and leave out extreme events. The team added new data on severe drought and warmer temperatures. They also used 648,316 records of where cacti have been found, and built computer models of suitable climate. In 91% of cases, the models that included severe drought fit better than those using average climate.
paragraphs.ko: 기후 변화와 야생 생물에 관한 대부분의 예측은 장기 평균 기후를 쓰고 극단적 사건은 빼요. 연구진은 심한 가뭄과 더 높은 기온에 관한 새 자료를 더했어요. 또 선인장이 발견된 위치 기록 648,316건을 써서 알맞은 기후를 보여 주는 컴퓨터 모델을 만들었어요. 91%의 경우에 심한 가뭄을 넣은 모델이 평균 기후만 쓴 모델보다 더 잘 맞았어요.

pro.en: A new study published in Nature on Nov. 11 examines how severe drought, compounded by warming, may affect cacti, a family long assumed to be drought tolerant yet already among the most threatened plant groups; the analysis covers 993 species.

Because most projections of climate-driven biodiversity loss rely on long-term mean conditions and omit extreme events, the authors integrated new spatial data on severe drought and warmer temperatures with 648,316 occurrence records and species distribution models, finding that models incorporating severe drought were better supported in 91% of cases.

Including drought raised the share of species projected to lose suitable climatic area from 58-61% to 69-72%, the share losing over a quarter from 26-43% to 55-58%, and the share losing over four-fifths from 1-15% to 25-35%, while restricting dispersal to zero kilometers pushed the share losing area to 84-85%.

Five bioregions could forfeit more than 25% of their species, and an accompanying Nature expert opinion warned that more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of suitable area by 2100; the authors contend that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability.

They argue that incorporating such extremes will be critical to designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems, and further work will show whether other species yield comparable results.

views.view: Including severe drought makes the risk of extinction for cacti much higher than average-climate forecasts show.
More than a quarter of cactus species could lose at least 80% of suitable area by 2100.

pro.en: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon has claimed the top position on MathArena, a benchmark of AI mathematical ability, becoming the first model from a developer other than OpenAI to lead the rankings in some time and displacing GPT-6.1 Sol. Claude Fable 5.2 placed second, which makes both contenders arguably among the most capable publicly accessible systems for mathematical work, while OpenAI's newest models, said to have recently cracked formidable problems such as the Navier-Stokes equations, remain unavailable to the public.

The evaluation also exposed distinct weaknesses in Carbon: its most frequent failure was overrunning the time limit, and it almost never abandons a problem, a tendency that can be judged either an asset or a liability, as when it launched a script that ran for more than eleven hours without once checking its own progress.

That extra performance carries a steep premium, however. Under the reasoning settings applied in testing, Carbon and Fable 5.2 cost roughly 15 and 40 times as much as GPT-6.1 Sol, respectively, so the two leaders excel at mathematics but are far more expensive than the model they displaced.

Google's AI overview still links to his discredited papers when people search for Himalayan landmarks.

paragraphs.en: Experts do not agree on what to do. Svante Pääbo says his 1985 mummy DNA paper was wrong because of contamination, yet he thinks it should stand. pro.en: Nature reported that the scientific literature still holds decades-old papers detailing fraudulent, unethical or merely incorrect results that carry no warning label. Many were neglected for decades, but digitization now allows AI tools that summarize research to feed their errors to a new generation, leaving publishers to weigh whether to retract such work or simply flag it.

One case involves Vishwa Jit Gupta, a celebrated Indian palaeontologist, whose Himalayan research was challenged in 1987. Investigations later found more than 450 publications containing non-existent collection sites, plagiarized images and stolen specimens. Gupta died in 2022, and none of his papers has been retracted; Google's AI overview still directs searchers looking up Himalayan landmarks to his discredited work.

Retraction as a safeguard is a relatively recent practice. In the early 2000s only about 30 retraction notices appeared each year, whereas more than 10,000 were recorded in 2023. Nature's analysis identified 358 retraction notices and 120 expressions of concern for papers more than 20 years old when the action was taken. Such papers accounted for roughly 0.7% of retractions since 2015, up from 0.2% before 2010, and the longest gap on record is 80 years, for a prank case report published in 1923.

Experts disagree about how to proceed. Svante Pääbo concedes that his 1985 mummy DNA paper was erroneous owing to contamination but contends that it should stand, arguing that correcting very old papers would generate more confusion than clarity. By contrast, Elsevier scrubbed two 1984 papers on caesium cancer therapy this April, after a student review uncovered 20 case reports of people ingesting the toxic chemical; ethics guidelines permit deletion when content could pose a serious health risk.

Responses have also been inconsistent. King's College London concluded in 2019 that 24 articles by Hans Eysenck and a collaborator were unsafe, yet only 16 have been retracted and four more carry expressions of concern, and 94 of Eysenck's papers in all have been retracted or flagged so far. A Springer Nature research integrity director said that when available information is limited, an expression of concern is likely the preferred mechanism.

views.view: Publishers are unsure whether to retract or only flag very old flawed papers, and experts do not agree.
Digitized old papers can feed misinformation to a new generation through AI tools that summarize research.

issues.title: Runway releases open-source Praxis-1, a robot model that learned from video
issues.gist: AI company Runway has released its robot model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code. It learned from video and scored well in the company's own tests.
issues.gistKo: AI 회사 런웨이가 로봇 모델 프락시스-1을 공개했어요. 코드와 모델 가중치를 누구나 쓸 수 있게 열었고, 회사가 직접 한 시험에서 좋은 결과를 냈어요.
issues.easyKo: 프락시스-1은 영상을 보며 배운 지식으로 로봇을 움직이는 AI 모델이에요. 아직은 비슷하게 생긴 물건을 헷갈리기도 하고, 시험 결과도 회사가 직접 낸 거라 다른 곳의 확인이 필요해요.

paragraphs.en: AI company Runway has released Praxis-1, an AI model that controls robots. The model weights and source code are free to download under the Apache 2.0 license, which allows commercial use. Runway first introduced Praxis-1 in late September but at first gave access only to select partners. With the release, it also published a detailed research report with new performance tests.
paragraphs.ko: AI 회사 런웨이가 로봇을 제어하는 AI 모델 프락시스-1을 공개했어요. 모델 가중치와 소스 코드는 상업적 이용을 허용하는 아파치 2.0 라이선스로 누구나 내려받을 수 있어요. 런웨이는 9월 말에 프락시스-1을 처음 소개했지만, 처음에는 일부 파트너에게만 쓰게 했어요. 이번 공개와 함께 새 성능 시험이 담긴 자세한 연구 보고서도 냈어요.

sents.en: AI company Runway has released Praxis-1, an AI model that controls robots.
sents.ko: AI 회사 런웨이가 로봇을 제어하는 AI 모델 프락시스-1을 공개했어요.

paragraphs.en: Praxis-1 takes in camera images, text instructions and information about a robot's position. From these inputs, it predicts how the scene will change and works out the right robot movements. As new camera frames arrive, the model keeps adjusting its control. Runway calls it a World Action Model, and it is built on a video model that learned how objects move from ordinary footage. This approach could reduce the need for costly datasets collected only for robots.
paragraphs.ko: 프락시스-1은 카메라 영상, 글로 된 지시, 로봇의 위치 정보를 받아들여요. 이 입력으로 장면이 어떻게 바뀔지 예측하고, 알맞은 로봇 움직임을 계산해요. 새 카메라 화면이 들어올 때마다 모델은 계속 제어를 고쳐요. 런웨이는 이를 월드 액션 모델이라 부르고, 평범한 영상에서 물체가 움직이는 법을 배운 영상 모델 위에 만들어졌어요. 이 방식은 로봇만을 위해 모은 값비싼 자료의 필요를 줄일 수 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Runway ran the tests itself, and the results have not been independently verified yet. On Nvidia's RoboLab-120 leaderboard, Praxis-1 scored a 46.2 percent success rate, ahead of FLUX 3 Action at 42.9 percent. That puts it first among World Action Models, but fifth on the overall leaderboard. On a real Franka robot arm, Praxis-1 succeeded 88 times in the ten-task test, while FLUX 3 Action succeeded 80 times. On a robot type it had never seen, the model reached an 80 percent average success rate in simulated tests. Google's RT-1 model scored 52.4 percent on the same benchmark.

paragraphs.en: The model still has limits. It sometimes confuses similar-looking objects, and it cannot yet plan complex action sequences on its own. It also still needs robot data, with about 277 hours of recordings for a Franka arm. A dual-arm robot needed between 1,400 and 2,600 hours of training material. Whether it needs less robot data overall than similar models is still an open question.

paragraphs.en: Since September, Standard Bots, Noble Machines and Ultra have tested Praxis-1 on a humanoid robot, an industrial arm and a warehouse robot. Developers can download it from Hugging Face after agreeing to the terms, and the code is on GitHub. Runway sees it mainly as a system for fast robot movements that could one day work with general AI models that break tasks into steps.

sents.ko: 런웨이는 이것을 주로 빠른 로봇 동작 시스템으로 보고, 언젠가 일을 단계로 나누는 일반 AI 모델과 함께 쓸 수 있다고 봐요.

pro.en: Runway has open-sourced Praxis-1, its robot-control model, releasing the weights and code under the Apache 2.0 license, which permits commercial use. The company unveiled the model in late September but initially limited access to selected partners, and it has now accompanied the release with a detailed research report containing fresh benchmarks.

Praxis-1 ingests camera images, text instructions and robot proprioceptive data, forecasts how the environment will evolve, and derives matching motor commands, continuously refining its control as new frames arrive. Runway describes it as a World Action Model, one built atop a video model that absorbed how objects move and interact from ordinary footage, an approach that could lessen reliance on costly robot-specific datasets.

All of the tests were run by Runway itself and have yet to be independently verified. On Nvidia's RoboLab-120 leaderboard, Praxis-1 posted a 46.2 percent success rate against 42.9 percent for FLUX 3 Action, making it the top World Action Model but only fifth overall. On a real Franka arm it succeeded 88 times in the ten-task trial to its rival's 80, and on a robot platform absent from its earlier training it averaged 80 percent in simulation, versus 52.4 percent for Google's original RT-1.

Limitations remain: the model occasionally mistakes similar-looking objects and cannot yet reliably plan complex action sequences unaided. It also still depends on specialized robot data, roughly 277 hours for the Franka arm and 1,400 to 2,600 hours for a dual-arm system, so whether it truly needs less robot data than comparable models is unresolved.

Standard Bots, Noble Machines and Ultra have been trialing Praxis-1 since September on a humanoid, an industrial arm and a dual-arm warehouse robot. Developers can obtain it from Hugging Face after accepting the access terms, with code on GitHub, and Runway envisions it chiefly as a fast-execution layer that might eventually pair with general-purpose models that decompose tasks into steps.

paragraphs.en: TechCrunch has started a running list of AI projects and startups that did not make it. Last month, the chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after it launched. A few weeks ago, the privacy-focused assistant Ollie said it would shut down. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence, about 42% of AI initiatives are in the end abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons include too little money, technical problems, competition, trouble with scaling up, and weak demand from users.

pro.en: TechCrunch has launched a running catalogue of AI products, startups and bets that have folded, pivoted or badly missed expectations. Chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy last month, only five years after its debut, and the privacy-focused assistant Ollie announced its closure a few weeks ago. S&P Global Market Intelligence estimates that roughly 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents, owing to inadequate funding, technical hurdles, competition, difficulty scaling and tepid user demand.

Industry heavyweights have not been spared. On July 9, OpenAI folded ChatGPT into a "super app" with distinct Chat, Codex and Work modes, but users complained that the interface was confusing and cluttered, and the company swiftly reversed course. It discontinued the stand-alone browser ChatGPT Atlas on August 9, absorbing its most useful features into ChatGPT, while its video-sharing platform Sora closed in March 2026 after struggling with steep operating costs and weak retention.

Apple's troubles centered on Siri: after touting a more capable assistant in 2024, it repeatedly postponed the release, a delay that fed into a $250 million settlement over the marketing of the iPhone 16's AI features, and the new Siri only surfaced in the iOS 27 beta in July. Character.ai, founded in 2021, raised $150 million at a $1 billion valuation in 2023, but later faced lawsuits from families and a cease-and-desist letter from Disney before filing for bankruptcy in early October.

Disney has now emerged as the opening bidder, offering $20 million for a license to some of the company's intellectual property, with the sale expected to conclude by late November or early December. Smaller outfits were squeezed as dominant platforms replicated their offerings: the workflow tool Relay closed in August 2026 once larger rivals embedded comparable automation, and the Humane AI Pin was wound down in February 2025 after raising $230 million, with HP acquiring most of its assets for $116 million.

TechCrunch frames the list less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of the lessons these ventures hold for the wider industry. It underscores that a splashy launch is no guarantee of a durable product, and students weighing careers in AI would do well to treat the sector as risky as well as promising. Readers can watch how the Character.ai sale ends and which closures are added next.

pro.en: Anthropic has launched Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin that gives its AI direct access to the industrial software used on factory floors. The tool connects to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft 365 and Infor through four universal interfaces, and other systems can be integrated by way of file exports to Microsoft 365.

Equipped with 17 specialized skills, the assistant can prepare quotes based on actual inventory, benchmark suppliers, and generate quality reports and design variants. During machine downtime it can also analyze sensor readings and technical manuals.

Through an additional Infor plugin, Claude can place orders with backup suppliers when deliveries slip and reschedule production, though only once a human has signed off. Every output is tied back to its source documents so that employees can review it before it is passed to customers or suppliers.

The plugin is offered to Team and Enterprise customers but does not yet operate physical machinery. To address that gap, Anthropic is separately developing the Model Hardware Standard as a research preview, which uses standardized drivers to link AI agents to equipment such as robotic arms and microscopes. Setup time shrinks from weeks or months to hours or minutes, yet human oversight remains necessary given the AI's limited grasp of physical processes.

pro.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited the Panmunjom truce village on the demilitarized zone dividing the Korean Peninsula on Friday, Oct. 30, DW reported, briefly stepping onto the North Korean side inside a barracks building.

The two Koreas have been divided since hostilities ended in 1953, with a border cutting across the peninsula. Recalling Germany's reunification 36 years earlier, Merz told reporters that he hoped Korea, too, would one day have the opportunity to regain its unity.

He remarked that the site underscored how deeply a country suffers from division and how strong the longing for reunification is, at least in the southern half of the peninsula, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience during his stay in Seoul.
DW noted that Pyongyang has retreated from diplomacy with Seoul in recent years, formally striking language on reunification from its constitution.

DW separately reported that Merz toured Japan, South Korea and Singapore, while President Frank-Walter Steinmeier traveled to Beijing to reinforce ties with China; in its assessment, the twin visits reflect Berlin's effort to reduce risks without decoupling from China.

views.view: Merz hopes for Korean reunification, while North Korea has dropped reunification language from its constitution.

paragraphs.en: The first tip is to stop writing phrases such as "think hard" or "think carefully." Anthropic says Opus 5.5 always reasons on its own and adjusts how deeply it thinks to the task and the effort level. In the company's tests, answers without these phrases started faster and were not worse. The phrases date back to the early days of reasoning models, about a year and a half ago.

pro.en: Anthropic has installed Claude Opus 5.5 as the default model across its Pro, Max, Ultra and Team subscription tiers, and has issued guidance arguing that many customers are throttling the system with prompting conventions inherited from earlier generations of AI models.

Chief among the recommendations is to abandon directives such as "think hard" or "think carefully." The company contends that Opus 5.5 reasons autonomously and calibrates the depth of its deliberation to the task and the chosen effort setting; in its own trials, responses produced without such cues began sooner with no discernible loss in quality, and the cues are a relic of reasoning models' infancy roughly eighteen months ago.

Anthropic further advises beginning at the Medium effort level, the model's default, saying it matched the previous Opus 5 running on High. Higher settings carry greater cost without guaranteed gains, and the firm urges teams that have reserved Opus for complex projects while relying on the cheaper Sonnet to reconsider, since a more capable model may complete work in fewer steps; users who routinely push Sonnet to Extra High or Max, it says, end up paying roughly what Opus 5.5 would cost.

Users are encouraged to state the objective in a single message, specifying the desired outcome, the output format and the circumstances in which the model should check back with questions, to attach charts and tables as images or files rather than transcribing them, and to request a finished document or spreadsheet outright instead of a draft. For design tasks, the company recommends naming particular unwanted styles, such as a cream-colored background or pill-shaped buttons, rather than prohibiting "generic design" in the abstract.

Anthropic asserts that Opus 5.5 interprets dense charts more accurately at its lowest effort level than Opus 5 does at its highest. Every one of these findings comes from the company's own claims and tests, and it adds that linking Claude to a user's files through connectors yields more tailored output because the model can retrieve the information it needs unaided.

issues.title: Fund managers warn that US stocks look like the dot-com bubble as AI spending grows
issues.gist: At a Korean business roundtable, an investor said US stocks are probably in a bubble like 1999 and 2000. Other fund managers warned about risks in AI-related loans.
issues.gistKo: 한국 경제 행사에서 한 투자자가 미국 주식이 1999~2000년 같은 거품 속에 있을 가능성이 크다고 말했어요. 다른 운용사 대표들은 AI 관련 대출의 위험을 경고했어요.
issues.easyKo: 미국 주식 값이 닷컴 거품 때와 비슷하게 오른 것 같다는 경고가 나왔어요. 다만 시장이 꼭 꼭대기에 닿았다는 뜻은 아니라고 해요. AI 데이터센터 대출 같은 곳의 위험도 이야기됐어요.

paragraphs.en: Owen Lamont of Acadian Asset Management said US stocks are probably in a bubble like the one in 1999 and 2000. He spoke at the seventh CIO Roundtable, which was hosted by The Korea Economic Daily on Wednesday, Nov. 11. He pointed to four warning signs: very high valuations, faster issuing of new shares, and heavy buying by retail investors. The fourth sign is continued buying even though people think the market is overvalued. He also said this does not mean the market has peaked, and valuations could stay high for years.
paragraphs.ko: 아카디안 자산운용의 오언 라몬트는 미국 주식이 1999~2000년과 같은 거품 속에 있을 가능성이 크다고 말했어요. 그는 수요일(11월 11일) 한국경제신문이 연 제7회 CIO 라운드테이블에서 발언했어요. 그는 높은 평가 가치, 빨라지는 신주 발행, 개인 투자자의 대규모 유입이라는 신호를 짚었어요. 네 번째 신호는 고평가라 믿으면서도 계속 사는 투자 행태예요. 그렇다고 시장이 정점을 찍었다는 뜻은 아니며, 높은 가치가 몇 해 이어질 수 있다고도 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: Lamont used data compiled by Yale economist Robert Shiller. The cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio for US stocks stood at 40.7 in October. That is close to the all-time high of 44.2, reached in December 1999. Lamont said the big IPO of Anthropic next week, which follows SpaceX's record-breaking market debut in June, is another sign. He expects hundreds of small IPOs after it.

paragraphs.en: Other speakers looked at the risks of AI in private credit, which means loans made outside banks. Theodore Koenig of Monroe Capital said AI spending could create new risks, especially in the financing of data centers and graphics processing units, or GPUs. He noted that loans of five to 10 years may pay for hardware that could become outdated within two or three years. Data center loans also face risks from electricity, water and possible community opposition.

pro.en: Owen Lamont, a senior portfolio manager at Acadian Asset Management, told the seventh CIO Roundtable, hosted by The Korea Economic Daily on Wednesday, Nov. 11, that US equities are probably in a speculative bubble on a par with the dot-com boom of 1999 and 2000. He cited four warning signs: stretched valuations, accelerating new share issuance, heavy retail inflows and persistent buying by investors who believe the market is overvalued, while cautioning that none of this proves the market has peaked and that elevated prices could endure for years.

Drawing on data compiled by Yale economist Robert Shiller, Lamont noted that the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio for US stocks reached 40.7 in October, approaching its record of 44.2 set in December 1999. He regarded Anthropic's blockbuster IPO next week, coming after SpaceX's record-setting market debut in June, as further evidence of a surge in equity issuance, and said he expected hundreds of small listings to follow.

Other panelists focused on the hazards AI poses to private credit, the lending that takes place outside the traditional banking system. Theodore Koenig, chairman of Monroe Capital, warned that the AI spending spree could generate fresh risks in markets, particularly in financing for data centers and graphics processing units, observing that loans maturing in five to 10 years are being used to buy hardware that may be obsolete within two or three. Data center lending, he added, carries project-specific exposure to electricity and water supply and to potential community opposition.

Ted Goldthorpe of BC Partners Credit described AI as "a durability test" for borrowers. US private credit default rates stood at 2.4% at year-end, yet including distressed borrowers granted maturity extensions or interest deferrals, Fitch Ratings estimates the figure could reach 6-8%. Stuart Wrigley of Sixth Street observed that many private equity firms acquired companies at inflated valuations and that those businesses are taking longer than anticipated to grow into them, and he expects valuation multiples to compress over the coming years.

Young Lee of Audax Private Equity said distributions as a share of net asset value slid to 4% in the first half, the lowest since 2000 and far below the long-term average of 21%, while the average holding period has lengthened to more than seven years. According to Bain & Company, the unrealized value of global buyout investments hit a record $3.8 trillion in 2025.

pro.en: The Seoul Metropolitan Government announced on Friday that it had lodged criminal complaints against five individuals who, between September 2025 and August 2026, made a combined 8,710 calls and text messages to the 119 emergency line. City officials said the persistent contacts had disrupted the operations of its emergency operations center.

The nature of the contacts varied: some callers remained silent after dialing, while others transmitted unrelated photographs or asked to be driven home while intoxicated. Between June and August alone, the five contacted 119 a combined 4,034 times; the Seoul Emergency Operations Center issued several warning texts, but the individuals went on filing the same or similar reports.

A single person accounted for 5,547 contacts over that year, placing 2,661 calls and sending 2,886 text messages. The center had examined the content, frequency and timing of communications from the 10 people who most frequently reached 119 for reasons unconnected to its services.

It then sought legal counsel from the special judicial police unit of the Seoul Metropolitan Fire and Disaster Headquarters to determine whether the conduct was deliberate and whether it constituted obstruction of official duties, and the city filed its complaints once that review was complete.

The center vowed to keep acting against conduct that impedes its work, weighing the content and frequency of the contacts, the intent behind them and their effect on emergency response. Hong Young-geun, head of the Fire and Disaster Headquarters, urged citizens to help foster responsible reporting practices so that 119 can respond swiftly in a genuine emergency.

pro.en: Business and policy leaders from South Korea and France convened in Seoul on a Friday in October to discuss artificial intelligence and industrial sustainability at the France-Korea Tech Summit 2026, the second summit of its kind, held as part of the Korea Electronics Show and organized by the French-Korean Chamber of Commerce and Industry with the Korea Electronics Association.

Speakers urged that both AI and green technology graduate from experimentation to commercial deployment, and Arthur Barichard, director of the French government's Digital and AI Council, called it highly relevant to link the AI revolution with the environmental one; representatives of KT SAT, Veolia Korea, GenesInk and Korea Electric Power Corp. also took part, covering applications from corporate decision-making and advanced materials to energy systems and industrial inspection.

Eight French and Korean companies competed in a startup pitch contest, in which the French deep-tech firm TiHive took the top prize for a terahertz-based nondestructive inspection system, South Korea's FUST Lab placed second with clean energy technology and Voltify finished third with technology in energy and semiconductors.

Held to mark the 140th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries and the 40th anniversary of the French-Korean Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the summit underscored corporate efforts to turn emerging technologies into products that can be deployed at scale, a test that will be closely watched.

pro.en: With the winter kimchi-making season approaching, an annual festival is under way at Imsil Cheese Theme Park in North Jeolla Province, where visitors can prepare kimchi from locally grown ingredients; the event is now in its 11th year.

Known as kimjang, the tradition involves producing large quantities of kimchi in late autumn or early winter in anticipation of the colder months, and families, relatives and neighbors frequently gather to make and share it.

Hosted by Imsil County and co-organized by Imsil N Seasoning Village, the festival opened at 10:30 a.m. on Friday and runs through Sunday; roughly 900 participants from 300 teams registered in advance, receive pre-salted cabbage and prepared seasonings, and take home what they make.

Singing contests, prize giveaways and food stalls serving freshly made kimchi alongside boiled pork round out the program, and a county official said the organizers hope visitors will enjoy using fresh cabbage, high-quality red peppers and carefully selected Imsil seasonings, while the festival is meant to secure stable sales and income for local farmers.

views.view: The festival gives people a chance to make kimchi and supports local farmers' sales.

issues.title: Korean broker Mirae Asset teams up with LSEG on AI wealth services
issues.gist: Mirae Asset Securities signed a deal with the London Stock Exchange Group on Nov. 13. The two firms want to improve AI wealth management and build a global investment platform.

paragraphs.en: Mirae Asset Securities, a South Korean securities firm, has teamed up with the London Stock Exchange Group, or LSEG. pro.en: Mirae Asset Securities, the South Korean brokerage, has entered a strategic tie-up with the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), with the two firms signing a memorandum of understanding on Nov. 13 to advance AI-driven wealth management and to build a global investment platform. The pact followed the first visit to Korea by David Schwimmer, chief executive of LSEG Group.

LSEG is a London-based global financial data provider whose operations stretch from data analytics and index calculation, through FTSE Russell, to risk management and exchange operations. Mirae Asset Securities intends to concentrate its collaboration on LSEG's Data & Analytics division, which is responsible for supplying financial data and linking it to AI services.

Mirae Asset Securities intends to merge its investment platform and research capabilities with LSEG's extensive global financial data. The company is pursuing a strategy known as Mirae Asset 3.0, which converges traditional assets, digital assets and AI, and it is accelerating the digital transformation of its wealth management business around its global platform, MAPS. Its ultimate objective is Agentic WM, a model in which AI actively supports every stage of a client's wealth management.

Joo Se-min, who heads the Tech & AI Division at Mirae Asset Securities, said that securing reliable data lies at the heart of competitive AI services. Ryu Hirayama, LSEG's head of Japan and Korea, commended the company's drive to adopt AI and said LSEG's data would help enhance the investment experience.

For Korean university students, the agreement signals that retail investing platforms and careers in finance are shifting toward data and artificial intelligence, so aspiring finance professionals may need fluency in both markets and technology. Observers will be watching whether the partnership yields new AI-based services for clients.

issues.title: Robust AI builds robots that work with people, not instead of them
issues.gist: Robust AI, a startup, makes a cart-like robot called Carter that helps workers in warehouses and factories. Its founders say robots should do the work that fits them while people do what they do best.
issues.gistKo: 스타트업 로버스트 AI는 창고와 공장에서 사람을 돕는 수레 모양 로봇 '카터'를 만들어요. 창업자들은 로봇과 사람이 각자 잘하는 일을 나눠 맡아야 한다고 말해요.
issues.easyKo: 사람 일자리를 빼앗는 로봇이 아니라 사람과 함께 일하는 로봇 이야기예요. 손으로 밀고 당길 수 있는 수레 로봇이 이미 창고와 공장에서 쓰이고 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Many people worry that robots will replace human workers. Robust AI, a startup, takes a different path and builds robots meant to work alongside people. Its mobile robot, Carter, looks like a utility cart on wheels. Carter has a handlebar that senses force, an AI-powered vision system, and wheels that can move in any direction at once. A worker can push or pull it with one hand, or direct it with gestures or a touch screen.
paragraphs.ko: 많은 사람이 로봇이 사람 노동자를 대신할까 봐 걱정해요. 스타트업 로버스트 AI는 다른 길을 택해 사람 곁에서 일하도록 만든 로봇을 만들어요. 이 회사의 이동 로봇 '카터'는 바퀴 달린 작업용 수레처럼 생겼어요. 카터에는 힘을 감지하는 손잡이, AI 시각 시스템, 어느 방향으로든 바로 움직이는 바퀴가 달려 있어요. 작업자는 한 손으로 밀고 당기거나 몸짓이나 터치스크린으로 로봇을 이끌 수 있어요.

paragraphs.en: The robots now work in logistics warehouses and on factory floors. They help people pick items or stock shelves, and they can also carry items across a site on their own. In one workflow, the robot guides a worker to the right spot to find an item. In another, it follows a worker to a place where goods must be loaded. The company says workers in huge warehouses or factories can walk about 30,000 steps a day on average.
paragraphs.ko: 이 로봇들은 지금 물류 창고와 공장 작업장에서 일하고 있어요. 물건을 고르거나 선반을 채우는 일을 돕고, 스스로 물건을 현장 곳곳으로 옮기기도 해요. 한 작업 방식에서는 로봇이 작업자를 물건이 있는 곳으로 안내해요. 다른 방식에서는 로봇이 작업자를 따라 짐을 실어야 할 곳으로 가요. 회사는 아주 큰 창고나 공장에서 일하는 사람이 하루 평균 약 3만 걸음을 걸을 수 있다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: The company was co-founded by Anthony Jules and Rodney Brooks, a professor emeritus at MIT. Brooks taught at MIT from 1984 until 2010 and led its computer science and AI lab, CSAIL, from 1997 until 2007. He also co-founded iRobot, which made the Roomba, and Rethink Robotics. pro.en: Despite widespread fears that robots will displace human workers, Robust AI, a startup, is building machines designed to complement them. Its mobile robot, Carter, resembles a utility cart on wheels and is equipped with a force-sensitive handlebar, an AI-powered vision system and wheels that allow instant movement in any direction. A worker can push or pull it with one hand or steer it through gestures or an onboard touch screen.

The robots are currently deployed in logistics warehouses and on factory floors, where they assist workers in picking items and stocking shelves and can also haul goods across a facility autonomously. In one workflow, the robot leads a worker to the precise spot where an item is stored; in another, it trails the worker to a location where goods need to be loaded. The company says staff in vast warehouses or factories can walk roughly 30,000 steps a day on average.

Robust AI was co-founded by Anthony Jules and Rodney Brooks, an MIT professor emeritus who served on the faculty from 1984 to 2010 and directed its Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, CSAIL, from 1997 to 2007. Brooks also co-founded iRobot, maker of the Roomba, and Rethink Robotics. The two men met in the 1990s and spoke again at a robotics conference in 2019, the year the company was founded; during the Covid-19 pandemic it first built surface-disinfecting robots before being forced to change course once more.

Jules argues that most people imagine the 5 percent of factories running fully automated systems that cost $50 million to $200 million, whereas the vast majority are not automated at all and will not scrap their operations for such an expensive overhaul, so Robust AI designs robots that can be phased in gradually. Robust AI vice president Leila Takayama found a study of hospital robots, many of which were found switched off and parked against walls; nurses called them broken, but he says they had simply halted in corridors and obstructed nurses rushing patients on gurneys.

The firm's philosophy is to understand workers' core tasks in depth and to build features that accelerate them, leaving humans to do what they do best in the physical world while digital systems handle what they do well, according to Brooks. For students, the story suggests that future robotics jobs may revolve around collaboration between people and machines rather than replacement, and observers will watch whether more factories and warehouses adopt robots that people can guide by hand.

pro.en: South Korea and Nepal have concluded a framework agreement to coordinate their efforts to curb greenhouse gas emissions and adapt to climate change, Seoul's foreign ministry announced. The pact was signed on Friday on the margins of a United Nations conference in Türkiye.

South Korea's Deputy Foreign Minister Kyun Jong-ho signed the accord alongside Maheshwor Dhakal, head of climate change management at Nepal's Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment. Kang Kum-sil, South Korea's ambassador for global climate and environment, and Rajendra Prasad Mishra, secretary of the Nepali ministry, also attended the signing.

The agreement is intended to establish a legal and institutional foundation for deeper bilateral cooperation and to bolster each country's capacity to reduce emissions and adapt to a changing climate. Seoul and Kathmandu had been pursuing the deal since 2024.

Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide trap heat in the atmosphere and warm the planet, while adaptation refers to preparing for changes already under way, such as hotter weather. For Korean students, the accord illustrates that climate policy forms part of foreign policy, and observers will watch how both governments turn the framework into joint projects.

pro.en: Yun Yuh-soon, a former executive at LG Group, has published a new book, "The Time to Awaken Half," a direct translation of its Korean title. Its message extends beyond gender equality: she contends that organizations that fail to recognize and cultivate women's potential squander half of their talent.

Yun, 71, is best known as the first woman to become an executive at LG Group. She joined LG Academy, the conglomerate's human resources development center, in 1995 at the age of 40 and was promoted to its first female executive in 2000. She subsequently served as president of the LG Arts Center and now works as a leadership coach and lecturer.

Yun writes that women account for only 20 to 30 percent of employees at many organizations, while their share of executive positions frequently remains between 3 and 5 percent. A Ministry of Gender Equality and Family report released on Sept. 29 found that women held just 7.4 percent of executive posts last year at 3,240 companies subject to mandatory business disclosures, and South Korea ranked 28th of 29 countries in The Economist's 2026 Glass Ceiling Index.

Yun questions why a country that has made such strides in education has failed to translate them into leadership opportunities for women, arguing that social expectations surrounding motherhood and children's schooling push many women to put their careers aside. She is equally critical of companies that shift the burden of change onto women and urges male leaders instead to reconsider how they identify and develop talent; the book examines unconscious bias, promotion systems, informal networks and performance evaluations.

The book draws on interviews with more than 20 executives and employees at large corporations, small and midsize businesses and startups. Yun says the urgency is mounting as companies confront artificial intelligence, a declining birthrate and intensifying competition for talent, and she describes equal opportunity as a rational business decision rather than an act of generosity. For students, the argument suggests that fair promotion practices may weigh in choosing an employer, and observers will watch whether Korean firms change how they elevate women.

issues.title: Korea's "Hyunbaek-core" trend shows a fascination with rich-looking lives
issues.gist: A fashion trend called "Hyunbaek-core" copies the look of a rich young woman at a department store. A Korea Herald report links it to weaker faith in social mobility.
issues.gistKo: 「현백코어」라는 패션 유행이 백화점에 가는 부유한 젊은 여성의 모습을 따라 해요. 코리아헤럴드는 이를 사회 이동에 대한 믿음이 약해진 흐름과 연결해 보도했어요.

paragraphs.en: A fashion trend called "Hyunbaek-core" is spreading on Korean social media. It is based on the image of a rich young woman shopping at Hyundai Department Store in clothes that look simple but expensive. The style uses well-cut basics, small accessories and quiet luxury labels.
paragraphs.ko: 「현백코어」라는 패션 유행이 한국 소셜 미디어에서 퍼지고 있어요. 부유한 젊은 여성이 단순해 보이지만 비싼 옷을 입고 현대백화점에서 쇼핑하는 모습에서 나온 유행이에요. 옷은 잘 재단된 기본 아이템에 작은 액세서리와 티 나지 않는 명품 상표로 꾸며요.

Ha Yu-rim, a 22-year-old college student, said that dressing this way makes her feel stylish, even without money for luxury goods. Another student, Lim Soo-young, said she envies the freedom to try something new without checking the price first. The interest in wealth goes beyond clothes and is not limited to fashion trends.

paragraphs.en: The trend appears at a time of weaker faith in social mobility. A survey of 3,000 adults in 2025 by the Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs was released in June. pro.en: A social-media fashion phenomenon dubbed "Hyunbaek-core" is gaining traction in South Korea, drawing on the image of an affluent young woman browsing Hyundai Department Store in outfits that appear simple yet costly. The look relies on well-cut basics, subtle accessories and discreet luxury labels.

Some Instagram users have labelled the style the "Go Youn-jung look." Ha Yu-rim, a 22-year-old university student, said that dressing this way made her look stylish even though she could not afford luxury goods, while fellow student Lim Soo-young said she coveted the freedom to try something new without first weighing the price. The fascination with wealth also extends beyond fashion, and is not limited to fashion trends.

The vogue emerges as confidence in social mobility erodes. A 2025 survey of 3,000 adults conducted by the Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs, published in June, found that only about one in four respondents regarded mobility in South Korea as dynamic, and among those who considered it constrained, 43.4 percent cited the influence of parents' wealth and social background. Even so, 42.5 percent rated the likelihood of improving one's standing through personal effort as high, and 50.7 percent as moderate.

Two academics offered their assessments to The Korea Herald. Lee Eun-hee of Inha University characterised the trend as an extension of status-conscious consumption that began with handbags and now encompasses entire outfits, whereas Heo Chang-deog of Yeungnam University tied it to a desire for recognition and acceptance, noting that the pace at which trends travel in Korea encourages swift imitation of celebrities.

The report also underscores the distance between aspiration and everyday reality. Lim said that even when she mimics the trend, she must still weigh spending against saving for her future, and Lee questioned whether consumers are exercising their own taste or merely pursuing widely admired notions of success.

views.view: The trend shows a wish for status and approval, and it appears while many people doubt that social mobility is active.

pro.en: A coalition of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won a sweeping victory in the Malaysian state of Melaka's election on Saturday, Nov. 14, capturing 24 of the 28 seats and a two-thirds majority in the legislature, up from the 23 seats the two blocs had won separately in 2021.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's Pakatan Harapan (PH) took four seats, one fewer than five years earlier, while the parties Bersatu and Bersama lost every seat they contested. PH's candidate for chief minister, Adly Zahari, was also unseated in his own constituency of Bukit Katil by a PN rival.

The Election Commission confirmed that BN had secured the 15 seats required to form a government by 10 p.m., and the alliance nominated the incumbent chief minister, Ab Rauf Yusoh, for a second term. BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi described the outcome as a continuing "blue wave" that had started in Johor and carried through Negeri Sembilan.

The Singapore-based outlet CNA reported that the outcome could revive doubts over Anwar's ability to halt eroding support among Malay voters, and might embolden BN and PN leaders to push for an early general election, which must be held by February 2028. Friction between PH and BN, partners in the federal government, had been sharpened by the decision to place former prime minister Najib Razak under house arrest.

One day before the vote, the pollster ILHAM Centre had identified 24 seats in which the alliance held a commanding lead, and BN and PN had split the contests, with BN fielding candidates in 23 seats and PN in five, to avoid dividing the Malay vote. For Korean readers, the episode illustrates how electoral pacts can reshape outcomes; the next steps are Ab Rauf's formal appointment and whether calls for an early national poll gather force.

views.view: The result could raise questions about Anwar's hold on Malay voters and may push BN and PN leaders to call for an early election.

pro.en: NASA has announced that Voyager 1 is about to become the first human-made object to cover a distance of one light-day from Earth. On Wednesday, the probe will have travelled at least 16 billion miles since its 1977 launch, the distance light covers in 24 hours.

Voyager 1 completed its Saturn flyby in 1980 and is now moving at roughly 36,000 miles per hour through interstellar space, the vast expanse between stars. NASA projects that it will take 18,000 years to cross a full light-year.

Voyager 2, launched shortly after its twin, is expected to reach the one light-day mark in 2035. Both craft continue to relay data to Earth daily, including measurements of magnetic field strength and direction, pressure, dust and galactic cosmic rays.
A skeleton crew of NASA engineers transmits commands about once a week. In October, controllers briefly lost contact with Voyager 1, and they have yet to determine the cause.
Project manager Suzanne Dodd described Voyager 1 as "a national treasure," and the probe also captured the celebrated "Pale Blue Dot" image of Earth in 1990.

views.view: The probe's long journey is a proud record, and its team calls it a national treasure that still sends useful data.

issues.title: Sudan's Army Gains Ground in Kordofan in the War Against the RSF
issues.gist: Sudan's army has taken several towns and villages in West Kordofan this week. Analysts say the fight against the RSF is turning in the army's favour.
issues.gistKo: 수단 정부군이 이번 주 서코르도판의 여러 마을과 지역을 차지했어요. 분석가들은 RSF와의 싸움이 정부군에게 유리하게 바뀌고 있다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: The Sudanese Armed Forces, or SAF, took control of several important villages and localities in West Kordofan this week. On Friday, the army took al-Khuwai, one of the main towns in West Kordofan, according to local media. The campaign began several weeks ago. The SAF and allied Darfur forces have already broken the RSF siege of al-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan.

pro.en: Sudan's armed forces seized a string of strategically significant villages and localities in West Kordofan this week, according to Al Jazeera. On Friday the army captured al-Khuwai, one of the state's main towns, local media reported, in a campaign that opened several weeks ago and has already allowed the army and allied Darfur forces to break the Rapid Support Forces' siege of al-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan.

The region is rich in agricultural products such as sesame seeds, groundnuts and gum arabic, and in gold and oil. The Heglig and Balila fields in West Kordofan account for 90% of Sudan's oil output, and Mohamed al-Nayer, a professor of economics, noted that South Sudan's crude exports likewise depend on transit through Sudanese territory to Bashayer Port.

Mohamed Ali, an independent analyst, argued that the RSF's pivot from offence to defence will alter a force that was built on rapidly mobilising tribal backing, adding that Kordofan is not a social stronghold for it and that a withdrawal toward Darfur is likely, which could turn Darfur into the new epicentre of the conflict. He also cited the army's growing air superiority and extensive use of drones.

The war erupted in April 2023 from a power struggle between General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti. Roughly 150,000 people have been killed and more than 14 million of Sudan's 53 million inhabitants displaced. The United Nations describes Kordofan as the conflict's epicentre, most humanitarian operations there have stalled, and aid driver Omer Yousif said deliveries could improve if the army's offensive succeeds.

The RSF nevertheless retains al-Nuhud and parts of South Kordofan and consolidates control across all five Darfur states, including el-Fasher, which fell to it in October 2025. The question now is whether the fighting shifts toward Darfur and whether aid can reach civilians in Kordofan.

views.view: Analysts say the army's gains in Kordofan are shifting the war in its favour, while civilians still suffer badly.

issues.title: FAA Expands an AI Tool to Help Manage Air Traffic Across the US
issues.gist: The US air safety agency is expanding an AI tool that advises air traffic controllers to the whole country. Airlines support it, but the controllers' union says it was not involved.
issues.gistKo: 미국 연방항공청이 항공 관제사를 돕는 AI 도구를 전국으로 넓혀요. 항공사들은 환영하지만 관제사 노조는 개발에 참여하지 않았다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: The US government has expanded an AI tool that advises air traffic controllers so that it now covers the whole national airspace system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since September 21. That was the day it began over Washington, DC. The agency claims the average saving was 10 minutes and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight. In a statement posted on November 10, it said SMART will now be used in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country.

A human team of FAA specialists in Washington validates the recommendations before they go to air traffic control facilities. The FAA says SMART cannot replace controllers or take over control of an aircraft, and local controllers can decide whether to accept its advice.

pro.en: The US government has widened the use of an artificial intelligence tool that advises air traffic controllers so that it now spans the entire national airspace system. The Federal Aviation Administration says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since it went live over Washington, DC, on September 21, saving an average of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight, and a statement posted on November 10 said it will now operate in the airspace of all 22 centers nationwide.

The agency's fact sheet characterises SMART as a cloud-based platform that predicts traffic patterns by drawing on weather, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics, with the aim of recommending schedules, identifying optimal routes and sequencing arrivals. A human team of FAA specialists in Washington validates its output before it reaches air traffic facilities, and the FAA stresses that the system cannot replace controllers or assume control of an aircraft, leaving local controllers free to accept or decline its advice.

Airline executives have endorsed the rollout, and the September announcement carried supportive statements from Delta chief executive Ed Bastian and American Airlines chief executive Robert Isom. The National Air Traffic Controllers Association, which represents more than 15,000 members, nonetheless told Flying magazine that it was not consulted on, or involved in, the design, testing or implementation of SMART and therefore cannot comment on its effect on the workforce.

Following the initial deployment above Washington, the FAA extended coverage to the centers in Atlanta, Jacksonville and Miami, The Dallas Morning News reported. The agency offered that paper an instance in which SMART proposed a shorter, faster route for a cargo flight bound for Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, though the newspaper noted that the flight was not identified and no information was supplied on the tool's effect on passenger traffic. The open question is whether the results seen in Washington can be replicated nationwide.

pro.en: The European Union has called on Israel to reopen all Gaza border crossings and grant aid organisations "immediate, unimpeded access" following devastating flooding in the territory this week. In a statement issued on Saturday by the office of Kaja Kallas, the EU's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and a vice-president of the European Commission, the bloc said civilian infrastructure and medical facilities in Gaza "must be protected."

Heavy rain has submerged large areas of the enclave, and local officials and the UN say damage from Israeli attacks on infrastructure has aggravated the flooding. Gaza's media office reported that more than 700km of the sewage network has been destroyed, and UNICEF said the rain had directly affected at least 106,000 people in recent days, with thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians submerged and latrines overflowing into camps.

The EU said Israel must enable the work of the UN and its agencies as well as humanitarian organisations, NGOs included, and comply with its obligations under international law, including humanitarian law. It described the recent airstrike on Nasser Hospital as "deeply alarming"; an Israeli air attack on the Nasser Medical Complex on Thursday had killed at least six Palestinians, among them a surgeon.

Separately, an Israeli drone strike on Saturday killed two more Palestinians in Jabaliya, according to the director of Shifa Hospital, while the Israeli military said it had struck two Hamas militants in the area.

The EU reaffirmed its commitment to a two-state solution and demanded the full withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza, together with sustained delivery of humanitarian assistance and early recovery support at scale. What remains to be seen is whether the crossings reopen and aid groups can reach the flooded areas.

pro.en: South Korea is bracing for its annual college entrance examination, the Suneung, and forecasters now say Seoul could see its first subzero exam morning in six years. The Korea Meteorological Administration projects that temperatures will sink to minus 1 degree Celsius on Thursday.

Should the forecast hold, it would be the first sub-freezing Suneung morning in the capital since 2020, when the test was pushed back to December because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The last time temperatures fell below freezing for a November sitting was 2019.

The chill is set to arrive on the heels of several days of rain. Wet weather is forecast nationwide from Friday through Sunday morning, with another round on Tuesday and Wednesday, before cold air sweeping in from the northwest drives temperatures sharply lower. Seoul's morning lows are projected to slide from 8 C on Tuesday to 4 C on Wednesday and minus 1 C on Thursday.

Strong winds and rough seas are expected in waters around the peninsula on Tuesday and Wednesday, potentially disrupting ferry services, and students traveling from islands to sit the exam are advised to check transport schedules ahead of time. The weather agency cautioned that the forecast remains subject to change and said it would hold another briefing on exam-day conditions on Tuesday.

pro.en: Samsung Medison, a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, inaugurated a new manufacturing building at its Hongcheon complex in Gangwon Province on Friday. The ultrasound maker said the 50 billion won ($37.4 million) investment is aimed at vaulting it into the ranks of the world's top three manufacturers.

The project marks the company's most sizable production-facility expansion since it joined Samsung in 2011. The two-story structure spans 14,548 square meters and forms part of a blueprint to lift annual ultrasound output from roughly 24,000 units this year to as many as 40,000 by 2030.

The most consequential change is the consolidation under one roof of processes previously scattered across several buildings, linking circuit board fabrication, assembly, testing, packaging and storage in a single production flow. Eight high-speed machines mount components as minuscule as 0.1 to 0.2 millimeters onto boards, and each scanner contains 15,000 to 20,000 such parts. Boards are then subjected to 48 hours of testing at 40 degrees Celsius, and fully assembled scanners undergo a further 24 hours.

Samsung Medison contends that its sales are outpacing the broader market: revenue climbed 16.2 percent last year against 3.7 percent growth for the global ultrasound equipment sector, and it anticipates double-digit growth again in 2026. Chief Executive Yoo Kyu-tae said the company is now within reach of cracking the top three.

Existing equipment can already sustain roughly 27,000 to 28,000 scanners annually, and the company intends to add machinery incrementally as demand rises, including robots and uncrewed transport systems. It is also broadening its AI-powered diagnostic software and probing new clinical areas.

views.view: The paper describes the new plant as a step that helps the company push toward the top three, citing automation and faster-than-market sales growth.

pro.en: President Lee Jae Myung will hold bilateral talks with his Thai and Philippine counterparts next week, his spokesperson said Friday. The meetings will take place on the margins of a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, and Lee is also scheduled to attend a regional meeting in China during the same trip.

Spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said Lee is due to attend the ASEAN summit in Manila on Monday and Tuesday before traveling to Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday for a two-day trip to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

On Monday afternoon, Lee will meet separately with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr., with both sessions arranged on the sidelines of the ASEAN gathering.

On the sidelines of the APEC summit on Wednesday, he will also host a luncheon with South Korean residents in southern China, home to some 24,000 South Korean nationals, Kang said, in a gathering that will bring the president together with compatriots living abroad.

issues.title: Little-known journals publish AI-made papers under famous professors' names
issues.gist: An investigation found small academic journals publishing low-quality AI papers under the names of professors who did not write them. Some of the named professors, including Stanford's Jure Leskovec, say they never agreed to this.
issues.gistKo: 한 조사에서 이름이 덜 알려진 학술지들이 교수들이 쓰지 않은 저질 AI 논문을 교수들의 이름으로 싣고 있다는 사실이 드러났어요. 스탠퍼드대 유레 레스코벡을 포함해 이름이 오른 교수들은 동의한 적이 없다고 말해요.
issues.easyKo: 어떤 학술지들이 유명한 교수의 이름을 멋대로 붙여 AI가 만든 듯한 논문을 올리고 있었어요. 이름이 오른 교수들은 논문을 쓰지도, 허락하지도 않았다고 해요. 대학원생이 이런 학술지를 믿고 논문을 낼까 봐 걱정하고 있어요.

paragraphs.en: An investigation found that little-known academic journals are publishing poor AI-made papers under the names of professors who never wrote them. Many academics worry that their real names are being misused.

pro.en: An investigation has found that a cluster of obscure academic journals has been publishing AI-generated papers of poor quality under the names of professors who never wrote them. Scholars fear that their identities are being appropriated.

The trail began when Alan Said, a professor of computer science at the University of Gothenburg, received a Google Scholar notification about a paper published under his name in the American International Journal of Research and Innovation, known as AIJRI. The article, titled "Intelligence Systems Supporting Sustainable Global Development," bore a loose connection to his research on artificial intelligence and sustainability, but he had not written it. He said its citations and content appeared machine-generated and amounted to "slop." When he reported the matter to the journal's domain registrar, he was told the article had been taken down. The paper nonetheless remained online under another person's name, and two days later the byline changed again, leaving three versions attributed to different authors.

Said also identified two similar titles, AJAMRI and AJFMR, which share comparable graphics, the same editor in chief and the same board members. AJAMRI has carried dozens of papers credited to prominent academics, among them the Stanford computer scientists Fei-Fei Li and Christopher Manning and the Berkeley professors Michael I. Jordan and Stuart Russell. All three domain names were registered in 2026, yet the sites display archives of papers purportedly published several years earlier. The journals describe themselves as peer-reviewed and open access while advertising publication fees. AIJRI and AJAMRI said they charge $200 for papers with five or more non-Indian authors, whereas AJFMR charges $80 for one to four authors and $10 for five or more.

Several academics named in the journals confirmed that they had neither written the papers nor consented to being listed. Jure Leskovec, a professor of computer science at Stanford University, said he had not written his paper or authorized the use of his name, calling the situation quite concerning. Said voiced worry that a new Ph.D. student who sees his name there might conclude it is acceptable to submit work to such outlets. Kanakaraju Manupati, a postdoctoral fellow at Virginia Commonwealth University, appeared on an editorial board but said he had never agreed to serve.

All three journals identify Denish Brown as editor in chief and list a WhatsApp number with a U.S. area code. Times Higher Education contacted the journals but received no response before publication. For students, the case underscores the need to verify where a paper is published before relying on it or submitting work there.

issues.title: A Picture Book Helped a Student With Autism, but Seoul Has Too Few Specialist Teachers
issues.gist: A Seoul teacher made an AI picture book that helped a student with autism change her behavior in a few months. Experts say schools need more specialist teachers and clear laws.
issues.gistKo: 서울의 한 교사가 AI로 만든 그림책이 자폐 스펙트럼 학생의 행동을 몇 달 만에 바꿨어요. 전문가들은 학교마다 전문 교사와 분명한 법적 근거가 필요하다고 말해요.
issues.easyKo: 한 초등 교사가 학생이 주인공인 그림책을 만들어 읽어 주자 아이의 행동이 좋아졌어요. 하지만 이런 전문 교사는 서울에 아주 적어서 법과 제도가 필요하다는 목소리가 나와요.

paragraphs.en: At a job interview this year, Jang Se-ra held a well-worn picture book. She is an elementary school teacher with 23 years of experience, and she was applying to be a behavioral intervention specialist teacher at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education. She had made the book herself about a 13-year-old student with the pseudonym Ji-woo, who has autism spectrum disorder. Ji-woo used to shout, sit down on the hallway floor and cry, and she also threw objects and overturned desks.
paragraphs.ko: 올해 면접 자리에서 장세라 교사는 낡은 그림책 한 권을 들고 있었어요. 그녀는 경력 23년의 초등 교사로, 서울시교육청의 행동 중재 전문 교사에 지원하고 있었어요. 그 책은 가명이 지우인 13세 학생, 자폐 스펙트럼 장애가 있는 아이를 주인공으로 직접 만든 거예요. 지우는 소리를 지르고 복도 바닥에 주저앉아 울곤 했고, 물건을 던지고 책상을 엎기도 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Jang asked for help from Kim Sun-woong, a behavioral intervention specialist teacher at the same school. Kim suggested using social stories, which use pictures to explain everyday situations and how to respond to them. Using artificial intelligence, Jang made a picture book with Ji-woo as the main character, showing six or seven situations such as eating in the cafeteria and riding in an elevator. Ji-woo tore up the book at first, but she soon became curious and asked adults to read it to her. Within two to three months her challenging behaviors decreased, and by graduation in December she could eat meals with her classmates.

pro.en: At an interview this year for a post as a behavioral intervention specialist teacher with the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, Jang Se-ra, a veteran elementary school teacher of 23 years, brought a well-worn picture book that she had created herself. Its protagonist was a 13-year-old student with autism spectrum disorder, identified by the pseudonym Ji-woo, who had been prone to shouting, sitting down on the hallway floor and crying, and who also threw objects and overturned desks.

Jang turned for help to Kim Sun-woong, a behavioral intervention specialist teacher at the same school, who proposed social stories, an approach that uses illustrations to explain everyday situations and appropriate ways of responding. Using artificial intelligence, Jang produced a picture book starring Ji-woo that depicted six or seven recurring difficulties, such as eating in the cafeteria and riding in an elevator. Ji-woo tore up the book at first, but her curiosity grew and she began asking adults to read it aloud; within two to three months her challenging behaviors had diminished, and by her December graduation she was able to eat alongside classmates.

Jang was selected as one of 10 candidates for the third cohort of such specialists and now works at Seongseo Elementary School in Seoul, where she has been in training since March. She aims to establish a schoolwide positive behavior support system during her five years there. Critics note, however, that because the arrangement is an education office initiative rather than an established program, it relies heavily on the enthusiasm and dedication of individual teachers.

An analysis by the Good Teachers Movement, a teachers' organization, of health insurance data found that 280,270 children and adolescents aged 5 to 19 received treatment for ADHD or depression last year, an increase of roughly 16.4 percent. The first cohort of specialist teachers in 2024 numbered 10, but the second was cut to five, and even with the latest recruits the total will reach just 40, against 2,092 schools in Seoul.

Rep. Kang Kyung-sook of the Rebuilding Korea Party introduced an amendment in September that would provide a legal basis for assigning such teachers to mainstream schools. Kim Ye-ri, of the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, said there were limits to what a handful of dedicated individuals could achieve and that legal and institutional support was essential to a sustainable schoolwide system. The question now is whether the amendment passes and how many specialists ultimately reach classrooms.

pro.en: Seoul Metro Line 9 Corporation announced on Friday, Nov. 13, that train timetables on Seoul Subway Line No. 9, a route notorious for severe overcrowding, would be revised from Monday to ease congestion, and it urged passengers to consult the updated schedules in advance.

During the morning rush from 5:40 to 7 a.m., trains bound for VHS Medical Center will run in a revised sequence of two express services followed by one all-stop service, replacing the current alternating pattern of one express and one all-stop train. Headways will also be trimmed by up to 20 seconds so that the frequency of all-stop services stays at roughly its present level.

In the evening, the window of concentrated service will be brought forward by 30 minutes, from 4:30 to 7 p.m. to 4 to 6:30 p.m. Express trains bypass some stations whereas all-stop trains call at every station, and the report did not indicate how many riders would be affected.
Commuters who use Line 9 would be well advised to check the new timetable before Monday. The key question is whether the revised pattern genuinely reduces rush-hour crowding.

views.view: KBS World reports the plan plainly: new patterns to ease crowding, with passengers urged to check timetables.

issues.title: Eurovision Asia Holds Its First Song Contest in Thailand
issues.gist: The first Eurovision Asia song contest takes place in Thailand on Saturday with 11 countries. Malaysia and the Philippines are seen as favorites.

pro.en: The inaugural Eurovision Asia song contest takes place in Thailand on Saturday, a more compact affair than its European counterpart, with only 11 countries taking part and the show staged at One Bangkok Forum.

A Guardian writer observes that the entries are tamer than the European contest's, and that restrictive attitudes toward homosexuality in some of the countries broadcasting the show have muted the LGBTQ+ presence long associated with Eurovision; nearly half the songs still rely on English lyrics.

Malaysia's Aina Abdul is the favorite among fans and bookmakers, and her power ballad Bluest Sky has been handed the closing slot in the running order. The Philippines' Carmelle, with Sobra-Sobra, a feminist anthem blending pop and rap, is considered another frontrunner, while Mongolia's Beck was forced to change songs because the national-final winner had already been released.

Woody Milintachinda and Cindy Bishop host the show, and Dara, the 2026 Eurovision winner, will headline the interval act. Broadcasts run on SBS in Australia and on Eurovision's YouTube channel in Europe at 13.30 GMT.

views.view: The writer expects fewer wild acts than in Europe and names Malaysia and the Philippines as favorites.
