issues.title: Busan Mayor Visits London to Learn How to Build a Maritime Law and Finance Hub
issues.gist: Busan's mayor went to London to meet maritime arbitration, shipping, and court officials. Busan wants to grow from a port city into a place that also sells legal, finance, and insurance services for shipping.
issues.gistKo: 부산시장이 런던에서 해사 중재, 해운, 법원 관계자를 만났어요. 부산은 항만 도시에서 해운을 돕는 법률·금융·보험 서비스까지 하는 도시로 크고 싶어 해요.
issues.easyKo: 부산시장이 영국 런던의 해운 관련 기관 세 곳을 찾았어요. 2028년 3월 문을 여는 부산 해사 국제상사법원을 앞두고 런던의 경험을 배우려는 거예요. 배와 항구만 다루던 도시가 법률과 금융 서비스까지 키우려는 계획이에요.

paragraphs.en: Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo visited London on Nov. 12 local time. He met officials from three groups: the London Maritime Arbitrators Association, the UK Chamber of Shipping, and the Admiralty Court. The talks were about maritime arbitration, the shipping industry, and how special courts work.
paragraphs.ko: 전재수 부산시장이 현지 시각 11월 12일 런던을 방문했어요. 그는 런던해사중재인협회, 영국해운회의소, 해사법원(Admiralty Court)의 관계자를 만났어요. 이야기의 주제는 해사 중재, 해운 산업, 전문 법원의 운영이었어요.

sents.en: Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo visited London on Nov. 12 local time.
sents.ko: 전재수 부산시장이 현지 시각 11월 12일 런던을 방문했어요.

sents.en: He met officials from three groups: the London Maritime Arbitrators Association, the UK Chamber of Shipping, and the Admiralty Court.
sents.ko: 그는 런던해사중재인협회, 영국해운회의소, 해사법원(Admiralty Court)의 관계자를 만났어요.

sents.en: The talks were about maritime arbitration, the shipping industry, and how special courts work.
sents.ko: 이야기의 주제는 해사 중재, 해운 산업, 전문 법원의 운영이었어요.

paragraphs.en: Busan's government said on Nov. 13 that the mayor wants to widen the city's sea business. Today it is built mostly around ports and logistics. The city now hopes to add expert services such as legal work, arbitration, finance, and insurance. It plans to open the Busan Maritime International Commercial Court in March 2028, and it wants to learn from London before then.
paragraphs.ko: 부산시는 11월 13일 시장이 도시의 바다 관련 산업을 넓히고 싶어 한다고 밝혔어요. 지금은 항만과 물류가 중심이에요. 부산은 이제 법률, 중재, 금융, 보험 같은 전문 서비스를 더하고 싶어 해요. 부산시는 2028년 3월 부산 해사 국제상사법원을 열 계획이고, 그전에 런던에서 배우고 싶어 해요.

sents.en: Busan's government said on Nov. 13 that the mayor wants to widen the city's sea business.
sents.ko: 부산시는 11월 13일 시장이 도시의 바다 관련 산업을 넓히고 싶어 한다고 밝혔어요.

sents.en: Today it is built mostly around ports and logistics.
sents.ko: 지금은 항만과 물류가 중심이에요.

sents.en: The city now hopes to add expert services such as legal work, arbitration, finance, and insurance.
sents.ko: 부산은 이제 법률, 중재, 금융, 보험 같은 전문 서비스를 더하고 싶어 해요.

sents.en: It plans to open the Busan Maritime International Commercial Court in March 2028, and it wants to learn from London before then.
sents.ko: 부산시는 2028년 3월 부산 해사 국제상사법원을 열 계획이고, 그전에 런던에서 배우고 싶어 해요.

paragraphs.en: Busan was interested in how London combines shipping with law, finance, and insurance firms. The city noted that shipping companies, arbitration bodies, special courts, and professional firms all sit together there. Together they form a separate service market that supports shipping. At the arbitrators' association, founded in 1960, Chun spoke with president Jonathan Ehle about wider cooperation. Busan suggested international conferences, memorandums of understanding, and mock arbitration programs.
paragraphs.ko: 부산은 런던이 해운을 법률, 금융, 보험 회사와 어떻게 묶어 두었는지에 관심을 보였어요. 부산시는 그곳에 해운 회사, 중재 기관, 전문 법원, 전문 회사가 모두 함께 있다고 짚었어요. 이들이 합쳐져 해운을 받치는 별도의 서비스 시장을 이뤄요. 1960년에 세워진 중재인협회에서 전 시장은 조너선 에일 회장과 협력 확대를 이야기했어요. 부산은 국제 회의, 양해각서, 모의 중재 프로그램을 제안했어요.

sents.en: Busan was interested in how London combines shipping with law, finance, and insurance firms.
sents.ko: 부산은 런던이 해운을 법률, 금융, 보험 회사와 어떻게 묶어 두었는지에 관심을 보였어요.

sents.en: The city noted that shipping companies, arbitration bodies, special courts, and professional firms all sit together there.
sents.ko: 부산시는 그곳에 해운 회사, 중재 기관, 전문 법원, 전문 회사가 모두 함께 있다고 짚었어요.

sents.en: Together they form a separate service market that supports shipping.
sents.ko: 이들이 합쳐져 해운을 받치는 별도의 서비스 시장을 이뤄요.

sents.en: At the arbitrators' association, founded in 1960, Chun spoke with president Jonathan Ehle about wider cooperation.
sents.ko: 1960년에 세워진 중재인협회에서 전 시장은 조너선 에일 회장과 협력 확대를 이야기했어요.

sents.en: Busan suggested international conferences, memorandums of understanding, and mock arbitration programs.
sents.ko: 부산은 국제 회의, 양해각서, 모의 중재 프로그램을 제안했어요.

paragraphs.en: At the UK Chamber of Shipping, the talks covered green and digital change and the need for skilled workers. Chun met president Karin Orsel and chief executive Rhett Hatcher. He raised cooperation on eco-friendly ship fuel, digital ship management, and ship maintenance. He also proposed internships linking local universities with British shipping companies.
paragraphs.ko: 영국해운회의소에서는 친환경·디지털 전환과 전문 인력 확보를 이야기했어요. 전 시장은 카린 오르셀 회장과 렛 해처 대표를 만났어요. 그는 친환경 선박 연료, 디지털 선박 관리, 선박 정비에서의 협력을 꺼냈어요. 또 지역 대학과 영국 해운 회사를 잇는 인턴십도 제안했어요.

sents.en: At the UK Chamber of Shipping, the talks covered green and digital change and the need for skilled workers.
sents.ko: 영국해운회의소에서는 친환경·디지털 전환과 전문 인력 확보를 이야기했어요.

sents.en: Chun met president Karin Orsel and chief executive Rhett Hatcher.
sents.ko: 전 시장은 카린 오르셀 회장과 렛 해처 대표를 만났어요.

sents.en: He raised cooperation on eco-friendly ship fuel, digital ship management, and ship maintenance.

sents.en: He also proposed internships linking local universities with British shipping companies.
sents.ko: 또 지역 대학과 영국 해운 회사를 잇는 인턴십도 제안했어요.

paragraphs.en: At the Admiralty Court, Chun reviewed how a specialist maritime court runs. The court handles disputes such as ship collisions, marine salvage, and cargo transport. Busan plans joint seminars, exchanges of precedents, and academic research with the UK side. Chun said London grew into a maritime hub because shipping, arbitration, legal, financial, and insurance services are closely linked. He said Busan will work hard to foster specialist personnel.
paragraphs.ko: 해사법원에서 전 시장은 전문 해사 법원이 어떻게 운영되는지 살펴봤어요. 이 법원은 선박 충돌, 해난 구조, 화물 운송 같은 분쟁을 다뤄요. 부산은 영국 쪽과 공동 세미나, 판례 교류, 학술 연구를 할 계획이에요. 전 시장은 런던이 해운, 중재, 법률, 금융, 보험 서비스가 긴밀히 이어져 해운 중심지로 컸다고 말했어요. 그는 부산이 전문 인력을 키우는 데 힘쓰겠다고 말했어요.

sents.en: At the Admiralty Court, Chun reviewed how a specialist maritime court runs.

sents.en: The court handles disputes such as ship collisions, marine salvage, and cargo transport.

sents.en: Busan plans joint seminars, exchanges of precedents, and academic research with the UK side.

sents.en: Chun said London grew into a maritime hub because shipping, arbitration, legal, financial, and insurance services are closely linked.

sents.en: He said Busan will work hard to foster specialist personnel.
sents.ko: 그는 부산이 전문 인력을 키우는 데 힘쓰겠다고 말했어요.

pro.en: Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo traveled to London on Nov. 12 local time to confer with officials from three institutions, among them the London Maritime Arbitrators Association. The others were the UK Chamber of Shipping and the Admiralty Court, with discussions covering maritime arbitration, the shipping industry and the operation of specialist courts.

According to the Busan Metropolitan City government on Nov. 13, Chun is seeking to broaden a marine economy long anchored in ports and logistics into specialized services such as legal work, arbitration, finance and insurance. Ahead of the planned March 2028 opening of the Busan Maritime International Commercial Court, the city hopes to draw on London's experience in resolving international maritime disputes.

What caught Busan's attention was London's industrial structure, in which shipping and port infrastructure coexist with legal, financial and insurance firms, arbitration bodies and specialist courts, forming a distinct service market that underpins the shipping trade. At the arbitrators' association, founded in 1960, Chun discussed deeper cooperation with president Jonathan Ehle and proposed international conferences, memorandums of understanding and mock arbitration programs.

Talks at the UK Chamber of Shipping, with president Karin Orsel and chief executive Rhett Hatcher, centered on the sector's green and digital transition and the challenge of securing specialist personnel. Chun called for bilateral cooperation on eco-friendly ship fuel, digital ship management and vessel maintenance, and floated internships linking local universities with British shipping companies.

At the Admiralty Court, which handles disputes arising from ship collisions, marine salvage and cargo transport, Chun examined how a specialist maritime court operates. Busan intends to draw on British experience through joint seminars, exchanges of precedents and academic research, and Chun credited London's rise to an ecosystem linking shipping with arbitration, legal, financial and insurance services, vowing to foster specialist personnel.

views.view: Busan wants to grow from a port and logistics city into a hub for maritime law, arbitration, finance, and insurance, learning from London.

pro.en: Rain across most of South Korea is forecast to taper off from late Saturday, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration, which expects it to begin easing that night in Seoul, Incheon, northern Gyeonggi Province, South Chungcheong Province and North Jeolla Province.

Showers are expected to linger elsewhere, however, persisting until Sunday morning on Jeju, the southernmost island, and until Monday in Gangwon Province on the east coast and in the Gyeongsang provinces in the southeast.

Accumulations of up to ten millimeters are forecast for Seoul, Incheon and Gangwon Province, up to 20 millimeters for northern Gyeonggi Province, up to 30 millimeters across the Chungcheong, Jeolla and Gyeongsang regions, and as much as 50 millimeters on Jeju Island.

Sunday morning lows are projected between seven and 13 degrees Celsius, with daytime highs of 16 to 21 degrees. Temperatures are expected to slide in the latter half of next week, with the mercury dropping below freezing on Thursday morning, when the national university entrance exams are scheduled to be held.

issues.title: Anthropic's CEO Admits Big Uncertainty Days Before Its Record IPO
issues.gist: Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei said buying computing power is his company's hardest business choice. He spoke days before the company's planned Nov. 19 IPO.
issues.gistKo: 앤트로픽의 다리오 아모데이 CEO는 컴퓨팅 자원을 사는 일이 회사의 가장 어려운 사업 결정이라고 말했어요. 11월 19일로 예정된 기업공개(IPO)를 며칠 앞둔 때였어요.
issues.easyKo: 앤트로픽은 AI를 돌리는 컴퓨팅 자원을 1~2년 앞서 사야 해요. 그때는 돈이 얼마나 벌릴지 아무도 몰라요. CEO는 이 불확실함을 인정하면서, IPO로 모은 현금이 완충 장치가 될 것이라고 설명했어요.

paragraphs.en: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said there is "a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year." He spoke on Friday at a JPMorgan Chase investor event in New York, days before the planned Nov. 19 IPO. In a talk with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, he called compute "the deepest business dilemma" the company faces.
paragraphs.ko: 앤트로픽의 다리오 아모데이 CEO는 「내년에 무슨 일이 일어날지 큰 불확실성이 있다」고 말했어요. 그는 금요일 뉴욕의 JP모건 체이스 투자자 행사에서 11월 19일 예정된 IPO를 며칠 앞두고 말했어요. JP모건 CEO 제이미 다이먼과의 대화에서 그는 컴퓨팅 자원이 회사가 마주한 「가장 깊은 사업상 딜레마」라고 했어요.

sents.en: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said there is "a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year."
sents.ko: 앤트로픽의 다리오 아모데이 CEO는 「내년에 무슨 일이 일어날지 큰 불확실성이 있다」고 말했어요.

sents.en: He spoke on Friday at a JPMorgan Chase investor event in New York, days before the planned Nov. 19 IPO.

sents.en: In a talk with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, he called compute "the deepest business dilemma" the company faces.
sents.ko: JP모건 CEO 제이미 다이먼과의 대화에서 그는 컴퓨팅 자원이 회사가 마주한 「가장 깊은 사업상 딜레마」라고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Amodei said compute has to be bought one to two years ahead, before anyone knows whether revenue will justify the cost. If Anthropic buys too little, it will lack resources for customers and new technology, and revenue will suffer. If it buys too much, he said, it can financially overextend itself. Bloomberg says Anthropic has committed nearly $901 billion, mostly to compute and chips. About $71 billion of that comes due by September 2027.
paragraphs.ko: 아모데이는 매출이 비용을 정당화할지 알기 전인 1~2년 앞서 컴퓨팅을 사야 한다고 말했어요. 너무 적게 사면 고객과 신기술에 쓸 자원이 모자라 매출이 줄어요. 너무 많이 사면 재정적으로 무리하게 될 수 있다고 그는 말했어요. 블룸버그에 따르면 앤트로픽은 대부분 컴퓨팅과 칩에 쓰기로 약 9,010억 달러를 약속했어요. 그 가운데 약 710억 달러는 2027년 9월까지 내야 해요.

sents.en: If it buys too much, he said, it can financially overextend itself.

sents.en: About $71 billion of that comes due by September 2027.
sents.ko: 그 가운데 약 710억 달러는 2027년 9월까지 내야 해요.

paragraphs.en: In February 2026, Amodei warned that he could buy $1 trillion of compute starting at the end of 2027 and go bankrupt if revenue fell short. Being off by just one year could mean bankruptcy. He described two cushions: gross margins that are "quite good" and a large cash balance. The company also buys relatively little compute upfront and can turn to the spot market for more. Amodei compared this to buying insurance.

pro.en: Days before a planned Nov. 19 stock-market debut that could prove the largest IPO ever, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei conceded at a JPMorgan Chase investor event in New York on Friday that there is "a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year." In conversation with JPMorgan chief executive Jamie Dimon, he called compute "the deepest business dilemma" the company faces.

The difficulty, Amodei said, is that computing capacity must be purchased one to two years ahead, before anyone knows whether revenue will justify the outlay; buy too little and the company lacks resources for customers and new technology, hurting revenue, while buying too much risks financial overextension. According to Bloomberg, Anthropic has committed nearly $901 billion, mostly to compute and chips, with roughly $71 billion falling due by September 2027.

In February 2026 Amodei warned more starkly that buying $1 trillion of compute from late 2027 could bankrupt him if revenue fell short, since being off by a single year might suffice. He outlined two cushions, gross margins he called quite good and a large cash balance, and noted that the company buys relatively little compute upfront and can tap the spot market for more, an approach he likened to insurance.

The compute wagers, Amodei said, were the chief reason to go public, since more cash widens the margin for error. Bloomberg reports that Anthropic plans to raise up to $64.4 billion in the IPO and a further $26 billion via private placement, which would make it the biggest listing ever and is reportedly about six times oversubscribed, while company filings show annualized revenue running at $81 billion at the end of October.

Amodei struck a relaxed tone on timing, noting that Anthropic went from nothing to its present size in just six years, and said the advice that resonated most was never to let a company be worth a single dollar more than it is really worth. He also voiced hope that AI will cure cancer and Alzheimer's within five to 15 years, though he said he does not know exactly, an aspiration The Decoder notes may already count as under-promising in Silicon Valley.

views.view: Amodei says compute is the hardest business choice and nobody knows how it will pay off, but he says margins and cash soften the risk.

issues.title: Nigeria worries about AI fakes ahead of its 2027 elections
issues.gist: Nigeria's election body found voter-list pictures that seem to be made with AI. Experts warn that AI fakes could hurt trust in the 2027 vote.
issues.gistKo: 나이지리아 선거 기구가 유권자 명부에서 AI로 만든 것 같은 사진을 발견했어요. 전문가들은 AI 가짜가 2027년 선거의 신뢰를 흔들 수 있다고 경고해요.
issues.easyKo: 나이지리아에서 2027년 선거를 앞두고 AI 가짜 정보 걱정이 커졌어요. 유권자 명부에 이상한 사진과 겹친 이름이 나왔고, 선거 기구가 AI 위협을 감시할 부서를 만들기로 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Nigeria will hold national elections in 2027, and many people worry about fake content made with artificial intelligence. The election body, called INEC, recently released a preliminary voter list. The list reportedly contains pictures that seem to have been made with AI. Signs include exaggerated faces, repeated names, and people who have died since the last election.
paragraphs.ko: 나이지리아가 2027년 총선을 치르는데, 인공지능으로 만든 가짜 콘텐츠를 걱정하는 사람이 많아요. 선거를 관리하는 기구 INEC가 최근 잠정 유권자 명부를 공개했어요. 명부에 AI로 만든 것으로 보이는 사진이 들어 있다고 알려졌어요. 눈에 띄는 징후는 과장된 얼굴, 겹치는 이름, 지난 선거 이후 숨진 사람들이에요.

She said some parties already use inflated crowds to show that they have wide support. Akintunde Babatunde of the journalism group CJID said the deeper danger is that people may doubt real information. He noted a lawmaker who made harsh remarks at a rally and later claimed the clips were manipulated. Chibuike Mgbeahuruike of CDD-West Africa said AI is not itself the threat, but weak accountability is.

pro.en: Nigeria heads into its 2027 general elections amid mounting anxiety over AI-generated falsehoods, after the Independent National Electoral Commission, or INEC, published a preliminary voter register that reportedly contains images believed to have been produced with artificial intelligence. Telltale signs include distorted facial features, duplicated names and entries for people who have died since the last election.

INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission is investigating the anomalies and announced a dedicated unit to monitor AI-related threats and detect deepfakes, cautioning that the credibility of the vote could otherwise come under attack.

Lois Ugbede of the fact-checking platform DUBAWA described AI-driven disinformation as serious and increasingly commonplace, noting that parties are already deploying inflated crowds to project popular support. Akintunde Babatunde of the Center for Journalism, Innovation and Development, or CJID, argued that the more insidious danger is that people begin to doubt authentic information, and he cited a lawmaker who made inflammatory remarks at a rally and later claimed the recordings had been manipulated. Chibuike Mgbeahuruike of CDD-West Africa maintained that AI is not inherently a threat, and that the real problem is the absence of effective accountability.

Fabricated content is hardly unprecedented in Nigeria: ahead of the 2023 elections, deepfakes falsely tied candidates to terrorism. Electoral technology dates back to 2011, when machines were introduced to scan fingerprints, and in 2023 a newer system known as BVAS faltered in places because of weak cell coverage. That year's turnout, at 27 percent of registered voters, was the lowest since 1999.

With more than 103 million Nigerians on the register, incumbent President Bola Tinubu is set to face former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and opposition figure Peter Obi. The question now is whether INEC's new unit can expose fakes and restore public confidence.

pro.en: Technology shares tumbled last week after the Democrats secured control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, with the so-called Magnificent Seven shedding more than $1 trillion in market value in a single session. Nvidia then lost nearly 10 percent over two days this week, and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, stepped down on Thursday.

Many AI stocks had touched record highs in the first half of 2026, but Wall Street has grown wary of the sheer scale of outlays. In September, Goldman Sachs calculated that the large cloud providers would need roughly $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even, leaving a shortfall of about $230 billion.

Anthropic still intends to list later this month, having said it will offer 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78. Although it initially sought a valuation above $2 trillion, it now puts the figure at roughly $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, while OpenAI has pushed its own listing back to next year. Analyst Dennis Dick said he was puzzled by the decision to proceed, arguing that a company with roughly $52 billion in revenue today sounds overvalued at that price.

Others are more sanguine. Kit Rees of Quilter described last week's rout as a healthy correction and said the AI build-out remains in its early stages. Even so, borrowing costs for infrastructure firms such as CoreWeave and Oracle have climbed sharply, the price of insuring Nvidia's debt against default has risen 76 percent in a month, according to CNBC, and Oracle's shares have slid 65 percent from their peak.

Rees pointed to slowing AI revenue, waning appetite for financing and new rules that complicate data center construction as signals to monitor; New York and Texas both temporarily halted new data center approvals this summer. Economist Gary Smith likens the boom to earlier manias and predicts a crash, and strategist Joachim Klement believes a reckoning could arrive in 2027 or 2028.

paragraphs.en: Many families in the region have been split for generations, and Yaseen says his own family was divided between two countries. pro.en: Young vocalists across the mountains of Kashmir, Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan are circulating songs in the Shina language online. The music travels across the Line of Control, which separates the Indian-administered and Pakistani-administered portions of Kashmir. Among them is Aasim Yaseen, a 25-year-old singer from the village of Buglinder in the Tulail Valley.

Families in the region have been separated for generations, and Yaseen says his own kin were split between two countries. Residents of Gurez and Drass say security restrictions make them wary of phoning or messaging relatives across the line, fearing that contact could draw suspicion. Songs feel safer, since listeners on the far side can hear them without any direct exchange. Artists began posting on Facebook and YouTube in the late 2010s, and by 2020 residents were using the music to reconnect.

Salman Paras, a 38-year-old Shina folk singer from Gilgit-Baltistan, blends folk tradition with contemporary pop. His collaboration with the Pakistani singer Ali Zafar has drawn millions of views on YouTube. On November 3 he performed live on Instagram, attracting listeners from Gurez, Drass, Kargil and Gilgit-Baltistan, and he says he hopes to perform in Gurez and Ladakh if the necessary permissions and a visa can be arranged.

The musicians nonetheless contend with considerable obstacles. Yaseen says producing a single song, including studio time and production, costs between 30,000 and 35,000 Indian rupees. Some villages near the Line of Control have little or no mobile coverage, and certain artists can upload a track but cannot earn income from it. To hold down expenses, singers pool microphones, speakers and editing skills.

For Shina speakers, the songs also serve to safeguard the language itself. Iftikhar Uddin Iftikhar, a 29-year-old singer in Gilgit, says he is not merely promoting songs but keeping the language alive. Younis Majeed, a 27-year-old singer from Izmarg, says the internet helps people get to know one another again. The report forms part of an Al Jazeera series examining how borders shape daily life and divide families.

views.view: Sharing Shina songs online helps young musicians keep their language alive and renew ties across the divide, despite money and internet problems.

issues.title: MIT's new AI copilot lets engineers guide computer-made designs for buildings and bridges
issues.gist: MIT researchers built an AI copilot that asks human engineers for feedback while a computer designs a structure. The team says designs became easier to build and stronger against buckling, and the process took only 15 seconds longer.
issues.gistKo: MIT 연구팀이 컴퓨터가 구조물을 설계하는 도중에 사람 엔지니어에게 의견을 묻는 AI 부조종사를 만들었어요. 설계가 더 만들기 쉽고 좌굴에 강해졌는데, 설계 시간은 15초만 늘었다고 해요.
issues.easyKo: 컴퓨터가 건물이나 다리의 뼈대를 설계하면 사람은 끝난 뒤에야 결과를 보고, 마음에 안 들면 처음부터 다시 해야 했어요. 이 시스템은 설계가 진행되는 중에 사람이 고칠 곳을 짚어 주게 해요. 그래서 믿고 쓸 만한 설계가 더 쉽게 나와요.

paragraphs.en: MIT researchers have built an AI system that works like a copilot for engineers who design buildings and bridges. Computers can already create strong, light structures with a method called topology optimization. But the engineer usually sees the design only at the end, and often must start over to make a change.
paragraphs.ko: MIT 연구팀이 건물과 다리를 설계하는 엔지니어를 돕는 부조종사 같은 AI 시스템을 만들었어요. 컴퓨터는 이미 위상 최적화라는 방법으로 튼튼하고 가벼운 구조물을 만들 수 있어요. 하지만 엔지니어는 보통 끝에서야 설계를 보고, 바꾸려면 처음부터 다시 해야 하는 경우가 많아요.

sents.en: Computers can already create strong, light structures with a method called topology optimization.

paragraphs.en: That also makes it harder to trust that the final design is structurally sound. For example, some designs need eight or more beam connections at a single point, which would be hard to build. Lead author Dat Ha says engineers are very skeptical of programs that give weird or unexpected designs. He says the black box nature of the method has kept it from being used widely in industry.

paragraphs.en: In the new system, the algorithm shows regions of the design to a human while it is still working. A machine-learning model quickly guesses which regions a person would most likely want to change. To train it, the team made a synthetic dataset of likely human feedback on thousands of designs. pro.en: A team at MIT has developed an AI system that acts as a copilot for engineers designing buildings and bridges, inviting their input while an algorithm is still generating a structure. Algorithmic techniques such as topology optimization can already yield strong yet lightweight structures, but designers typically see the result only once the run is complete and frequently must begin again to alter it.

That opacity also undermines confidence that the final design is structurally sound; some outputs, for instance, call for eight or more beam connections to converge at a single point, a detail that would be difficult to fabricate. Lead author Dat Ha says engineers are deeply skeptical of software that produces odd or unexpected geometries, and he argues that the method's black box character has limited its uptake in industry.

Under the new system, the algorithm presents regions of the design to a human while it is still running, and a machine-learning model rapidly predicts which regions a person is most likely to want to alter. To train the model, the researchers assembled a synthetic dataset of probable human feedback on thousands of designs, spanning aesthetics, performance goals and ease of manufacture.

In demonstrations, the human-in-the-loop approach improved manufacturability and linear buckling load by 39 percent, while the paper in Communications Engineering reports that it added just 15 seconds to total design time. At present, users can only thicken or thin marked regions, though the team intends to introduce other modification options in later versions.

Senior author Josephine Carstensen says the technique should complement approaches that rely solely on AI, since there is room for both depending on the computing power a team has. She adds that in some settings humans must make the final call before a design advances, and the team hopes the tool will reach a wider circle of industry users, researchers and students.

She says she earns a high six-figure income, and she now teaches courses on using AI to produce books. One study, still awaiting peer review, estimates that about one fifth of recently self-published books contain at least 25 percent AI-generated text.

pro.en: A Guardian long read reports that allegations of AI use are sending shock waves through the publishing industry, with some authors losing lucrative deals and others being struck from prize shortlists. Romance novelist Coral Hart says she has written 370 novels under 21 pen names with the help of AI since 2025, earning what she describes as a high six-figure income, and now teaches courses on producing books this way. One study, still awaiting peer review, estimates that roughly a fifth of recently self-published books contain at least 25 percent AI-generated text.

Much of the fury stems from how such models are built. Last year, a class action covering around 500,000 titles secured a $1.5 billion settlement from the AI firm Anthropic. A group of 70 prominent authors, meanwhile, wrote an open letter urging the five largest publishers to pledge never to release books created by a machine; the publishers declined to make that promise.

In March, Hachette pulled the romance novel Shy Girl from publication after evidence emerged that AI had been used. In July, agents withdrew from a $2 million book deal with a debut novelist once he was accused of using AI, which he denied beyond using it for research. Last month, a novel was also removed from the Goncourt Academy longlist after users ran it through AI detection software.

The Guardian notes that accused writers struggle to clear their names, since there is no definitive proof either way. Research estimates the detector Pangram is at least 95 percent accurate with a near-zero false-positive rate, yet the report says non-native and neurodivergent writers are more likely to attract unfounded suspicion. Hannah Bowman of the Association of American Literary Agents says agents are split over whether detectors should be used routinely, and she calls for a fair and thoughtful process in which writers can make their case.

Experts point to different ways forward. Publishing expert Thad McIllroy argues that publishers should be bold and publish explicit AI policies, while writer Stephen Marche says the answer lies in full transparency about what is and is not AI-generated. US copyright law requires a book to be human authored, which poses a problem for publishers when text originates with AI, and in France a new prize for fiction written with AI was launched last month.

views.view: With no clear rules and no proof either way, publishing needs AI policies and fair processes, and readers will likely still prefer human writing.

why: AI writing is forcing publishers, prizes and readers to decide what counts as a human-made book.
The rules are still unclear, so accusations are spreading faster than answers.
lines.agree: Many people say publishers need clearer rules on AI, and writers need a fair way to respond to doubts.
lines.split: Some agents want to use AI detectors routinely, while others prefer to rely on trust.

pro.en: Jacob Coxon, a onetime researcher at both OpenAI and Anthropic, has said that a chart in Anthropic's investor materials was a major factor in his decision to leave the company. He lasted only about four months there. The graphic was unveiled during the roadshow ahead of the company's planned IPO, its first offering of shares to the public.

The chart tracks how much computing power Anthropic requires over time to train its models. Its vertical axis is compressed to the point that a tenfold increase and a hundredfold increase are barely distinguishable. Even so, the curve rises sharply, which Coxon reads as evidence that algorithmic methods are improving at an accelerating rate. He called it an insane plot and said he was surprised the company had made it public.

In Coxon's account, Anthropic's Mythos model, a significant leap in capability this spring, was one point along that accelerating trajectory. He wrote that Anthropic could already retrain Mythos using a fraction of the compute it originally demanded, and he believes refinements to such methods are close to being automated. Anthropic itself cautions that the data points rest on internal estimates and are intended for illustration only.

For that reason, Coxon is calling for a pause in frontier model development next year so that rivals can close the gap. A pause, he argues, would turn human-level intelligence into a commodity, and it would harm only OpenAI and Anthropic.

Coxon first attracted broad attention in September, when he issued public warnings about the dangers of advanced AI systems, a stance other industry figures have echoed. Among the central fears is that advanced AI capable of improving itself could slip beyond human control. The details here derive from his own post on X, as relayed by The Decoder.

pro.en: A "Baby on board" decal is a familiar sight on cars. One Korean father, however, opted for a different banner for a considerably older child, one announcing that his son had just completed his military service and was riding along.

The father said he wanted to mark the end of his son's 18-month compulsory military service. The family made the journey from Inje, in Gangwon Province, to Cheongyang, in South Chungcheong Province, a distance well in excess of 200 kilometers. By the father's account, fellow motorists lowered their windows to flash a thumbs-up, formed finger hearts and sounded their horns in congratulation.

On Wednesday, the father published a message of thanks on the online forum Bobaedream, writing that the family sincerely appreciated the warm reception. He conceded that some might regard the gesture as excessive, and he apologized if the car had caused any inconvenience along the route.

The post swiftly went viral. Commenters described the idea as creative and adorable, and one predicted the son would look back on the trip with fondness. The episode illustrates how a modest, lighthearted gesture can transform a family milestone into a moment shared with strangers on the road.

views.view: Online commenters called the banner creative and adorable and said the son would remember the trip fondly.

issues.title: Korean families give new good-luck gifts, from temple key rings to rice cakes, before the Suneung exam
issues.gist: Ahead of the Suneung college entrance exam on Nov. 19, Korean families are mixing old luck rituals with new gifts like key rings that sound like a temple instrument. Scholars say the forms change while the wish stays the same.
issues.gistKo: 11월 19일 수능을 앞두고 한국 가족들은 목탁 소리 열쇠고리 같은 새 선물과 오래된 풍습을 함께 쓰고 있어요. 학자들은 모양은 바뀌어도 바라는 마음은 같다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: Ahead of South Korea's college entrance exam, the Suneung, families are finding new ways to wish students luck. The exam takes place on Nov. 19 this year. At a shop near Jogyesa in central Seoul, a merchant sells key rings that play the sound of a wooden instrument called the moktak. The merchant said the shop has sold about 1,000 of them in two weeks. The idea is that each press adds a little Buddhist merit, known as gongdeok.

pro.en: As the Suneung, South Korea's national college entrance exam, approaches, families are devising fresh ways to wish students good fortune. This year the exam falls on Nov. 19. At a shop near Jogyesa in central Seoul, a merchant is selling key rings that emit the hollow tapping of a moktak, a wooden instrument used in Buddhist rituals, and he said roughly 1,000 had sold in two weeks. The notion is that every press accrues a little Buddhist merit, or gongdeok.

Traditional gifts remain in demand. Families still hand students paper talismans, sticky rice cakes and traditional sweets. On Wednesday, ahead of the opening of the Hyundai Department Store in Pangyo, a queue stretching hundreds of meters formed for fruit-filled sticky rice cakes. Rice cakes and candy are favored because the same Korean verb can mean both to stick and to pass an exam, while some students avoid seaweed soup, whose slippery texture evokes an expression that can also mean to fail.

A university's name can carry a wish as well: a box of Yonsei Milk's ice cream rice cakes lets a giver convey a more pointed message to a student aspiring to enter Yonsei University. The exam also reshapes the day for those who are not sitting it. Government offices and businesses have been asked to begin work at 10 a.m. or later, and aircraft takeoffs and landings will be adjusted during the English listening section.

Scholars attribute the proliferation of rituals to the exam's standing as a turning point in students' lives. Shim Hyoung-june of the Korea Institute for Religion and Culture observes that people fashioned charms from ordinary items such as dried pollock and rice cakes, and that although the materials have changed, the way people select charms appears largely unchanged. Lee Song-chong, a professor of religious studies at Seoul National University, says people continue to hope for luck even after doing everything within their power.

Lee expects such practices to assume new forms as culture evolves, and he cites a virtual Buddhist temple called online Sansa, which recently drew attention in South Korea. Built with the help of AI, it allows visitors to perform 108 bows through avatars. Back near Jogyesa, the merchant said demand for paper talismans has dwindled, which he attributes to the wider range of good-luck charms now on offer.

views.view: Scholars say the materials of luck charms change with the times, but the way people choose them stays much the same.

issues.title: Korea's Pension Fund Gains on US Tech Stocks Even as Chip Shares Fall
issues.gist: The National Pension Service's US stocks were worth $158.74 billion at the end of September, up $3.66 billion in three months. Big tech stocks drove the gain while chip stocks were weaker.
issues.gistKo: 국민연금의 미국 주식은 9월 말 1587억 4000만 달러로 석 달 새 36억 6000만 달러 늘었어요. 대형 기술주가 오름세를 이끌고 반도체주는 약했어요.
issues.easyKo: 국민연금이 가진 미국 주식 가치가 3분기에 올랐어요. 마이크로소프트 같은 큰 기술주가 올랐고, 반도체 주식은 상대적으로 부진했어요. 원화로 보면 가치는 줄었어요.

pro.en: The value of US equities held by South Korea's National Pension Service rose in the third quarter, lifted by gains in major technology shares despite a selloff in semiconductor stocks. The fund held $158.74 billion across 553 US-listed companies at the end of September.

That marks an increase of $3.66 billion from three months earlier, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. Its shareholdings climbed 0.9 percent to 936.18 million shares. The portfolio's value in Korean won, however, slipped from about 239 trillion won at the end of June as the won strengthened against the dollar.

The holdings in the so-called Magnificent Seven, namely Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Tesla, jumped 12.6 percent to $49.1 billion, while the share count edged up only 0.5 percent, indicating that price appreciation accounted for most of the gain. Microsoft led the advance, with the value of its stake surging 38.2 percent to $7.86 billion.

Semiconductor positions fared worse. The value of the Micron stake dropped 7.4 percent, and Applied Materials, Lam Research, Intel and Broadcom all registered declines. The NPS nonetheless added to most of its major US chip positions, increasing shareholdings by 0.1 to 0.9 percent, although its Super Micro Computer holdings shrank 35.1 percent.

The pension fund also expanded its exposure to space and defense names, building on its holdings in SpaceX and Rocket Lab as well as Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Palantir and RTX. It initiated a position in the stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group and trimmed its stakes in the bitcoin-linked companies Strategy and Coinbase by 0.7 percent and 10.1 percent, respectively.

views.view: Big tech gains lifted the pension fund's US holdings, while chip shares fell and the strong won cut the value in won.

why: The NPS is one of the world's big pension investors, and its choices show where it sees growth.
Its US holdings reflect how tech and chip stocks are moving.

lines.next: Watch the next quarterly filing to see whether the NPS keeps adding to chip stocks.

issues.title: Fake AI Images and Posts Spread After the Krakow Shooting, DW Fact Check Finds
issues.gist: After a deadly shooting in Krakow, Poland, on Nov. 7, fake AI images and false posts spread fast online. DW Fact Check looked at three viral claims and found them fake or false.
issues.gistKo: 폴란드 크라쿠프 총격 사건 뒤 AI가 만든 가짜 이미지와 거짓 게시물이 빠르게 퍼졌어요. DW 팩트체크는 인기 주장 세 가지를 살펴 가짜 또는 거짓으로 밝혔어요.
issues.easyKo: 큰 사건이 터지면 사실이 알려지기 전에 가짜 사진과 글이 먼저 퍼질 수 있어요. 이번 크라쿠프 사건에서도 AI 탐지기와 계정 기록 확인으로 가짜가 가려졌어요.

paragraphs.en: A gunman killed six people in Krakow's Old Town on Saturday, Nov. 7. Police shot and detained him, and he later died in hospital. He is also suspected of killing three family members before the attack.
paragraphs.ko: 11월 7일 토요일에 총기를 든 남성이 크라쿠프 구시가지에서 여섯 명을 숨지게 했어요. 경찰이 그를 쏘아 붙잡았고, 그는 나중에 병원에서 숨졌어요. 그는 공격 전에 가족 세 명도 숨지게 한 혐의를 받아요.

paragraphs.en: On Monday, Nov. 9, Poland's national prosecutor's office announced a formal investigation. Much is still unknown about the crime, so social media users filled the gap with fake images and alleged screenshots. DW Fact Check examined several viral claims.

paragraphs.en: First, a viral picture claimed to show the real face of the attacker. DW called it fake because two AI detectors flagged it. Hive Moderation identified it as 99.5% AI-generated, and Google's SynthID Detector found a SynthID watermark. DW also noted that AI cannot recover details that are not visible in an original photograph.
paragraphs.ko: 첫째, 한 인기 사진은 공격한 사람의 진짜 얼굴이라고 주장했어요. DW는 AI 탐지기 두 곳이 걸러 냈기 때문에 이를 가짜로 판정했어요. 하이브 모더레이션은 99.5% AI가 만든 것으로 봤고, 구글의 신스ID 탐지기는 신스ID 워터마크를 찾았어요. DW는 또 AI가 원래 사진에 보이지 않는 세부를 되살릴 수 없다고 짚었어요.

pro.en: A gunman killed six people in a shooting spree in Krakow's Old Town on Saturday, Nov. 7, before police shot and detained him; he later died in hospital. He is also suspected of having killed three family members ahead of the attack.

On Monday, Nov. 9, Poland's national prosecutor's office announced a formal investigation. With so much about the crime still unknown, social media users rushed to fill the information vacuum with fabricated images and purported screenshots, and DW Fact Check scrutinized several of the viral claims.

The first was a widely shared picture said to show the attacker's true face. DW judged it fake after two AI detectors flagged it: Hive Moderation rated it 99.5% likely to be AI-generated, and Google's SynthID Detector found a SynthID watermark. DW also stressed that AI cannot restore details absent from an original photograph.

The second was an X post, viewed more than 700,000 times, asserting that the attacker's Telegram account displayed sympathy for Ukraine. DW concluded the channel was almost certainly inauthentic, since its posts and profile photo were altered on November 8, after the suspect had been apprehended. It described this as a familiar tactic in which fake accounts retroactively edit old posts after a breaking event to appear to have foreseen it.

The third was an X post, viewed nearly 100,000 times, showing a trunk packed with weaponry and alleging a link to an American group operating in Ukraine. DW established that the photo does not depict the attacker's car, as the license plate is registered with the Krakow police. Such small details, it noted, can help separate fact from fiction in a fast-moving story.

views.view: Fake and AI-edited images and posts spread quickly after the attack, so checking small details is important.

pro.en: The cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Thursday it had completed coverage of assets compromised in a sweeping cyberattack, having committed more than $6.34 billion of company funds to offset the losses.

To do so, Binance drew on its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, while acquiring the affected tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions. The firm pledged to replenish SAFU to roughly $1 billion, so that it remains fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve.

The breach occurred on Oct. 29, when hackers allegedly tied to North Korea made off with more than $6 billion in digital assets. The FBI attributed the theft to a North Korean group known as TraderTraitor, cautioning that the proceeds could be laundered through decentralized finance platforms and cryptocurrency exchange services.

Kim Yo-jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, dismissed the FBI's findings earlier this month as a “grave political provocation” against Pyongyang. The US State Department, for its part, reiterated its concern over North Korea's use of cybercrime to bankroll its weapons programs, framing it as a global problem touching firms and jurisdictions worldwide.

Taken together, the Binance statement and Washington's remarks present two sides of the case: a company shoring up its losses and governments warning of cybercrime. For Korean readers, the episode is of interest because the alleged culprits are linked to Pyongyang.

views.view: Binance says it covered all the losses, while the US blames North Korean hackers and North Korea rejects the claim.

pro.en: Samsung Biologics' labor dispute is entering a new phase as its union moves to join the Federation of Korean Trade Unions (FKTU), with a second partial strike in its second week and collective bargaining due to resume next week.

The union will conduct an online vote from Friday through Tuesday on affiliating with the FKTU, the nation's second-largest umbrella labor body, having concluded that it needed higher-level backing after hitting the limits of an enterprise-level union. Approval requires turnout by a majority of registered members and support from a majority of those voting; the union has about 4,000 members, all eligible.

Roughly 500 members are taking part in the walkout, which began Nov. 6 and is scheduled to run through Nov. 27, covering roles such as quality control testing, logistics and manufacturing support. Its partial character follows a court ruling that widened strike injunctions to nine categories of work, while the company says production has not been disrupted so far.

Negotiations are expected to resume Tuesday after plans for intensive talks on Nov. 3 collapsed. Management had sought a two-week postponement, citing trust concerns and the union's demand to replace certain negotiators; the union accused the company of unilaterally abandoning the talks. Both sides maintain that they remain open to dialogue.

Whether the proposal will pass remains uncertain, with some industry observers questioning whether the union's relatively young membership will favor joining an FKTU that has often been embroiled in political disputes. For students planning careers, the dispute offers a close look at how unions, courts and companies handle a strike in Korea.

views.view: The report says the union hopes FKTU support will strengthen its hand, while some observers doubt the vote will pass.

pro.en: Incheon Metropolitan City invited diplomatic envoys from 36 countries stationed in South Korea to rally support for its bid to host the 2028 G20 Summit, at a briefing held Nov. 13 at Gyeongwonjae by Walkerhill in Songdo, attended by Mayor Park Chan-dae, city officials and Zakariya Al Saadi, the Omani ambassador to Korea.

Mayor Park asserted that Incheon has the agenda, the location and the capabilities needed to host the summit. He noted that 2028 marks the 20th anniversary of the G20 Summit's launch and vowed to carry forward the spirit of cooperation shown during the 2008 financial crisis.

The city said it has a number of competitive advantages, among them the capacity to put major G20 agenda items such as climate change and technological innovation into practice, drawing on the Green Climate Fund secretariat and the bio cluster in Songdo. It also pointed to AI logistics innovation around Incheon International Airport and Incheon Port as a major achievement.

Officials stressed geography and security as strengths: Songdo can be reached from the airport within 25 minutes, with venues and accommodations concentrated nearby, and the area's connection by bridges is advantageous for security. Incheon has previously hosted the 2010 G20 Sherpa Meeting, the Asian Games and an annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank, and it will host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Senior Officials' Meeting next year.

Speaking for the delegation, the Omani ambassador responded positively, saying the transformation of Songdo and Incheon's future industries was leaving a deep impression worldwide. The envoys then toured the Incheon Free Economic Zone promotional hall to view its smart city management system, and the city said it would keep using diplomatic channels to pursue the bid.

views.view: The report shows Incheon's case for the bid and notes the Omani ambassador's positive response.

issues.title: Google meets key map security checks in Korea and picks Tmap as its local partner
issues.gist: South Korea says Google has put key security measures in place for using detailed Korean map data. Google has also chosen Tmap Mobility to process the data in Korea.
issues.gistKo: 한국 정부가 구글이 상세한 한국 지도 데이터를 쓰기 위한 핵심 보안 조치를 갖췄다고 밝혔어요. 구글은 국내에서 데이터를 처리할 파트너로 티맵모빌리티를 골랐어요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea said on Friday that Google has put in place key security measures for using detailed Korean map data. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said a review committee checked Google's compliance after a meeting with government officials and private experts. This brings Google a step closer to full navigation services in Korea after nearly two decades of regulatory hurdles. Seoul gave conditional approval on Feb. 27, which ended a 19-year standoff over moving Korean map data to servers overseas.

paragraphs.en: Google removed latitude and longitude coordinates for South Korean territory from Google Maps and Google Earth, on both web and mobile. pro.en: South Korea confirmed on Friday that Google has implemented the key security measures required to export detailed Korean map data, edging the U.S. technology giant closer to offering full navigation services after nearly two decades of regulatory hurdles. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said an interagency review committee verified Google's compliance following a meeting with officials and private-sector experts, building on Seoul's conditional approval on Feb. 27, which ended a 19-year standoff over transferring Korean map data to overseas servers.

Google stripped latitude and longitude coordinates for South Korean territory from Google Maps and Google Earth across web and mobile platforms, and developed a Korea-specific control system that blocks app updates if restricted location data is detected. Military installations and other sensitive sites are obscured in satellite imagery, although the transition to imagery screened by Korean authorities remains incomplete, and Google has also removed Street View images of those facilities and of roads within 50 meters of their boundaries.

The government has required Google to rely on a Korean partner to process map data on domestic servers before it leaves the country, and only base maps and transport information, including road networks, road names, lane counts and speed limits, qualify for export. Industry sources said Google has selected Tmap Mobility for that role and could begin using Tmap-processed data as early as 2027; the arrangement is confined to static map information and excludes users' personal data, real-time locations and search histories, while neither company has disclosed the contract's value, which industry estimates put at several million dollars annually.

Google has designated the president of Google Korea as its local point of contact and established a round-the-clock system for handling government requests, and any violation must be remedied within one business day. A committee official said authorities will continue to monitor the process and verify that coordinate restrictions stay in place, and serious violations could result in the suspension or revocation of the export approval.

The committee judged that applying Korean security standards to Google Maps and Google Earth could help address longstanding national security concerns. Google also pledged a multiyear cooperation program with Korea's geospatial industry, with details to be worked out alongside domestic firms, and the reports characterize the approval as a step toward full navigation services in Korea without providing a launch date.

views.view: Seoul confirms Google met key export conditions, but officials say they will keep checking and could cancel approval after serious violations.

issues.title: Korean math instructor calls medical school prep for 4-year-olds child abuse
issues.gist: A well-known Korean math instructor says intensive programs for children aged 3 or 4 are child abuse. Korea has recently limited placement tests for young children, but some academies may find ways around the rules.
issues.gistKo: 유명한 한국 수학 강사가 3, 4세 아이를 위한 강도 높은 프로그램은 아동 학대라고 말했어요. 한국은 최근 어린 아이의 레벨 테스트를 제한했지만, 일부 학원이 규칙을 피할 수 있다는 우려가 있어요.

paragraphs.en: A well-known Korean math instructor has started a debate about very early education in South Korea. Jung Seung-je said on the YouTube channel ChimChakMan that people who run intensive programs for children aged 3 or 4 should face criminal punishment. He called the programs child abuse and said the government should step in. His example was medical school preparation classes for preschoolers.

pro.en: A prominent Korean math instructor has ignited debate over South Korea's increasingly early education culture. Jung Seung-je, appearing on the YouTube channel ChimChakMan, called for criminal punishment of those running intensive programs for children aged 3 or 4, branded the programs child abuse and urged the government to intervene, citing medical school preparation classes for preschoolers.

Jung made the remarks in a video weighing which subject matters most, Korean, English or math, alongside fellow instructors Yoo Dae-jong and Kim Ji-young. Yoo said he could scarcely believe medical school preparation might begin at age 4, given that people retain no memory of what happened at that age.

The programs belong to a phenomenon Koreans call the age 4 entrance exam, in which young children sit placement tests for elite private academies, and some courses market themselves as early preparation for medical school or as gateways to English-language preschools. Last month the government introduced legal restrictions barring placement tests for infants and preschoolers, and Education Ministry guidelines described in the report prohibit cognitive instruction for children under 3 and cap lessons for those aged 3 and older at three hours a day.

Concerns persist, however, that some academies are skirting the rules by staging entrance examinations as ordinary interviews or disguising lessons as play. A report by the Korea Institute of Child Care and Education concluded that private education in early childhood, English-language preschools included, produced no clear positive effect on language development, problem-solving ability or executive function by first grade, and that children receiving more academically oriented tutoring tended to report lower self-esteem.

The controversy has drawn international media attention as an emblem of Korea's fierce academic competition. For university students it raises the question of how early the race for coveted schools ought to begin, while the report does not indicate whether the government will introduce additional rules.

pro.en: Construction Industry Guarantee, South Korea's leading provider of construction guarantees, marked its 30th anniversary on Thursday. At a ceremony in Seoul, it announced plans to accelerate AI-driven innovation and broaden its digital financial services.

Roughly 250 guests attended the commemorative event at the Westin Josun Seoul, among them an official from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, a deputy mayor of Incheon and former chairmen of member companies. The organization also unveiled a long-term vision titled “A Leap Forward in Trust: Building the Next 100 Years through AI Innovation.”

Under the blueprint, the group aims to improve the safety and efficiency of its asset management while introducing AI-powered businesses and upgrading digital financial services for its members. Acting chairman Choi Un-gu said the organization's three decades had been built on trust and partnership with its members.

By the end of 2025, membership had grown to 10,054 companies and total assets had reached 1.55 trillion won ($1.16 billion). Originally focused on guarantees for construction-related transactions, the group has since moved into lending and mutual aid, with eight mutual aid products, and has recently lowered guarantee and mutual aid fees while expanding digital offerings such as self-serve guarantees and Kakao-based guarantee services. The episode illustrates how AI strategies are now reaching long-established sectors such as construction finance.

issues.title: Democrats likely to keep Schumer and Jeffries despite party tension
issues.gist: Democrats won back Congress, but some want new leaders. Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries still seem likely to keep their top jobs.
issues.gistKo: 민주당이 의회를 되찾았지만 일부는 새 지도부를 원해요. 그래도 척 슈머와 하킴 제프리스는 최고 직위를 지킬 것으로 보여요.
issues.easyKo: 선거에서 크게 이긴 미국 민주당 안에서 지도부를 바꾸자는 목소리가 나와요. 그래도 상원의 슈머와 하원의 제프리스가 자리를 지킬 가능성이 커요. 투표는 11월과 12월에 있어요.

paragraphs.en: More than a week after Democrats won back control of the US Congress, the party is showing deep divisions. Senator Chuck Schumer and Representative Hakeem Jeffries now seem likely to keep their top jobs. Schumer, 75, leads Senate Democrats now, and Jeffries, 56, leads House Democrats. Schumer wants to lead the new Senate majority, and Jeffries wants to become speaker of the House. Some Democrats want fresh leaders, while others prefer continuity.

Senator Ruben Gallego said that when a manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract. Schumer says he has enough votes, and Senate Democrats choose their leader by private ballot with a simple majority.

pro.en: More than a week after Democrats rode a historic wave of support to retake Congress, deepening divisions threaten to blunt the party's momentum. Senator Chuck Schumer, 75, the Senate minority leader, and Representative Hakeem Jeffries, 56, his House counterpart, appear poised to retain their leadership posts, with Schumer seeking to head the new Senate majority and Jeffries the speakership. The prospect has laid bare a rift between lawmakers who favor continuity and those who want fresh leadership.

Allies point to the party's electoral gains as the chief justification. They credit Schumer with helping flip at least eight Republican-held Senate seats, leaving Democrats poised to hold as many as 56 seats, their largest majority since Barack Obama's first term. Senator Ruben Gallego likened Schumer to a manager who has taken a team to the World Series and deserves a new contract. Schumer says he has the votes, and Senate Democrats pick their leader by secret ballot, needing only a simple majority.

Dissent is nonetheless visible. Senator Chris Van Hollen said on Thursday he would challenge Schumer. By an Al Jazeera tally, 12 Democratic senators have pledged to back Schumer, while at least 10 have said they will not, though only half of those holdouts have endorsed Van Hollen. Senator Bernie Sanders argued that Schumer's views are out of step with the party base, and Senator Elissa Slotkin demanded a concrete plan for wielding the new majority. Tre Easton of the Searchlight Institute countered that a chamber leader's task is to hold the caucus together and count votes.

Jeffries faces no prominent rival as he seeks to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress convenes on January 3. The New Democrat Coalition, representing 142 lawmakers, has endorsed him. Representative Pramila Jayapal said she is withholding her backing unless he commits to Medicare for All, a government-funded health plan, but conceded that nobody can be beaten by nobody.

House Democrats will hold their leadership votes on November 18 and 19, and Senate Democrats on a date in December that has yet to be announced. Even with both chambers, the party will fall short of the 60 Senate votes generally needed to overcome a filibuster and will need Republican support for much of its legislation. Whoever prevails will face pressure from progressives seeking tougher action against President Donald Trump and from moderates favoring a more centrist path.

issues.title: Korean president says hostile takeovers could fix undervalued stocks
issues.gist: President Lee Jae Myung said hostile takeovers are the most important way to normalize Korea's stock market. He asked officials to review rules that block them.

paragraphs.en: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Friday that hostile takeovers are the most important way to fix the country's stock market. He spoke at a capital market policy meeting at the Korea Exchange in Seoul that lasted two and a half hours. Many Korean stocks stay valued very low, and Lee asked officials to find what could help.

pro.en: President Lee Jae Myung declared on Friday that hostile mergers and acquisitions are the most important mechanism for normalizing the market, urging officials to examine what could address the country's persistently undervalued stocks. He spoke during a two-and-a-half-hour capital market policy meeting at the Korea Exchange in Seoul.

Lee argued that South Korea must significantly increase takeover activity so that the overall pie grows. When a share price is abnormally depressed, he reasoned, an acquirer could either resell the company at a normal price or run it directly. He called for a comprehensive review of mechanisms blocking hostile bids. Such takeovers are legal in Korea, yet concentrated ownership makes them difficult without the consent of controlling shareholders, and some firms trade below book value while remaining insulated from bids.

Lee also questioned whether companies run like private businesses through concentrated ownership should remain listed, citing firms in which controlling shareholders hold more than half, or even 70 to 80 percent, of outstanding shares. He was unsure whether a 50 percent threshold was appropriate and asked officials to look into it. He further urged the prompt delisting of financially unsound, underperforming Kosdaq companies while stressing the need to protect firms with technological capability and growth potential.

The meeting also addressed proposed mandatory tender offer rules, which would oblige acquirers to offer to buy shares from minority shareholders when control changes hands, letting them share in the takeover premium. Ruling and opposition parties have agreed to introduce the system by amending the Capital Markets Act during the current National Assembly session. Domestic and foreign asset managers, however, oppose a proposal requiring buyers to purchase at least 50 percent plus one share while letting controlling shareholders sell first, arguing it would deny minority shareholders an equal opportunity to sell.

Lee put to a show of hands whether acquisitions should involve offers for all outstanding shares or only 50 percent plus one share, and how selling opportunities should be allocated. He wondered whether full tender offers might push up acquisition costs enough to deter deals and sought empirical evidence. Describing the matter as a judgment between the interests of controlling and minority shareholders, he said neither approach was absolutely right but that he leaned toward invigorating M&A, adding that the decision was not his alone and hoping the process would not be delayed too long.

paragraphs.en: Business Korea reported that Samsung Electronics is in talks to buy Modine Manufacturing, a US company that makes cooling systems for data centers. pro.en: Business Korea reported that Samsung Electronics is in negotiations to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US maker of data center cooling systems. The outlet said Bloomberg News first reported the talks on Nov. 13, citing multiple sources, and that a deal could be reached within a few weeks, though no final decision has been made.

The negotiations could still collapse, or rival suitors could emerge. Headquartered in Wisconsin, Modine produces heating, ventilation, air conditioning and thermal management systems for large commercial facilities and industrial machinery. Its cooling business serving hyperscalers building vast data centers has been expanding rapidly, and last month it spun off its automotive operations to concentrate on thermal management.

Last year, Samsung acquired the German company FlaktGroup, a specialist in heating, ventilation and air conditioning, investing roughly 1.5 billion euros. Business Korea said a Modine acquisition would represent another step in expanding Samsung's AI data center business, combining Modine's cooling technology and business base with FlaktGroup.

Masahiro Wakasugi, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said a deal would help Samsung diversify given its heavy reliance on memory. He argued the company should deploy cash generated by semiconductors to secure new growth engines such as data center operations. The episode illustrates how a chipmaker seeks fresh growth beyond memory.

views.view: It sees a possible Modine deal as a way for Samsung to strengthen its AI data center business and diversify beyond memory.

pro.en: South Korea's top financial regulator cautioned on Friday against tapping the country's stock market stabilization fund, saying it should be held back for genuine emergencies. Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon made the remarks at a capital market policy meeting held at the Korea Exchange in Seoul and chaired by President Lee Jae Myung, after some market participants urged the authorities to activate the fund to dampen share-price volatility.

Lee noted that the fund, established in 2000 and repeatedly extended, remains ready to be deployed through a capital-call mechanism under which participating institutions contribute money as required. Yet he stressed that it was designed for highly urgent, temporary and exceptional circumstances, and said it remains an open question whether it should be used whenever markets turn volatile or only when systemic risks emerge, a matter he said warrants further discussion.

The call for restraint was not universal. Kim Jin-wook, a senior executive at Citibank Korea, contended that activating the fund could help restore investor confidence, arguing that the market requires a firm signal from the government to contain volatility. The president, for his part, asked whether fears of government intervention and of eroding market confidence had made officials reluctant to use the fund, and Lee acknowledged that they had.

President Lee urged officials to examine how the fund might be made more effective, what its appropriate size should be and whether alternative mechanisms are needed. Separately, Lee Seung-woo, a senior Financial Supervisory Service official, proposed broadening earnings calls, in which executives field investors' questions after results are announced, saying companies must do more to explain their profit outlook and how earnings will be shared with shareholders.

For young Koreans who invest or intend to, the discussion highlights a basic dilemma in market policy: when a government should step in to steady prices and when it should let them find their own level. The question remains unsettled, since the president has asked for a review of the fund, and attention now turns to what that review concludes about its size, its rules and any alternatives.

issues.title: Leaked Russian Records Show At Least 450,000 Deaths in the Ukraine War
issues.gist: Leaked records from Russia's statistics agency show at least 450,000 Russians died in the Ukraine war up to August. The data has not been independently verified, but media and analysts believe it is real.
issues.gistKo: 러시아 통계청에서 유출된 기록에 따르면 8월까지 우크라이나 전쟁에서 최소 45만 명의 러시아인이 숨졌어요. 독립적으로 검증되지는 않았지만 언론과 분석가들은 진짜라고 봐요.
issues.easyKo: 해커들이 러시아 통계청 기록을 빼내 공개했어요. 전쟁 사망자가 최소 45만 명이고 외국인도 4,000명 넘게 있었어요. 러시아 정부는 사망자 수를 공식 발표하지 않아요.

paragraphs.en: Records leaked from Rosstat, Russia's state statistics agency, show that at least 450,000 Russians died in the war in Ukraine up to August this year. Most of them were soldiers. More than 4,000 foreign citizens are also believed to be among the dead. Two hacking groups, the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Ukraine's Silent Crow, obtained the records. Moscow does not officially publish its military death toll.

pro.en: Leaked records from Rosstat, Russia's state statistics agency, indicate that at least 450,000 Russians, the great majority of them soldiers, had died in the war in Ukraine through August this year. The files also point to more than 4,000 foreign nationals among the dead. They were obtained by two hacking collectives, the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Ukraine's Silent Crow, while Moscow does not officially publish its military death toll.

Rosstat acknowledged that it had come under cyberattack between October 29 and November 1 but said it had found no evidence that its databases were compromised. The material has not been independently verified, though news organisations and analysts regard it as genuine. Financial Times investigations conclude that, once belatedly registered deaths are factored in, the toll through August will settle at roughly 550,000.

The files record about 410,000 deaths classified directly as war-related and a further 42,000 fighting-age men whose deaths were confirmed in court, and the Financial Times identified another 12,000 probable military fatalities, for a minimum of 450,000. The average age of the dead climbed from 34 in the first year of the war to 40 in 2025, and poorer minority regions bore heavy losses, including about 12,300 in Zabaykalsky Krai and 15,800 in Bashkortostan.

The Financial Times tallied 4,141 probable foreign fighters, whereas Bloomberg News, applying a broader definition, counted 11,335. Uzbekistan recorded the highest toll at 807, ahead of Tajikistan with 598. An estimated 28,000 foreigners from 136 countries are reported to be serving in the Russian army, and a September Amnesty International report said some had been lured with promises of well-paid civilian work before being pressed into service. Moscow denies coercion, and some 14,000 North Korean troops that Ukrainian officials say were sent to the Kursk region do not feature in the leaked data.

The Institute for the Study of War said the figures probably understate Russia's real losses and added that, as of July, casualties were outpacing recruitment. Russia analyst Janis Kluge told The Moscow Times that the deaths amount to about half a per cent of the working-age population, which may carry little economic weight, leaving the political significance as the main consequence.

issues.title: MIT Finds a Faster Way to Train Trustworthy AI Models for Climate Prediction
issues.gist: MIT researchers made a new way to train AI climate emulators using a small set of specially made synthetic data. The emulators predicted new scenarios better than traditional ones.
issues.gistKo: MIT 연구진이 특별히 만든 소량의 합성 데이터로 인공지능 기후 에뮬레이터를 훈련하는 새 방법을 개발했어요. 이렇게 훈련한 모델은 기존 모델보다 새로운 시나리오를 더 잘 예측했어요.
issues.easyKo: 기후를 예측하는 큰 컴퓨터 모델은 한 번 돌리는 데 몇 달이 걸려요. 그래서 이를 흉내 내는 빠른 인공지능 모델이 쓰여요. MIT 팀은 이 모델을 더 적은 데이터와 시간으로 훈련하는 방법을 찾았어요.

paragraphs.en: MIT researchers have developed a technique that helps make fast, trustworthy and adaptable artificial intelligence models for climate prediction. These specialized models are called climate emulators. They can quickly simulate how human activities change the future climate, for example temperatures or sea level. Because emulators run in seconds, scientists can use them to test thousands of different climate scenarios.

pro.en: Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have devised a training technique that streamlines the production of fast, dependable and adaptable artificial intelligence models for climate prediction. Known as climate emulators, these specialized models can rapidly simulate how human activities alter the future climate, including temperatures and sea level, and because they run in seconds, scientists can use them to probe thousands of scenarios.

Climate scientists customarily rely on earth system models for long-term projections, but these enormous, physics-based simulations can occupy supercomputer clusters for months to yield a single possible future. Emulators are fast AI surrogates that mimic the behavior of the full models. They are typically trained on six to eight scenarios, each of which has to be run through the full model, an expensive and time-consuming undertaking.

The MIT team's algorithm instead generates a synthetic dataset of optimized scenarios, so a user need run the full model just once. It begins with an arbitrary scenario drawn from a fast, simple model, gauges how closely the emulator reproduces the full model, and iteratively revises the training data until the error reaches a threshold. The resulting scenarios bear little resemblance to smooth real-world emissions trajectories, containing abrupt oscillations; the algorithm could, for example, sharply raise CO2 emissions in 2050.

According to the researchers, an emulator trained on a smaller quantity of carefully selected synthetic data accurately predicted outcomes in scenarios it had never encountered, whereas the conventional emulators they evaluated failed to adapt. The new emulator, for instance, could capture a local pollutant-control policy that reduces one pollutant while other emissions continue to climb. The findings are published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Noelle Selin, the senior author, notes that training an emulator can take months or even years, leaving the tools frequently out of date, and she believes shortening that process could be a game-changer for researchers and practitioners. The team next intends to test the approach with an emissions scenario produced by a full earth system model, and to explore its use with other climate models and in broader machine learning and computer vision.

issues.title: EU's "Made in Europe" Car Plan Worries Partners Including South Korea
issues.gist: The EU wants to subsidize only cars made in Europe. Partners such as Turkey, Morocco, Japan and South Korea fear they could lose out.
issues.gistKo: EU는 유럽에서 만든 차에만 보조금을 주려고 해요. 튀르키예, 모로코, 일본, 한국 같은 파트너는 피해를 볼까 걱정해요.
issues.easyKo: EU가 유럽산 부품 비율이 높은 차에만 보조금을 주는 법을 추진해요. 유럽 자동차 산업이 중국과 경쟁하는 데 쓰려는 건데, 유럽에 공장이 있는 한국과 일본 업체도 영향을 받을 수 있어요. 아직 법이 되려면 넘을 관문이 많아요.

paragraphs.en: A DW report from Oct. 28 describes an EU plan called the Industrial Accelerator Act, proposed in March. It aims to upgrade European car factories and to subsidize only vehicles made in Europe. But close partners such as Turkey, Morocco, Japan and South Korea are worried, because they are deeply tied to European supply chains.
paragraphs.ko: 10월 28일 DW 보도에 따르면 유럽연합에는 3월에 제안된 산업 가속화법이라는 계획이 있어요. 이 계획은 유럽 자동차 공장을 업그레이드하고 유럽에서 만든 차에만 보조금을 주는 것을 목표로 해요. 하지만 튀르키예, 모로코, 일본, 한국 같은 가까운 파트너들은 유럽 공급망에 깊이 엮여 있어서 걱정하고 있어요.

paragraphs.en: In October, Germany and France agreed on a compromise. Suppliers from non-EU countries such as the United Kingdom and Norway could qualify for European origin status. Other key players, including Turkey, would be left out, even though Turkey has had easy access to the EU market since the mid-1990s. The rules would require that 70% of the value of a vehicle's parts, not counting the battery, be made in Europe. The proposals still face major legislative hurdles in Brussels.
paragraphs.ko: 10월에 독일과 프랑스는 타협안에 합의했어요. 영국과 노르웨이 같은 비EU 국가의 부품 업체는 유럽산 지위를 얻을 수 있어요. 튀르키예는 1990년대 중반부터 EU 시장에 쉽게 접근해 왔지만, 튀르키예를 포함한 다른 주요 국가는 제외될 거예요. 규칙은 배터리를 뺀 차 부품 가치의 70%를 유럽에서 만들도록 요구해요. 이 제안은 브뤼셀에서 아직 큰 입법 관문이 남아 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Turkey could be hit hard. The head of a Turkish economic foundation told DW that 73% of Turkey's total automotive exports go to the EU. Turkey's auto exporters association calculated that exports to the EU were worth $30.1 billion last year. One reason for excluding Turkey is that Chinese carmakers are trying to enter the EU market through it. But BYD's plan for a $1 billion plant in Manisa has been put on hold. Morocco has received more than €10 billion in Chinese investment since the COVID-19 pandemic.
paragraphs.ko: 튀르키예는 큰 타격을 입을 수 있어요. 튀르키예 경제개발재단 대표는 튀르키예 자동차 수출 전체의 73%가 EU로 간다고 DW에 말했어요. 튀르키예 자동차 수출업체 협회는 지난해 EU로의 수출이 301억 달러어치였다고 계산했어요. 튀르키예를 제외하려는 이유 하나는 중국 자동차 회사들이 튀르키예를 통해 EU 시장에 들어오려 한다는 점이에요. 하지만 BYD가 마니사에 10억 달러 규모 공장을 짓겠다는 계획은 보류됐어요. 모로코는 코로나19 팬데믹 이후 100억 유로가 넘는 중국 투자를 받았어요.

pro.en: A DW report from Oct. 28 describes the European Union's Industrial Accelerator Act, proposed in March, which is intended to modernize European car plants and to subsidize only vehicles built in Europe. Yet the "Made in Europe" scheme is stirring deep unease among allied automaking nations, including Turkey, Morocco, Japan and South Korea, all of which are woven into European supply chains.

After months of deadlock, Germany and France reached a compromise in October under which suppliers from non-EU states such as the United Kingdom and Norway could qualify for European-origin status. Other significant players, Turkey among them, would be excluded despite enjoying seamless access to the EU market since the mid-1990s. The act would require that 70% of a vehicle's component value, excluding the battery, be sourced in Europe, and the proposals still face formidable legislative hurdles in Brussels.

Turkey stands to be especially hard hit. The head of a Turkish economic foundation told DW that 73% of the country's automotive exports are destined for the EU, and the exporters' association OIB put those shipments at $30.1 billion last year. Part of the rationale for excluding Ankara is that Chinese automakers are seeking back-door access to the EU through it, though BYD's plans for a $1 billion plant in Manisa have been shelved, and Morocco has drawn more than €10 billion in Chinese investment since the pandemic.

South Korean manufacturers could also suffer. Hyundai and Kia assemble cars in the Czech Republic and Slovakia but also ship models from Asia, which would not qualify, whereas Korean battery plants in Poland and Hungary would count as European. Cars imported from Japan would likewise fall outside the subsidies.

European automakers are lobbying to dilute the measure, warning that costlier parts would leave them at a further disadvantage against Chinese rivals. European component suppliers take the opposite view and are pressing for tougher rules, cautioning that up to 650,000 auto jobs in the region could be lost by 2035 without better protection. Their association's leader argues that partners meeting objective criteria should be welcomed.

issues.title: Canadian Steelmaker Stelco Will Bring Back 175 Laid-Off Workers
issues.gist: Stelco said it will recall all 175 workers it laid off in Hamilton and pay them back wages. The news came after weeks of pressure from the union and the Canadian government on its US owner.
issues.gistKo: 캐나다 철강 회사 스텔코가 해밀턴에서 해고한 노동자 175명을 모두 다시 부르고 밀린 임금도 주겠다고 했어요. 노조와 캐나다 정부가 미국 소유주를 몇 주 동안 압박한 끝에 나온 소식이에요.
issues.easyKo: 미국 회사가 산 캐나다 철강 공장에서 노동자들이 해고됐는데, 노조와 정부가 크게 반발했어요. 결국 회사가 12월 1일에 모두 복직시키고 그동안의 임금도 주기로 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Canadian steelmaker Stelco said on Friday that it will bring back all 175 workers it had laid off at its plant in Hamilton. The workers will return on December 1, and they will get back pay for the standard wages they would have earned while laid off. The decision ended a weeks-long standoff in which workers and the Canadian government faced the company's owner in the United States.
paragraphs.ko: 캐나다 철강 회사 스텔코는 금요일에 해밀턴 공장에서 해고했던 노동자 175명을 모두 다시 불러들이겠다고 밝혔어요. 노동자들은 12월 1일에 복귀하고, 해고된 동안 받았을 기본 임금을 소급해서 받아요. 이 결정으로 노동자와 캐나다 정부가 미국에 있는 회사 소유주와 맞선 몇 주간의 대치가 끝났어요.
